Sports.title: Bakole: Late-notice Wilder fight not like Parker | 'I like danger!'
Sports.content:
Martin Bakole explained his decision to step in as a replacement opponent for Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard next month.

After Jai Opetaia withdrew from his December 11 bout with former heavyweight world champion Wilder, Bakole came in to take his place on the Principality Stadium bill.

He insists it is a very different scenario to his short-notice assignment against Joseph Parker last year.

Bakole came in to box Parker for the WBO Interim title, landing in Riyadh just a day before the fight. Parker promptly put him down heavily and stopped him in their second round.

For this fight with Wilder though he's had more warning. He was training in Las Vegas to box on the same bill, albeit originally for a much lower-level opponent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Joseph Parker's spectacular knockout victory against Martin Bakole

"When I heard Wilder doesn't have an opponent, his opponent cancelled, they proposed me and I said why not? I'm ready to give a big fight," Bakole told Sky Sports. "Why not jump from a comeback fight to a big fight?

"I was surprised they mentioned my name and I said yes," he added. "I'm ready to come back again because I want to take over now the heavyweight division.

"I don't see Deontay beating me. He doesn't have the strength I have.

"I don't see any danger because I like danger, I like to impose myself.

"I'm ready and prepared for him."

That wasn't the case for Parker when he took that fight. "I was out in the Congo on holiday, I jumped in," Bakole said.

"In that fight I was giving Joseph Parker a hard time in the first round but because I was not fit and my head was not moving, he landed a punch. But I don't regret that fight. It's just part of my story.

"That was something to save the card."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Here's why no-one wants to fight Martin Bakole

While Bakole has been training in Las Vegas, he will still have long-time coach Billy Nelson in his corner for the fight.

"I came here to learn something new. I was getting ready for everyone," Bakole said. "Everything has changed [with his preparation], conditioning, nutrition."

He believes victory over Wilder will lead him to a world title shot next year.

"Of course," Bakole said. "That's why I wanted to change everything because I know next year, with my team, with His Excellency's [Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh] help, I will get a world title next year."

Sports.title: Eckert: Time to 'close the chapter' on Spygate ahead of Boro reunion
Sports.content:
"I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal."

It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man.

The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports.

Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now.

Eckert knows he broke the rules, and is thankful for the club and the support-base for backing him. Something that wouldn't have been easy after the ignominy of being kicked out of the play-offs.

"There have been some points, especially over the summer, where I think the club has made a commitment that not many clubs would have made," he admits.

"I'm very grateful, first of all, for the opportunity to step up in the first place, but also for the support over the summer. Obviously, that goes from everyone in the building to our supporters.

"This summer has been the biggest test we can possibly have in terms of the relationship between a football club and a fan base, and a manager and a fan base. I think the supporters have been great. It's been a tough period for them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tonda Eckert says he's relieved the FA's investigation into last season's spying controversy has concluded

"Towards the end of last season, it was difficult to process for everyone because of the process we used. I would have wanted to address the supporters a little earlier, so it took almost two weeks before I got to speak to them.

"From there on, I think the commitment has been very clear. It started with the football club and some players who committed to the project.

"You could just sense, the closer we got to the season, that everyone wanted to leave that behind and show what we are about as a football club and how much joy we bring when we go on the pitch. We felt that throughout the summer and on the first day of training.

"To come out of that situation with new strength just shows what this football club is about. Now it's for us to look forward and make sure that we continue to do that.

"There was still some uncertainty for the first block of games, and you just need to find a way, for me and obviously for everyone else in the football club, to put that to the side. As soon as the season starts, you need to perform.

"Then, obviously, to close that chapter finally, we needed a decision from the club. I think that's helped us to close that chapter."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Last month, Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert said it's time to move on after he was handed a six-week ban suspended until the end of next season over the Spygate scandal

The uncertainty came from the FA investigation, which wasn't resolved until October. In the end he was given a fine and a suspended six-week ban.

"Obviously, it's never easy to work on a daily basis if you have some uncertainty, and that's not just for me," he says. "I think it's the same for everyone at the football club.

"But I think we found a way, even in the first block of games, to perform. There's always something going on in football, sometimes a little bit bigger and sometimes not as big, but you need to push that to the side and make sure you find a way to perform.

"Once the decision came, I think it was important for everyone that we could finally close that."

For Eckert and Southampton it is just about points on the board, now. Trying to make up the deficit they were dealt at the start of the season.

"Obviously, if you could choose, no one would choose to start the season on minus four points," he says. "That's what it is. I think we are strong enough to make our way forward in the table.

"You shouldn't underestimate us coming from behind. We've shown that we are able to chase teams down, and that's the job for this year.

"It's been important for us to get some points on the board early in the season. We are still not where we want to be towards the end, so we need to make sure we continue."

Last week, Southampton handed Eckert, still just 33, a contract extension until 2029. They clearly feel he is their man to get them back to where they want to be.

"I think we've always been very open with our ambitions," he says. "There's no point in hiding that.

"I think the conditions are there to go up. It's never easy, but it's for us now to finish the job."

Sports.title: Taylor and Lewis suffer five straight defeats on Modus Super Series return
Sports.content:
Phil 'The Power' Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffered five losses from five matches for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth.

Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after claiming his 16th and final world title. However, the 16-time world champion returned to action to partner his long-time friend Lewis for the tournament.

Their opening match on Thursday saw them face Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton, with the England pair suffering a narrow 4-3 defeat.

Things failed to improve in their second outing, as Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-2 by Sweden's Andreas Harrysson and Anton Ostlund.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Taylor takes his first dart at double and checks out 84 in his competitive comeback in Modus Super Series International

A shock 4-3 defeat to unheralded Swiss duo Ansh Sood and Marcel Walpen followed, before Taylor and Lewis suffered a fourth consecutive loss, going down 4-1 to Germany's Daniel Klose and Liam Maendl-Lawrance.

Their fifth and final group-stage outing saw England take a 2-1 lead against Denmark, the only other side in their pool yet to record a victory. However, Ivan Springborg Poulsen and Andreas Toft Jorgensen responded by winning the next three legs in succession to condemn the English pair to a 4-2 defeat and a fifth straight loss.

Taylor revealed in September that the opportunity to partner Lewis was enough to tempt him back to the oche, although his return is not expected to signal a permanent comeback.

The 16-time world champion, who recently underwent successful hip replacement surgery, previously enjoyed considerable success alongside Lewis, with the pair winning four World Cup of Darts titles together.

The Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament continues in Portsmouth until November 28.

Sports.title: Bournemouth make European history after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo
Sports.content:
Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.

It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition.

Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.

But Alvaro Rodriguez equalised early in the second half, with substitute Rayan coming on to score a late winner to give Bournemouth an unlikely win.

Bournemouth were fortunate not to go behind after 10 minutes, with an offside flag chalking off Pablo Duran's poke home from close-range.

But the Cherries fell behind 10 minutes later when record Celta Vigo goalscorer Aspas scored a screamer.

Image: Celta Vigo's Iago Aspas celebrates after scoring the opening goal against Bournemouth

The 39-year-old had seen an overhead kick saved well by Michele Di Gregorio, but he picked up the ball on the right side of the area in the second phase of play, before cutting inside to curl past the goalkeeper and into the far corner off the post.

Things went from bad to worse for Bournemouth moment later when Diakite saw a yellow card upgraded to a red after a VAR check following a late challenge on Couhaib Driouech.

Tyler Adams replaced Justin Kluivert at half-time and the tactical switch drew an instant reward when Alvaro Rodriguez glanced home Amine Adli's cross to get Bournemouth back on level terms.

Image: Bournemouth's Alvaro Rodriguez, left, celebrates after scoring his side's opener

James Hill then drew a fine save from Ionut Radu - who is the only player ever to play for both clubs - before Di Gregorio was called into action at the other end to divert a long-range Aspas strike away.

But three Bournemouth substitutes combined for a late winner.

Adrien Truffert stole possession and broke before finding Marcus Tavernier the area. He laid the ball off for Rayan to sweep home and seal victory as Marco Rose's side made more history with a brilliant win at the Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.

11: GOAL RULED OUT! Duran follows up on an initial shot from Driouech to bundle home but is ruled off-side.

19: GOAL! Veteran striker and former Liverpool man Aspas scores a screamer to give Celta Vigo the lead!

25: RED CARD! Diakite is sent off after a VAR check for a late challenge on Driouech!

30: GOAL RULED OUT! Celta have the ball in the back of the net again, but Duran is again denied by an off-side flag.

39: SAVE! Kluivert shoots from a very tight angle - but it is well saved by Radu in the Celta Vigo goal.

46: GOAL! Rodriguez scores with a glancing header from close-range after a beautiful cross from the right-hand side by Adli.

60: SAVE! Scott goes for goal from a free kick from a tight angle but Radu has it covered.

63: SAVE! Hill has a go from range but the goalkeeper tips over.

73: SAVE! Aspas shoots from the edge of the area and Di Gregorio gets down well to save.

78: GOAL! What a turnaround! Rayan sweeps home to give Bournemouth the lead!

Everyone was motivated - Adli hails Cherries character in win at Celta

"Now we're enjoying a good run of form and things are going well for us," said Bournemouth midfielder Amine Adli. "We're in a good moment with confidence and a positive atmosphere.

"We're trying to maintain this energy and all the good things we're doing on the pitch, and keep reproducing them in every game."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury 'does NOT have schizophrenia' insists his wife Paris with their Netflix show to be amended - with his $150m showdown against Anthony Joshua now at risk as British boxing chiefs assess his mental health
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury 'does NOT have schizophrenia' insists his wife Paris with their Netflix show to be amended - with his $150m showdown against Anthony Joshua now at risk as British boxing chiefs assess his mental health

The biggest money fight in British boxing history will be called off if Tyson Fury is found to be mentally unfit to do battle with Anthony Joshua.

The British Boxing Board of Control are studying reports of the Gypsy King suffering from schizophrenia as well as being bi-polar before giving the go-ahead for his world heavyweight title clash with AJ in Cardiff's Principality Stadium late on the Friday night of December 11.

'Only one thing is certain,' says Board general secretary Robert Smith. 'That Tyson will not be allowed to enter the ring unless our doctors are satisfied there is no risk to his health. We are reviewing all the information about his mental condition and will come to a decision about authorising the fight in the next few days.'

The fight – along with purses of more than $150million between the two combatants – has been put in jeopardy by the Netflix documentary which claims that Fury has been diagnosed with schizophrenia as well as an historic bi-polar admission.

The US television streaming giant would also be among the heavy financial losers, having invested in Fury-Joshua in expectation of attracting more than 60million subscribers to cement their move into major boxing.

And just hours after we broke the story, the Furys scrambled to salvage the situation as his wife, Paris, rowed back on talk of schizophrenia. 'I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,' she said. 'I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word "schizophrenic".

'Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.'

Tyson Fury is due to fight long-time British rival Anthony Joshua on December 11 in Cardiff

However, that $150million fight is now at risk as the the British Boxing Board of Control are studying reports of the Gypsy King suffering from schizophrenia

His wife Paris insists that he is not schizophrenic with their Netflix show to be amended

Netflix added in their statement: 'Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.'

They would not be the only ones who took a financial hit if the fight was off. The Saudi Arabian backers under His Excellency Turki Alalshikh, the Stadium itself, as well as the city of Cardiff and its South Wales surrounds would suffer.

Smith, a leader in the worldwide campaign for making boxing safer for fighters, went through a similar situation before when Fury blamed clinical depression for an adverse drugs finding.

There is no suggestion whatsoever of wrongdoing by Fury in the current situation, except perhaps shooting his own bank balance in the foot. Although the context of the documentary which focuses principally upon Fury's state of mind and the family traumas bears discussion.

This piece of work came too close for comfort to putting the words mentioning 'mild schizophrenia' into the mouth of Tyson's wife Paris. And when its director, Lucy Wilcox, was asked why the coverage of his darker hours did not extend to the loss of his previous world title to Oleksandr Usyk, who beat him twice, she admitted she had never heard of the Ukrainian war hero.

Fury, natural born performer that he is, went along with some of the more extreme takes on his mental health.

The Board's consultants will be checking if there is any proper medical evidence to support the anecdotal broadcast. Or if the allegations in the documentary are at best exaggerated or at worst sensationalised.

Persisting public doubts still linger about whether the fight for which the boxing world has waited for a decade will indeed take place in a fortnight. Despite early reports of a one-hour 80,000-plus sell-out on the day tickets went on the market, there are still hundreds of seats for sale. Some being pushed with an offer of beer being thrown in.

Which raises further concern about the impact of alcohol on the traditionally rowdy Friday night in Cardiff when the Stadium empties the crowd onto the street at around 3am. So much so that the police are considering breathalysing late arrivals at the fight.

The odds favour Fury vs Joshua going ahead. If it does, the Welsh capital will be relieved if it ends without major incident.

Sports.title: Europa Fight League! Marseille hooligans descend on Levski Sofia end after 'Nazi salute' - while Besiktas match is SUSPENDED due to pro-Palestine propaganda... and away fans infiltrate Sunderland
Sports.content:
European football has endured another night of chaos with fan trouble at Marseille, Besiktas, and Sunderland.

Fans of Marseille and Levski Sofia clashed violently at their Europa League match, with home hooligans descending on the away end with bats and metal pipes after being provoked by a Nazi salute.

Turkish side Besiktas' clash with Israeli team Hapoel Be'er Sheva was brought to a temporary halt after fans of the former unfurled a pro-Palestinian flag, leading to a clash with police.

And Sunderland's home end was infiltrated by supporters of Jagiellonia Bialystok, who had been banned for the fixture by UEFA - with some of the visitors starting brawls.

The three Europa League disturbances cast another dark shadow over football.

Marseille saw the worst events as an estimated 200-300 home hooligans entered the away end with bats, pipes, and flares.

Marseille's supporters descended on the Levski Sofia end with bats and flares

It is believed that the Marseille ultras were provoked by a Nazi salute by a Levski Sofia fan

One supporter at the Marseille-Levski Sofia match nursed a bleeding head injury

Besiktas fans unfurled a Palestine flag at their fixture against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er Sheva

They had reportedly been provoked by some of Levski's ultras, who have a long association with neo-Nazism, and Marseille's supporters responded with an antifascist chant.

Some people kicked and punched each other - another even used a fire extinguisher, according to L'Equipe.

Bulgarian news agency Bgnes reported that the French hooligans also hurled bottles, flares and firecrackers.

Women and members of Levski's entourage were among the crowd, and several injured supporters had to be escorted out of the stadium, according to reports.

'Olympique de Marseille condemns the incidents that occurred on the sidelines of the match against Levski Sofia,' the hosts said in a statement.

'The swift intervention of the club's security teams restored calm, without affecting the match itself.

'The club is currently working to establish the precise circumstances of these incidents, in conjunction with the relevant authorities.'

Meanwhile, trouble spiked in the 25th minute of Besiktas' 2-1 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva.

One fan was seen being taken away on a stretcher at the Besiktas game, which was played in Batumi, Georgia

Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the advertising hoarding, covering the UEFA lettering

Police had to remove some Jagiellonia Bialystok fans who had infiltrated the home end at Sunderland

The match had been moved to Batumi, Georgia due to security worries surrounding ties between Turkish and Israeli clubs. There was even tension on the pitch, as Besiktas refused to shake hands with their opponents.

After a pro-Palestine banner was revealed by Besiktas' fans, the Georgian police appeared to react with tear gas or pepper spray and batons. One fan was seen being carried away on a stretcher.

The game had to be briefly suspended, with both sets of teams and the officials going to the dressing rooms.

After the match, Besiktas full-back Kassoum Ouattara hung the Palestine flag over the UEFA lettering on the pitchside advertising hoardings.

Besiktas condemned the local police, saying they had used 'disproportionate force'.

The club also wrote: 'Upon learning that security forces were obstructing our fans' entry into the stadium, we immediately contacted the UEFA delegate, who arranged for the stadium's evacuation gates to be opened, allowing our fans to enter the stadium quickly and safely.

'We announce that steps have been taken with our Consulate General in Batumi and UEFA regarding the disproportionate force used by security forces against our fans, and state that we will closely monitor the situation until each of our fans returns safely to our country.'

Turkey and Israel have long been simmering with tension amid the conflict and numerous Turkish clubs such as Galatasaray, Fenerbahce, and Mohamed Salah's Trabzonspor came out in support of Besiktas later - despite usually being bitter rivals.

A UEFA Disciplinary ruling meant Polish club Jagiellonia Białystok weren't meant to have any away supporters at The Stadium of Light for tonight's game at Sunderland, yet plenty of them have turned up in the home end… 🫣😭pic.twitter.com/lRBvHOp16T — Football Away Days (@AwayDaysFB) November 26, 2026

Jagiellonia Bialystok's supporters had been banned - but some bought tickets in the home end

Meanwhile, at the Stadium of Light, events were of a lower scale, but some away fans were seen brawling with the home faithful and police waded in to eject them.

Jagiellonia Bialystok's fans had been banned from attending the game by UEFA following disturbances between them and Levski Sofia fans earlier this month.

But around 20 of them managed to secure tickets, Sunderland believe, and squeeze into the stadium.

The club had already caught some out in advance, writing: 'The club is actively monitoring ticket purchases and has identified and cancelled tickets purchased by, or on behalf of, individuals identified as Jagiellonia supporters.

'All affected tickets will be refunded to the original purchasers.

'This restriction applies across all areas of the stadium, including home sections, and regardless of how tickets have been purchased or transferred.

'Any attempt to circumvent the restriction, including using tickets purchased through third parties or belonging to other supporters, will result in refusal of entry.

'Jagiellonia supporters without a valid entitlement to attend the fixture are strongly advised not to travel to Sunderland.

'No Jagiellonia supporters without valid permission to attend will be permitted entry into the Stadium of Light, and we strongly advise they stay away from the immediate surrounding vicinity.

'The club will continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to ensure UEFA's ruling is fully enforced and that the fixture takes place as a home supporter-only event.'

Sports.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win, Bournemouth win TENTH game in a row with comeback, and Brighton thrash Romanian minnows - but Sunderland are held at home
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win, Bournemouth win TENTH game in a row with comeback, and Brighton thrash Romanian minnows - but Sunderland are held at home

Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad, by Will Pickworth

Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel of a second defeat in a week after a flat display against Real Sociedad, he may have been rueing that statement.

But when Chris Richards' long-throw was headed on by Axel Disasi, everything changed as Jean-Philippe Mateta was pulled down by Jon Martin.

The Real Sociedad defender was sent off, and after Mateta tucked away his penalty, a meek performance and atmosphere at Selhurst Park was transformed.

Having looked second best for much of the match, Palace were now quick, confident and incisive, and the Basque outfit were on the ropes.

Daichi Kamada had an effort cleared off the line to ramp up the pressure, before Jorgen Strand Larsen's audacious bicycle kick fell to the feet of Dwight McNeil to send the home fans into bedlam. To add to the chaos, Yeremy Pino saw a second penalty saved in added time.

Palace's season has been a disaster thus far, but their 2026-27 campaign and the Frank reign now has lift off, and most importantly belief heading into Sunday's crunch home game with Hull.

Thomas Frank got his first win as Crystal Palace boss as his side came from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1

The Dane, who received a warm reception from the Palace faithful ahead of his first home game, had spoken about rotation ahead of a busy period and he made five changes to the side that were beaten by Coventry at the weekend.

That included rare starts for Will Hughes, Ben Chilwell and Eddie Nketiah, with Frank perhaps wanting to take a look at as many of his squad as possible while also having an eye on the Hull clash.

Palace had practiced defending set-pieces in the warm-up in a clear demonstration of Frank's attempts deal with what has become their kryptonite this season, yet Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr was inches away from turning in after being left unmarked at the far post from a free kick just minutes in.

A noticeable difference to Palace’s European journey this season has been the calibre of opposition with the rise to the Europa League, and a talented Sociedad side that sit fifth in LaLiga and are captained by World Cup-winner Mikel Oyarzabal certainly demonstrated that.

The Basque outfit began to step things up after a poor opening half hour, with Dean Henderson forced into two good stops from Goncalo Guedes. Palace’s best play was coming through Yeremy Pino and Kamada, and Mateta headed narrowly over on the stroke of half-time.

Frank had called for a boisterous atmosphere ahead of kick off, but it was again quiet as Palace laboured and their midfield started to struggle. Chilwell looked short of sharpness at left-back and was repeatedly targeted as Sociedad began to dominate, before Oyarzabal somehow fired straight at Henderson from a few yards out.

The England stopper was alert again soon after and Sociedad's control eventually paid off when Sarr turned home from Job Ochieng's cross after a neat move.

But the tie changed when Mateta made no mistake from the spot before McNeil ensured that Frank is more than happy to be back in the madhouse of management.

Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth, by Luke Power

Can anybody stop Bournemouth? For long stretches here it looked as if their relentless march would finally be stopped - but the 10-man Cherries found another gear to continue their rampage.

Marco Rose’s men have won 10 games in a row now, extending a club record. For two months, they have steamrolled their opponents with dauntless football and racked up an aggregate score of 25-3. They sit top of the Europa League with a perfect record.

Underneath the red and black armour, fans are starting to wonder if these players are actually of our species. Is Justin Kluivert a man or a cyborg? If you prick James Hill, does he bleed?

With each victory, the cry of the football world grows louder: somebody, please, stop this Bournemouth juggernaut, for the sake of everybody else’s trophy prospects.

Celta Vigo stepped up as the next challengers and thought they would be the heroes. They found Bournemouth’s net four times in all, but were denied by the offside flag for three of them. For long stretches, they were in command.

Bournemouth have now won 10 games in a row after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1

After a disappointing first half, Alvaro Rodriguez got them level early in the second

Rayan scored the winner against the run of play as Bournemouth continued their perfect run in the Europa League

In the first half, Bournemouth looked average. They were gifting away the ball in their own half, Celta found ways to sneak through their pincer-movement press, and the Spaniards had the better chances.

The first red flag came 11 minutes in, when Michele Di Gregorio spilled a save into the path of Pablo Duran, who dinked over the goalkeeper but saw his effort ruled out for offside.

Such warning bells were unheeded. Not long later, former Liverpool man Iago Aspas forced a save with a spectacular overhead kick at the age of 39.

Bournemouth failed to clear their lines, and Aspas punished the visitors, ghosting past Alex Scott on his return from injury before blasting beyond Di Gregorio with his left foot.

Things went from bad to worse minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a stamp on Couhaib Driouech, his yellow card upgraded to a red after a review by referee Harm Osmers.

Celta almost doubled their lead when Duran beat Di Gregorio again, but he had strayed offside.

The cameras panned to Rose, who stood looking bewildered on the sidelines, hands on hips. It took them 37 minutes for Kluivert to register their first shot. Bournemouth had been played off the park. This was a case of clinging on.

But the side that emerged in the second half were unrecognisable. If Bournemouth were a man down, they played with all the swagger of having an extra body.

They were level within two minutes of the restart, Alvaro Rodriguez glancing in from Amine Adli’s header.

Suddenly Bournemouth were their efflorescent selves again. Antonio Silva, Adli, and Rodriguez combined for a beautiful passage of play but were spurned by the offside flag. Hill tested Ionut Radu from range.

They finally got their rewards on the counter-attack, when Marcus Tavernier teed up his fellow substitute Rayan to slot past Radu and stun their hosts. Another comeback job complete.

And so the Bournemouth army marches on unfettered. In the next nine days, they face Fulham, Brighton, and Hull in the Premier League. By the time they visit Arsenal in mid-December, they may be breathing down their necks.

Brighton 4-0 Craiova, by Ben Winstanley

Earlier this week, Brighton CEO Paul Barber revealed the lengths that his club go to before agreeing to sign a player.

'We try and talk to people that know them, people that have coached them, people that played with them, sponsors that have worked with them, media that have interviewed them, maybe even neighbours that have lived next door to them,' he told Men in Blazers media network. 'You know, what sort of people are we talking about? Are we talking about players that are entirely focused on their work?'

There can be little doubt that the rigorous selection process is working, and two of their budget buys were on the scoresheet in the first half as they made light work of the Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova - and continued to make a mockery of the supposed challenge of balancing domestic and European assaults.

In the third minute Ibrahim Osman - £16.6m from Nordsjaelland in 2024 – finished off a sharp team move from close range after a pinpoint Jack Hinshelwood cross. Then shortly after the half-hour mark full back Maxime de Cuyper, £17m from Club Brugge in 2025, seized on a slack defensive ball into midfield, took two touches in advancing forward and - still well outside the box – wrongfooted the goalkeeper as he stroked the ball into the far corner. He made the finish look much easier than it was.

Brighton thrashed Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova and look capable of competing on multiple fronts

If the result was still in any doubt then, it wasn’t by the 39th minute when Vladimir Screciu was sent off for a clumsy challenge on Matt O’Riley. Referee Matthias Jollenbeck showed a yellow card but a replay showed a hefty tread on the ankle and - after being sent to his monitor - upgraded it to red.

The second half, then, gave the Seagulls a chance to remind everyone of their ruthless side. Already the highest scorers in the Premier League - averaging 2.4 per game this season – they wasted little time adding to their tally.

First, 19-year-old Charalampos Kostoulas made it three with his sixth of the season thanks to a cool finish on the hour mark, two minutes before Osman – like Hinshelwood a constant menace - picked the ball up on the left and cut inside to roll home his second.

They ended 90 minutes of domination having had 27 shots – one of which saw Femi Azeez missing the chance to make it five on debut by inexplicably blazing over from five yards.

Brighton have now scored four or more in five of their eight home games this season, and ended last night’s rout top of the Conference League having yet to concede a goal. The competition does not look big enough for them.

Sunderland 1-1 Jagiellonia Bialystok, Miles Starforth

Sunderland still have work to do if the club is to reach the Europa League’s knockout stages after Jagiellonia Bialystok held them to a 1-1 draw in a game which saw some supporters of the Polish club evade a UEFA ban and get into the Stadium of Light.

Timur Tutierov was on target for Regis Le Bris’ side, who are hoping to secure a top-eight finish in the competition’s league phase and avoid the play-offs in their first European campaign in 53 years.

Le Bris had gone into the game without injured captain Granit Xhaka and striker Brian Brobbey, two of his most influential players. Sunderland’s head coach, mindful of forthcoming Premier League games against Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Newcastle United, took no chances with the pair for the visit of Jagiellonia, ninth in the Polish league.

He made six changes from the team which had held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at the weekend, again fielding a youthful team in the competition.

Sunderland had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok

A flat performance from a much-changed team had seen Sunderland beaten 2-0 by Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb in their last European outing at the Stadium of Light.

The visiting section had been bouncing that night, but this time the away end at the Stadium of Light was closed due to a one-match UEFA ban for Jagiellonia fans following crowd disturbances at the club’s fixture away to Levski Sofia on November 5.

On Wearside, the feeling ahead of the match was that third-bottom Sunderland, while shot shy, were slowly turning a corner, having taken four points from fixtures against Chelsea and Villa without conceding a goal to climb above Manchester United in the table.

The big one in Europe - AC Milan at the San Siro - is next in the competition for Sunderland, with the fixture having captured the imagination of supporters.

There were scarves with the slogan ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan? You’re about to!’ on sale outside the ground, with the merchandise a nod to a song which fans of their rivals Newcastle United can no longer sing.

With the visiting section eerily empty, Sunderland supporters were in good voice at kick-off time, though their team had an early scare when a Nik Prelec shot took a deflection off Ndah Sidiki, but Robin Roefs was able to gather the ball.

Within minutes of the game starting, it became apparent that a group of Polish fans had managed to buy tickets in the North Stand, and police were quickly called to remove them from the stadium amid cheers from Sunderland supporters.

On the pitch, it was another slow start for Le Bris’ side, though Malick Fofana tested Slawomir Abramowicz with a fine left-footed shot from outside the box.

Timur Tutierov was on target fo the Black Cats, but this was a flat performance

Enzo Le Lee did well to seize on a back pass in the 30th minute and cross from the left for Nilson Angulo - who was unmarked in the box - after rounding the goalkeeper. However, his shot struck the feet of Yuki Kobayashi.

Le Bris lost Omar Alderete to injury as the half-time break approached - he was replaced by Luke O’Nien - and Roefs beat away a free-kick from Kajetan Szmyt.

Sunderland went into the break knowing they should have led, but their finishing had again let them down in the absence of Brobbey, their talisman.

Le Bris made two more changes at the break - he sent on Thomas Meunier and Jules Ahoka - and his team were ahead within seconds of the restart.

Rigg broke through the middle, and the ball was worked to Le Fee, whose cross bounced off a visiting defender on its way to Tutierov at the far post, who headed the ball home.

The lead did not last, with Jozwiak seizing on a Nilson Reinildo backpass before rounding Roefs to level. Jozwiak’s goal was celebrated by a sizeable pocket of Jagiellonia fans high in the West Stand.

Roefs denied Jozwiak at the hour-mark with a low save as home fans became increasingly frustrated with their team.

A spirited Jagiellonia team pushed to win the game in the last 15 minutes, but the match ended in a stalemate.

Sports.title: Super Seaford on track for their best-ever finish in honour of inspirational former headmaster: DAILY MAIL SCHOOLS RUGBY TROPHY
Sports.content:
Seaford College are continuing their rise up the SOCS Daily Mail Schools Trophy ladder, inspired by former headmaster John Green.

The Sussex school hit the top ten of this national competition through a 28-24 win over Ipswich School in a match played in honour of their figurehead who retired last year.

Director of rugby Christian Head explained that Seaford were playing an annual match in honour of a teacher who was also twice head of rugby at the school.

He added: 'It’s a tribute to a man whose life has been shaped, and defined, by the values of rugby: courage, humility, resilience, respect, and an unwavering commitment to team.'

Last year, Seaford lost out on the very last play to Northampton School for Boys – the eventual Trophy champions – but this time held out to pip Ipswich.

Seaford have built a team around captain Tom Read and No8 Llewellyn Lourens in the pack while Jack Mills has provided good linking and an assured boot and power, and Jack Cosgrove delivered strength in midfield.

The win puts Seaford in ninth place and keeps them on course to beat their previous best finish of 12th in the 2015-16 season.

However, they face tough trips to heavyweights in former champions Clifton College and Sedbergh to finish their campaign.

Seaford College in action during the 28-24 win over Ipswich

Seaford have risen high to move into the top 10 of the Schools Rugby merit table

Seaford will finish their campaign with trips to former winners Clifton College and Sedbergh

Sedbergh slipped out of the top ten to 11th when losing to title contenders Wellington College in the annual midweek showdown at Broadstreet near Coventry.

For Wellington, the victory lifted them into top place ahead of Radley in second and third-placed Brighton who they play in final match of their campaign on Saturday week.

Wellington are finishing in top form having also beaten Clifton since half-term when they lost in the semi-final of the St Joseph’s Festival 7-8 to Brighton.

Before facing Wellington, Brighton this Saturday host fifth-placed RGS Guildford who are one of the busiest teams in the Trophy having won all nine matches so far.

LIVE SCHOOLS RUGBY Click HERE to watch Ipswich School v Berkhamsted this Saturday. Click HERE to view this season's streams so far - and for last season's broadcasts click HERE

The latest win was a 33-19 win at Skinner’s featuring two tries from Jola Akin-Olugbade.

RGS had survived a scare in their previous match against St John’s Leatherhead which was settled by fly half Ollie Krikorian kicking a late penalty to secure a 31-29 win. Gregor Mellor scored two tries.

Fourth-placed Cheltenham kept in contention by winning a local derby against Sir Thomas Rich’s, 40-13, in an annual floodlit match staged at Gloucester’s Kingsholm ground.

Cheltenham, coached by ex-England full-back Olly Morgan, are enjoying an unbeaten campaign including success at the St Joseph’s Festival where they beat the host school in the final.

The next live match to be screened on the SOCS channel is this Friday when Ipswich host Berkhamsted at Bury St Edmunds rugby club, kick off 7.30pm.

Having lost out to Seaford, Ipswich had previously beaten Hurstpierpoint, 59-10. Josh Strudwick, Silvin Leicher and Dom Ateba scored two tries each.

Sports.title: EDDIE JONES: I bumped into Fabien Galthie by the bins this week - this is how we'd use the Ryder Cup to make Nations Championship even better, why I think his France side will beat South Africa and how England became World Cup contenders
Sports.content:
On Wednesday night, I was standing outside Twickenham, chatting to the Daily Mail Sport boys for my weekly column. As usual, they took me to a posh location – this time it was next to the bins at the home of English rugby!

It was pitch black and the temperature was just above freezing. It was then that I had a nice surprise, with France coach Fabien Galthie coming over to say hello.

Fabien asked for my number as he wanted to arrange a visit to a training session. That’s what international rugby is all about. As coaches we’re rivals, but friends too. I must say though: I’ve talked rugby in better locations!

On Wednesday, the coaches of all of the top 12 teams in the world – except for the banned Rassie Erasmus – were at Twickenham for a big media launch event to preview the Nations Championship’s finals weekend. All 12 captains were there, too.

The creation of the new competition has been outstanding for rugby. It’s brought so much extra interest to the game and you’re going to see that over the next few days.

At what other point would you get Siya Kolisi, Antoine Dupont and Maro Itoje all in the same room at the same time? This weekend is going to be brilliant for the Test game. I love the chance to catch up with all my coaching compatriots – guys like Steve Borthwick and Fabien.

As Japan coach, I've loved the creation of the Nations Championship. It has been outstanding for rugby and brought so much extra interest to the game

As we exchanged numbers by the Twickenham bins, France boss Fabien Galthie told me he too has loved the Nations Championship

‘I love this competition too,’ Fabien told me. 'It reminds me of when I was at school. At the end of the season, we’d have a tournament for three days with all the best teams from all over France. Back then, we were very happy to all play together, especially if we made the final.

'The Nations Championship is like this – the best teams in the world, in one place, for three days. It’s fantastic. As coaches, we all have an admiration for each other. It’s the same with the players. We all love rugby, but it’s a small world – 10 or 12 countries, maybe a few more. It’s not a big world like football, so we need to work together. Not against each other.

'I’ve learned a lot from you. You always opened the door to me, especially in the 2000s when you were with Australia and I was coaching Stade Francais. I wasn’t a rival then, I was a young boy! But it was the same when you coached England too.’

It was nice of Fabien to describe me as a friend and mentor. I think France are playing so well at the moment. Fabien told me he’s had to use 50 players across his team’s Nations Championship campaign due to injuries, but they still made it to Sunday’s final with South Africa. We swapped numbers and I plan to visit the French camp during the Six Nations.

There’s been a fair bit of chat about future Nations Championship finals weekends being played in new destinations like Qatar, the USA or Saudi Arabia.

‘I’m happy with this (existing) formula,’ Galthie told me. ‘For me, the temple of our sport is here at Twickenham. It’s a church of rugby.’

I agree. I think one of the beauties of having the three straight days of finals matches in London is you don’t have to travel far. The difficult thing for the northern hemisphere teams coming to the south is the travel and that is what kills the players.

We talk a lot about injuries and I think travel is one of the major factors behind that. I don’t think we should be looking to take these matches to places like Qatar. We’ve got to look after rugby’s traditional communities and make them stronger.

The Nations Championship has been amazing. When else would you get all these wonderful captains in the same place?

Antoine Dupont is just brilliant. I think he'll lead France to glory against South Africa and they'll become the first Nations Championship winners

Rugby is a small game. But we can still be powerful within that. The World Cup has looked to expand by going to America in 2031 and that’s great. That can be a trial. But for this prestigious tournament, you want to play it in rugby heartlands. London is great.

An extra element I’d like in the Nations Championship is more emphasis on the battle between the north and the south. You could make the tournament more like the Ryder Cup, by making more of the wins by each hemisphere and really pitching them against each other. It would bring an extra competitive dimension.

My Japan team has had to deal with a lot of injuries this year. It’s been the same for France, Argentina and Italy. But all those sides will benefit in the long run, because they now know what more of their players can do in big games.

You’d rather have injuries now than at the World Cup. Fabien might have had to use 50 players, but all of them are good! And it helps a great deal when he has a player like Dupont to lead the team. He’s brilliant. I think France will go well against South Africa and become the first Nations Championship winners.

England have turned World Cup race into a five-way battle

Earlier this year, after the Six Nations and the summer’s first round of Nations Championship matches, I thought there were four teams who could win the World Cup and that England were not one of them. That's changed.

England have shown this month with their impressive performances against Australia, Japan and New Zealand that they’ve joined that group. The Big Four (New Zealand, South Africa, Ireland and France) has now become a Big Five.

They still have work to do but their development in their past three matches has been the big shift this November.

Also, England traditionally play well in Australia, where next year's World Cup will be. There is history there with the team that won Down Under in 2003, then won 3-0 and 2-1 on tour there in 2016 and 2022 – that counts for something.

I've been impressed with England captain Maro Itoje, who looks back to his best

And so does Ellis Genge, after a dip from his usual high standards

The prospect of competing for the World Cup would be a big boost for rugby in England. Every time I'm back here now, I’m amazed by how big football is. It just gets bigger and bigger.

I watch BBC News every morning and the amount of rugby on it is tiny. The game is shrinking here and we need it to grow. A World Cup win would be huge for that.

Before this month, England were supposed to be in disarray. I read they were all fighting, hated the coach and the camp was a nightmare. Now everyone is saying they’re close to being the best team in the world.

That doesn’t happen. You don’t go from no-hopers to the top in a couple of weeks. What England have done well is regenerate their older players and balance that with the younger guys coming through. There’s real power and pace in the team.

Look at Maro Itoje and Ellis Genge. Those guys in particular have summed up the team’s improvement. Over the past two years, they probably haven’t been at their best. They’re now back at top level.

Selection is always the biggest thing for England and they’ve got that pretty much right. They’ve got a nice balance to their game between kicking and running. They’re using the strengths of their players really well.

I’ve watched the first 20 minutes of last weekend’s New Zealand game a couple of times because I wanted to work out how England dominated so much. It was because they won every collision and were on the front foot the whole time. New Zealand just couldn’t get any possession.

England need to stay grounded. They’ve gone well this autumn, but you’re never as good or bad as people say. It’s always somewhere in between.

England, including Seb Atkinson (pictured), need to stay grounded. They’ve gone well this autumn, but you’re never as good or bad as people say

England beat the All Blacks last Saturday by winning every collision in the first 20 minutes and by being on the front foot the whole time

Maro is a very good and experienced captain now. He’s a 100-Test player, so he’ll know how to keep a lid on his team-mates and get the right messaging to them.

New Zealand are going to respond when the teams meet again on Saturday. The All Blacks never usually play without physicality two games in a row. So, you’re going to see a real test for England. We’ll see whether they’re as good as people think.

Whatever happens, this month has been great for their World Cup preparation. England are trending upwards with lots of positive signs.

Sports.title: Darren Bent's beach ball bedlam, Nani's controversial quick-thinking and Peter Enckelman's calamitous mishap: Our experts pick the strangest goals they have ever seen after Bruno Fernandes' 'divot strike' in Lisbon
Sports.content:
Darren Bent's beach ball bedlam, Nani's controversial quick-thinking and Peter Enckelman's calamitous mishap: Our experts pick the strangest goals they have ever seen after Bruno Fernandes' 'divot strike' in Lisbon

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United were the beneficiaries of a bizarre goal in the Champions League on Wednesday night, as the captain's long-range effort bounced up off the turf and deceived the goalkeeper to help earn Mauricio Pochettino a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in his second game in charge.

Football has certainly seen its fair share of quirky, bizarre and downright bonkers goals over the years, and Fernandes' effort in Lisbon is certainly one to add to the collection.

Here, Daily Mail Sport's reporters look back at some of the strangest goals they can remember, from outrageous goalkeeping blunders to freakish deflections and moments of sheer misfortune.

Darren Bent (Sunderland 1-0 Liverpool) - October 17, 2009

JAMES SHARPE

Forget bouncing in off a divot, try the ball flying into the net off a beach ball. Darren Bent’s winner against Liverpool at the Stadium of Light back in 2009 has got to be the strangest.

A Liverpool fan lobbed a gigantic red beach ball on to the pitch (in the middle of October) which was initially removed by a steward only for the wind to blow it back.

What made it even funnier was that when Bent’s shot struck it, Liverpool keeper Pepe Reina tried to save the inflatable, which now resides in the National Football Museum, instead of the actual ball that flew past him.

Thank heavens there was no VAR back then to spoil the day.

Pepe Reina had no chance after Darren Bent's strike ricocheted off a beach ball into the goal

Peter Enckelman (Birmingham vs Aston Villa) - September 16, 2002

KIERAN GILL

Obviously the mind immediately goes to balloons and players ghosting behind goalkeepers. But my favourite happened on September 16, 2002 between Birmingham City and Aston Villa.

Olof Mellberg took a throw-in. He threw it back to Peter Enckelman. The ball bounced under Enckelman’s foot and rolled into the Villa goal. Referee David Elleray reckoned he must have touched it with his studs.

It was all made worse for Enckelman with a Birmingham fan hopping out of the crowd to goad him to his face. I must have been nine years old and remember watching all this live.

Can’t imagine my parents told me what that hand gesture the fan was doing in front of Enckelman meant.

Peter Enckelman scored a disastrous own goal after the ball bounced underneath his foot

Mo Diame (Brighton vs Newcastle) - February 28, 2017

CRAIG HOPE

Brighton half cleared a corner and Christian Atsu returned a scuffed volley, which was helped on by the toe of Daryl Murphy, before Mo Diame planted his foot in the ground and allowed the ball to bounce off the back of his heel, looping up and over all inside the goalmouth and into the top corner.

I was there, and I have revisited my match report.

'Diame had been stood still for the majority of the previous 81 minutes,' I wrote. 'Finally, it was a tactic which served him well.'

I also refer to the goal as fluky and hilarious. It is now the stuff of legend on Tyneside, for it helped Newcastle to win promotion as champions. Indeed, without it, Brighton would have finished top and Newcastle second.

Mo Diame scored one of the craziest goals in Championship history against Brighton in 2017

Tony Popovic (Portsmouth vs Crystal Palace) - September 11, 2004

BEN WILLCOCKS

Some goals stay with you because of the sublime, others because of the ridiculous. And I doubt I'll ever see a stranger goal live than Tony Popovic's flying backheel into his own net in 2004.

With Portsmouth protecting a 2-1 lead late on against Crystal Palace, nerves were jangling around Fratton Park until Popovic's moment of spectacular misfortune.

Pompey's Steve Stone floated a hopeful cross into the Palace box, prompting Popovic to stretch out a leg in an attempt to clear. Instead, he somehow managed to flick the ball off his boot, onto the post and into the net, producing a finish any top striker would be proud of.

Olivier Giroud, eat your heart out.

Portsmouth couldn't believe their luck when Tony Popovic flicked the ball into in his own net

Nani (Manchester United vs Tottenham) - October 30, 2010

TARA ANSON-WALSH

This one has always stuck with me, partly for the sheer audacity of Nani and partly because it's the sort of goal that simply wouldn't escape VAR scrutiny today.

Back when a trip to Manchester United was still a fearsome prospect, Spurs were a goal down and chasing a late equaliser when Nani was brought down in the penalty area and appeared to handle the ball.

Crucially, though, Mark Clattenburg had not blown his whistle. Tottenham goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, assuming a free-kick had been awarded, placed the ball on the ground.

Still gesticulating, Nani got up, realised the ball was still live, and coolly passed it into the back of the net. Cue bedlam in the Stretford End.

Nani celebrates his controversial goal against Spurs, to the fury of goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes

Zlatan Ibrahimovic (Sweden vs England) - November 14, 2012

OLIVER HOLT

It's not weird in the category of a divot or a beach ball but the most outlandish goal I've ever seen live was Zlatan Ibrahimovic's 30-yard overhead kick for Sweden against England at the Friends Arena in Stockholm in November 2012.

A long ball came over the top of the England defence, Joe Hart ran out and headed it clear and Ibrahimovic launched himself into the air, hooking the ball in a majestic arc over England's disbelieving goalkeeper. Great goals can be strange, too.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic's acrobatic bicycle kick against England was both strange and sensational

Stan Collymore (Blackburn vs Liverpool) - February 24, 1996

BEN WINSTANLEY

As soon as I watched Fernandes' speculative long-range strike bobble past Sporting Lisbon goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, my mind immediately cast back to Tim Flowers being embarrassed by Stan Collymore at Ewood Park in 1996.

Not that it was the Blackburn goalkeeper's fault, of course. Collymore's feeble effort from distance in the 11th minute trickled along the turf before hitting a rogue divot and bouncing over Flowers' head into the net.

Collymore, who cracked a smile but toned down his celebrations, turned away in disbelief as Flowers stared down at the pitch with his hands on his hips.

Liverpool went on to win the game 3-2 and Flowers described it as 'one of those ridiculous situations'.

Stan Collymore scored one of the strangest goals when his effort bobbled over Tim Flowers

Gary Neville (England vs Croatia) - October 11, 2006

MATT BARLOW

Strange bobbles take me back to Gary Neville’s own goal in Zagreb. Early in the doomed England reign of Steve McClaren.

Neville rolled a simple back pass towards Paul Robinson who took a mighty swing at fresh air with his right boot and looked aghast as it trundled past him and into the net for Croatia's second in a 2-0 win. The Spurs keeper stamped furiously at the offending divot as the Maksimir Stadium erupted.

Adding another layer to the comic value were pitchside LED ad screens flashing up images of Sacha Baron Cohen’s new Borat film and one of his lame catchphrases: 'I like you'.

It was a bad omen at the start of the failed Euro 2008 campaign and the beginning of the end for both Robinson and Neville in England colours.

Gary Neville's own goal against Croatia came after Paul Robinson totally missed the ball

Stefan Kiessling (Hoffenheim v Leverkusen) - October 18, 2013

WILL GOVE

Legendary Bayer Leverkusen forward Stefan Kiessling has got to be one of the only players to score with a shot off target.

While away to Hoffenheim, a corner was swung in towards Leverkusen striker Kiessling, who, at first glance, simply headed home smartly.

But on closer inspection we can see that the ball was destined for the side netting and an inconspicuous hole in the side of the net let the ball slip in.

Even Kiessling himself had his head in his hands thinking he’d missed before turning around to see his teammates were celebrating.

Sports.title: Swansea investigate after naked image of player is shared on social media ahead of grudge match with bitter rivals Cardiff
Sports.content:
Swansea City have launched an internal investigation after an inappropriate image of one of its players was shared on social media.

The image, which emerged on X, formerly Twitter, on Wednesday night, appeared to show a Swansea City player naked standing beside a bed.

The photo, first taken on Snapchat, has since disappeared online after violating the social media site’s rules.

A Swansea City spokesperson confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that the club are investigating the photo internally but no further comment will be made at this time.

The photo, which was first shared by a Cardiff City fan, has emerged just days before this Sunday’s South Wales derby between Swansea and Cardiff, with tensions between both fanbases high now that they are back in the same division.

Swansea City have launched an internal investigation after an inappropriate image of one of its players was shared on social media

While Swansea plan to speak to the player to establish the key facts behind the image, there is also a legal side that cannot be ignored.

In England and Wales it is a criminal offence to share naked or intimate photos without consent under Section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

Should an investigation determine the image has been tampered with, including AI-generated or manipulated 'deepfakes,' which was one of the allegations on social media on Wednesday night, that too is a criminal act under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

Sports.title: The assist of the season! Remarkable new footage shows moment Bruno Fernandes created the divot HIMSELF before scoring one of the most bizarre goals EVER in Man United's chaotic draw with Sporting Lisbon
Sports.content:
Footage appears to show Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf that led to his fortunate second goal against Sporting Lisbon.

The Manchester United captain scored a bizarre goal against his former side on Wednesday night, with his long-range shot taking a fortuitous bobble off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch to leave goalkeeper Kaique Pereira helpless.

While fingers were initially pointed at the ground staff, footage shows the divot was actually created by Fernandes himself when he planted his boot into the turf while pressing high up the pitch moments earlier.

Reminiscent of former Liverpool forward Stan Collymore's famous bobbling goal past Blackburn Rovers goalkeeper Tim Flowers in 1996, Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The goal summed up another chaotic evening for United, in which goalkeeping calamities, controversial refereeing calls, three penalties and a red card resulted in a 2-2 draw and left them 19th in the Champions League standings.

United trailed at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved one penalty before conceding another 75 seconds later that was converted by Luis Suarez after the Belgian's reckless challenge on Max Araujo.

"This is the assist of the season" 😅



Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf which led to his second goal of the evening for Man Utd 🪄



📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/c4g2sC33pA — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 25, 2026

Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf

The visitors were left furious when Amad Diallo saw a first-half leveller ruled out after referee Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle too early for VAR to intervene, but United turned the game around shortly after the restart.

Lisandro Martinez, who had given away the first penalty, won one at the other end that Fernandes converted before the former Sporting star fired in the long-range effort that bounced over Pereira and into the net.

More drama followed as Lammens flapped at a cross under pressure from Suarez, allowing the striker to score, before Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have put undue pressure on Pereira when forcing an own goal from the goalkeeper.

United were left frustrated by what they viewed as a lack of consistency after Marciniak was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the second decision, and their mood darkened further when Youri Tielemans was sent off for a second booking late on.

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'.

Young told BBC Radio 5 Live: 'The referee’s performance was just simply wow. The decisions that he gave.

'Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal.

'The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

'His decision-making is nothing more than a disgrace.'

Former United player Ashley Young claimed that 2022 World Cup referee Marciniak's decision-making during the clash was a 'disgrace'

Young’s former United team-mate Rio Ferdinand echoed that frustration on X.

Writing alongside a pain image of himself, he said with two emojis indicating angry swearing: 'REFEREE. What have I just witnessed tonight!

'Regardless – individual mistakes again proving costly. Positives to take from tonight, recharge the batteries!'

In what is proving to be an eventful first week in charge, Pochettino was asked to provide his assessment of the game. The Argentine said: 'It depends which way you prefer (to analyse the game). So proud of the players. It was a very tough game. I like the team for the 90 minutes, the personality, the character.

'We showed the way we want to play. We've only been working together one week.'

But, he added: 'Always we need to concentrate more and focus more. Try to recover better. We start to fix. With a performance like today it's the best medicine to prepare the next game.'

United have little time to take stock before their next outing, with Brentford visiting Old Trafford on Saturday.

Sports.title: Gibbs goes off but 'Iceman' Williams, Bears steal the show in Thanksgiving thriller
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

DETROIT -- The Chicago Bears' first division win of the season came by way of a shootout, and wide receiver Rome Odunze used every inch of his 6-foot-3 frame to leap into the air and come down with the game-winning touchdown catch in the waning moments on Thanksgiving Day.

After two weeks of offensive struggles that bled into Thursday's game at Detroit, Chicago put together a 39-35 come-from-behind victory to mark the second-highest-scoring Thanksgiving game over the past 10 seasons.

Caleb Williams' 6-yard touchdown pass to Odunze with three seconds left marks the first time there has been a lead change in a Bears game since Week 1, when Chicago trailed 7-0 at the Panthers in the first quarter and then took a 14-7 lead in that same period.

The Bears earned their 10th win of the season and a critical tiebreaker against the Lions to finally gain some ground in the division as they leave Ford Field in sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images

What to make of the QB performance: Williams continues to struggle with pressure. He went 4-of-9 for 39 yards and took a season-high four sacks when pressured in Detroit, which was similar to how he performed under the same circumstances against the Saints (2-of-6, 35 yards, two sacks). He took a beating and his frustrations were visible. But when Williams turned into the "Iceman" in the fourth quarter, he shined. He made it a three-point game when he connected with Odunze for a 41-yard touchdown and ran in a two-point conversion. Then he delivered his signature late-game magic, finding Odunze once again for a 6-yard touchdown to win the game.

Trend to watch: The Bears were already shifting away from 13 personnel (three TEs, one WR, one RB) after tight end Cole Kmet was placed on season-ending injured reserve on Oct. 23. They may now have to use three-tight-end sets even less frequently after Colston Loveland was quickly ruled out with a left knee injury in the first quarter. Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson are the only healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster, and rookie Hayden Large, who caught Johnson's attention throughout the offseason, is still on IR. Loveland ranks third on the Bears in receiving (40 catches, 392 yards, three TDs). An extended absence would undoubtedly alter Chicago's offensive philosophy.

Stat to know: Thursday marked the Bears' 39th time playing on Thanksgiving. After missing five games (turf toe/thumb) and struggling in his return in Week 11, Kyle Monangai sparked the run game (7.2 yards per carry) and became the first Bears player with multiple rushing touchdowns on Thanksgiving since George Gulyanics in 1949. It marked Monangai's second career multi-touchdown game, with his previous coming in Week 4.

Next game: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (Dec. 6, at 1 p.m. ET)

Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images

Thanksgiving football has long been a marquee event in Detroit, and Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs had taken center stage on Thursday before Williams and the Bears stole the show.

Gibbs and the Lions were playing their third game in 11 days and didn't show any signs of fatigue early on but suffered a heartbreaking defeat in a pivotal NFC North showdown in which they could've taken command of the division with a victory.

Gibbs finished with 252 total yards and three touchdowns, including a 70-yard run in the fourth quarter, which prompted "M-V-P" chants at Ford Field, but it wasn't enough as Detroit saw its six-game winning streak snapped.

What to make of the QB performance: Lions QB Jared Goff routinely connected with his playmakers, displaying pinpoint accuracy as he went 19-for-28 with 249 passing yards and a touchdown in a head-to-head battle with Williams. Goff completed five receptions to WR Amon-Ra St. Brown for 114 yards while delivering darts for big gains to Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta. In six career games on Thanksgiving, Goff has 11 touchdowns with one interception as he continues to produce at an elite level this season.

Stat to know: Gibbs has continued to produce at a historic pace in his fourth NFL season, passing another mark by Hall of Famer Barry Sanders with the most rushing TDs before turning 25, both including (58) and excluding the playoffs (53). There have been only eight seasons in which a Lions player has scored at least 16 touchdowns, and Gibbs now has three of those.

Next game: vs. Atlanta Falcons (Dec. 6, at 1 p.m. ET)

Sports.title: Steelers owner: Rodgers' 'insubordination can't be tolerated,' backs McCarthy
Sports.content:
'He's got to go!' Stephen A. implores Steelers to move on from Mike McCarthy (2:02)

Open Extended Reactions

PITTSBURGH -- A day after Aaron Rodgers unleashed a firestorm of accusations about Mike McCarthy's fitness to coach, Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president Art Rooney II said in a statement to ESPN on Thursday that he has "100% confidence in Mike McCarthy" while also telling a newspaper that he supported moving on from Rodgers.

Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette that "insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

The stunning decision to bench and release Rodgers was prompted in part by the quarterback's demands to make changes to the playcalling structure.

Rooney told the Post-Gazette that he "expects" McCarthy to "be our coach this season, next season and beyond." He reiterated that sentiment to ESPN.

"I am disappointed in where this went with Aaron Rodgers, but I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy," Rooney said in his statement. "And I have tremendous confidence in Mason Rudolph and the other players in our locker room.

"Decisions were made on what we believe is in the best interest of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Our main focus right now is preparing for tomorrow's game."

Rodgers made a litany of accusations in a 34-minute interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday that included McCarthy sleeping in meetings, missing meetings and breaking down a huddle at halftime of last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles with "1, 2, 3, Packers" -- an incident McCarthy said was an "embarrassing moment."

Rooney told the Post-Gazette he doesn't have any concerns about McCarthy's health.

"Mike's as healthy as the rest of us," Rooney said. "Health was not an issue. I'm not sure where that part comes."

In Wednesday's interview, Rodgers said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched in favor of Rudolph and would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and hadn't heard the news from McCarthy.

McCarthy responded to the allegations when he met with the media later Wednesday, saying the Steelers front office was "very in tune with everything that goes on in football operations as far as my job responsibility."

Rooney said in his statement to ESPN that he has "responsibility for ensuring the team and entire organization meets our standards."

The Steelers waived Rodgers shortly after the interview Wednesday. He officially cleared waivers Thursday, making him a free agent.

Sports.title: Steelers activate Pittman, sign Hurleman, whom Rodgers recently advocated for
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

PITTSBURGH -- Amid a tumultuous stretch that saw their onetime starting quarterback give a scorched-earth interview about their head coach, the Pittsburgh Steelers added a pair of wide receivers to the active roster ahead of Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

The Steelers activated Michael Pittman Jr. from injured reserve Thursday and signed Max Hurleman to the active roster from the practice squad. One receiver filled the roster spot vacated by quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who was waived by the Steelers on Wednesday and cleared waivers Thursday, becoming a free agent.

The other roster spot was created by the Steelers placing wide receiver and special teams ace Ben Skowronek on IR with a calf injury. Skowronek also missed time earlier this season with a calf injury.

Hurleman led the Steelers with 61 receiving yards and a touchdown in his NFL debut a week ago as a practice squad game-day elevation. A second-year undrafted free agent, Hurleman sustained an injury in training camp that kept him out of practice for half of the season.

A day before he was waived, Rodgers advocated for Hurleman -- who spent the bulk of his collegiate career at FCS program Colgate -- to get more opportunities.

"I think everybody felt before the injury in camp that he was a 53 guy," Rodgers said Tuesday afternoon. "I know the guys in our room did for sure. So for him to go out there and finally get elevated and go out and play the way he played was not surprising to any of us, but great for his confidence and great reminder for the folks upstairs what kind of player he is."

Pittman, meanwhile, hasn't played since Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss at Cleveland, where he had two catches for 15 yards.

Acquired by the Steelers in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts just before free agency, Pittman sustained an undisclosed injury that caused him to miss a large part of training camp. He then missed the Steelers' Week 2 game against the New England Patriots with a foot injury that began as plantar fasciitis, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Pittman returned to play against the Bengals and Browns, but after the injury worsened in practice prior to the Week 5 game against his old team, Pittman was placed on IR.

The Steelers opened his 21-day practice window on Nov. 18, but he remained sidelined through their Week 10 loss to the Eagles.

"It's more about being able to move efficiently," Pittman said on Nov. 18 about managing the injury. "And if I can do that, then I'll be out there, and if the coaches decide I can't, then we'll see where that goes."

Pittman fully participated in each practice during the short week, leading to his activation. Though he was productive in six seasons with the Colts, Pittman has started slowly in Pittsburgh with just seven receptions on 12 targets for 89 yards.

Sports.title: Devils' Dillon receives 4-game suspension for illegal hit to the head
Sports.content:
New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon received a four-game suspension Thursday for an illegal hit to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk.

Dillon was assessed a match penalty for the check during the first period of the Devils' 3-2 shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game after the hit.

Dillon forfeits $82,474.24 based on his average annual salary and under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. The money goes to the Players' Emergency Assistance Fund.

On the play, Mateychuk skated through neutral ice and entered the zone before moving the puck to a teammate. Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a "high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable," the NHL's department of player safety said in a video.

Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness said after the game: "I've coached Dillon. He's not a dirty player. He's a hard player. He caught him in a bad spot, and that's a bad hit. It is."

Bowness said Wednesday that he spoke with Mateychuk and the defenseman "feels fine." Bowness added that "protocol will take over and we'll go from there."

Sports.title: Early 3 pushes Hidalgo to top of Notre Dame scoring chart
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

NASSAU, Bahamas -- Hannah Hidalgo had 22 points and nine steals as she became Notre Dame's all-time leading scorer during the 13th-ranked Fighting Irish's 78-64 win over No. 22 West Virginia on Thursday at the Battle 4 Atlantis.

Hidalgo has 2,648 career points, and her 3-pointer about three minutes into the game made it 10-0 and broke Arike Ogunbowale's record (2,626).

She has scored in double figures in 110 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the nation, and has three games this season with at least seven steals.

Jacy Abii added 16 points, 12 rebounds and four steals for Notre Dame (7-0). Madison St. Rose scored 16, Leah Macy had 10 points, and Anaya Hardy had 11 rebounds to go with eight points.

Gia Cooke led West Virginia (6-1) with 18 points, Zahirah Walton scored 17 and Skylar Forbes 11.

The Irish closed the first quarter with 11 consecutive points to take a 23-11 lead into the second.

Walton scored six points in an 11-2 run that cut West Virginia's deficit to 45-37 with 4:07 to play in the third quarter, but Notre Dame scored 13 of the next 15 points and led by double figures throughout the fourth.

The Irish scored 28 points off 24 West Virginia turnovers (including 18 Notre Dame steals), outrebounded the Mountaineers 48-33 and had a 22-7 advantage in second-chance points.

Notre Dame next plays Thursday at No. 12 Vanderbilt in the SEC/ACC Women's Challenge.
