Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Puts Canelo Alvarez Rematch Odds At Five Percent
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol doubts that Canelo Alvarez will fight him again, rating it as just a 5% chance. Both Canelo and his trainer, Eddy Reynoso, said last month they want to fight Bivol or Terence Crawford next, following Canelo’s win over Christian Mbilli on October 31. Interestingly, Bivol says his team has never received any offer from Canelo for a rematch.

Bivol (25-1, 12 KOs) is defending his IBF, WBA, and WBO light heavyweight titles next month against Callum Smith (31-2, 22 KOs) in Ekaterinburg, Russia, at the UMMC Arena.

“To be honest, I’m feeling like on 5% it could happen,” Bivol told The Stomping Ground. “Yeah. Just kind of past that.”

Canelo lost a 12-round unanimous decision to Bivol in May 2022 in Las Vegas. Despite the close scorecards, the fight was one-sided. Bivol dominated Canelo with combinations and in-and-out movement.

“Well, look, I would like an immediate rematch with Crawford. Hopefully, Crawford can return to boxing, which I think he already said he might come back, and I would like the rematch with him. And if that is not possible, someday also have a rematch with Bivol,” said Eddy Reynoso to Fight Hub TV Español.

Saudi Funding And U.S. Box Office Reality

The lack of movement on a rematch with Bivol may not be entirely Canelo’s fault. For the fight to happen, the Saudis would need to finance it. Canelo is signed with Turki Alalshikh and Riyadh Season and is being paid well, reportedly in the hundreds of millions, with his per-fight purses being large.

Unless Riyadh is willing to fund rematches with Bivol and Crawford, those fights have little chance of happening because of the purse requirements. Those two would want large purses as well, perhaps as much as Canelo.

The problem is, Bivol isn’t a big name in the U.S., so the PPV buys wouldn’t likely cover the guaranteed purses for him and Canelo. The interest from casual fans isn’t enough to make the rematch worth funding. Moreover, Bivol’s inactivity has hurt the measure of popularity that he’d gotten from his wins over Canelo and Artur Beterbiev.

It makes sense for Riyadh Season to not pursue rematches between Canelo and Bivol or Crawford. If Canelo loses again to one or both, his value to the Saudis declines. Also, what fans may be overlooking is how boring those fights were.

Bivol just boxed Canelo from the outside and rarely stood in front of him to go toe-to-toe, as fans like to see from their fighters. If the Saudis want to see pure action, they can get more return by targeting fighters with more entertaining styles for Canelo.

Bivol admitted that Canelo has a lot of options for other fights to keep him busy in this late stage of his career. Canelo doesn’t need him.

The Saudi spending changes have also been seen affecting Bivol’s trilogy fight with Artur Beterbiev, which still hasn’t taken place after they fought for the second time in 2025, due to Riyadh Season no longer choosing to finance it. With both fighters reportedly getting $10 million each for their first two fights that were funded by the Saudis, fighting for less than that without their involvement doesn’t work. It’s too risky a fight for Bivol and Beterbiev to take without receiving outside financing.

Why Bivol Rejects The Easy Rematch Talk

“Never. Never. Second fight is never easier against anybody. Maybe it even harder,” Bivol said when asked if a rematch with Canelo, now 36, would be easy, believing the adjustments the Mexican star would make would present a problem.

If the Canelo vs. Bivol rematch is going to happen, the Saudi financiers will need to come up with the money to fund it. Ideally, it would be great if Bivol agreed to take a smaller purse just so he could make the rematch happen, but that doesn’t sound realistic. If anything, he’d want a massive purse that doesn’t balance out with the low number of PPV buys the match would likely bring in.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Brushes Off Pressure Ahead Of Nelson Hysa Defense
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel says he feels no pressure going into Saturday night’s title defense of his WBC heavyweight belt against fringe contender Nelson Hysa at the Merkur Spiel-Arena in Düsseldorf, Germany. This is the type of fight where Kabayel can win and receive absolutely no credit. It’s considered a pure 100% mismatch.

Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) will be making his first defense of his WBC belt against the 42-year-old Hysa. It’s not the ideal type of fight for Kabayel, but the top contenders were all busy, leaving him with limited options. He’s in the ‘who needs him’ club, where he’s too risky for big-money stars like Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury, or Oleksandr Usyk to face. That leaves Kabayel stuck, fighting no-names like Hysa, and not getting much press because of that.

Since Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) is also with Queensberry, it was a no-brainer match-up to be made. It’s an in-house fight, and a large crowd of nearly 50,000 is expected.

“I was the underdog over and over again, and then right now I’m the favorite, and there is no pressure,” Kabayel said at Thursday’s DAZN Boxing press conference via a stage translator. “I am Agit Kabayel. I want to be better in every fight and I want to show that to the people, and there’s no pressure for me.”

Spencer Brown Calls Out The Resume Gap

Hysa made a big deal during the buildup for this fight, boasting about having done well in sparring with Kabayel in the past, and criticizing him about his delay in signing.

“About that I call him rabbit, it was before that he and his team accept the fight,” said Hysa. “He’s not a rabbit. He’s a good guy. He’s a good boxer.”

Hysa had to say something to get fans into the fight, because this match-up had been largely ignored by people for obvious reasons. Hysa is not a household name, has never beaten anyone recognizable, and is not exactly young at 42. In situations like this, there’s desperation to come up with trash talk that gets the attention of fans.

“He can talk so much bullst, you know, this is no problem,” said Kabayel. “I give him, you know, he’s the better trash talker than me, but in the ring you must fight. After that, he say, ‘You are afraid from me.’ So bro, I never scared from one guy in the heavyweight division.”

Well, Hysa looked powerful in his last fight, knocking out previously unbeaten Thomas Narmo (14-1, 14 KOs), but he was facing a guy with a resume filled with second-tier opposition. Hysa beat him, but he was just as unknown as his previous 24 opponents.

“Let’s have a look at the levels of the different fighters that you’ve faced and he’s faced,” Brown told Hysa on the dais. “Let’s not get into it because they’re completely different levels. Anybody they’ve thrown in front of him, he has taken them out. These are world-class one, two, three boys.”

Returning Heavyweight Boxing To Düsseldorf

Saturday’s heavyweight championship event in Düsseldorf, Germany, will be the first one at the venue since Tyson Fury defeated 39-year-old Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. That fight wasn’t the most entertaining to watch, as there was very little action between the two large heavyweights. Kabayel vs. Hysa should provide more sparks while it lasts in their fight live on DAZN.

“The fight 11 years ago when Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury, it was bad for Germany, but Tyson Fury kind of inspired me, and now I got the same manager, and this was kind of the starting point,” said Kabayel.

Kabayel will surely take the fight to Hysa immediately, targeting his body, looking to wear him down and score a stoppage to please the large German crowd.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Eyes Willy Hutchinson To Escape 168 Minefield
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez would be showing genuine bravery if he actually returned to light heavyweight to face WBC champion Willy Hutchinson in the first quarter of 2027. Hutchinson is the target right now over the three super middleweights, Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

“Canelo has given the green light,” said talkSPORT Boxing host Ade Oladipo.

Trainer Eddy Reynoso will have a say in whether Alvarez signs for this fight. Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs) defeated Joshua Buatsi on November 7 to win the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, switch-hitting, moving, jabbing, and landing clean shots.

He had Buatsi tied in knots throughout that fight with his versatility. Hutchinson showed that he can punch, move, and take a shot. At 28, the 6’1″ Hutchinson is confident, and he’s not going to fight timidly against Canelo the way unbeaten contender Christian Mbilli did in their fight on October 31.

“Willie Hutchinson could sneak a points victory against Canelo in my view,” said talkSPORT analyst Gareth A. Davies. “I’ve seen enough from Willie now in the last couple of years to know this guy walks into the ring just so confident and has the style as a mover to cause Canelo problems. Those are the fighters that have caused the big man problems.”

Canelo (64-3-2, 39 KOs) looked overmatched the last time he fought at 175 against the pure boxer Dmitry Bivol in May 2022, losing a 12-round unanimous decision. In a sign of resignation and defeat, Canelo never attempted to avenge the loss by signing for a rematch with Bivol. Instead, he moved on toward softer targets, fighting 40-year-old Gennady Golovkin and John Ryder.

The 36-year-old Canelo’s mobility is slower now than it was in 2022, and he would have to find a way to improve that for him to have a chance of dethroning the 28-year-old Hutchinson in early 2027. The way Canelo looked against Mbilli, slow and always waiting near the ropes, he’d get picked apart by Hutchinson.

Reynoso has no easy outs for Canelo at 168. Against Mbilli, it was the perfect situation: fighting a guy who changed his normal fighting style of volume punching and instead attempted to outpunch Canelo with single shots. Even with the fight slipping away, Mbilli never switched to plan B by returning to his normal fighting style.

If Canelo stays at super middleweight, he can’t count on IBF champion Osleys Iglesias (16-0, 15 KOs) or interim WBC titlist Lester Martinez (21-0-1, 17 KOs) mentally undermining themselves by changing their normal fighting styles in an attempt to beat him at his own game. They’d both stick with what’s worked for them, which is an attack-oriented style that provides no rest breaks for their opponents.

Choosing Hamzah Sheeraz would result in Canelo being ridiculed by fans, who view the British fighter as a classic example of a fake manufactured hype job. Reynoso has been around long enough to know what the fan perception is of Hamzah by now, and he would recognize ahead of time what the reaction would be if Canelo picked him as his next opponent. It would be a PR disaster.

For Canelo, the best strategy would be moving back up to 175 pounds to face Hutchinson to try and figure out this difficult puzzle. He would be gambling by facing him, but staying at 168 could be far worse. If Canelo loses at 168, he won’t have the weight excuse he gets by moving back up to light heavyweight.

Sports.title: Joseph Parker Ready To Break Daniel Dubois Will Again
Sports.content:
Could Daniel Dubois quit if Joseph Parker takes him into the later rounds and he feels the fight slipping away? Dubois has proven to be a royal basket case when the going gets tough in fights. He’s fine when things are going well, but he goes to pieces when dealing with adversity.

We may see that happen before our eyes on January 30 when he defends his WBO heavyweight title against the experienced veteran Parker at the Co-op Live in Manchester, England. Parker is accustomed to war in the trenches and thrives on conflict. You can’t say the same thing about Dubois.

Queensberry Promotions is trying to sell this thing as unfinished business from February 2025 in Riyadh, where Dubois pulled out during fight week sick, and Parker knocked out an out-of-shape Martin Bakole in two rounds. Plenty of boxing fans still think Dubois got cold feet back then rather than being ill.

All I can say is he didn’t look thrilled sitting across from Parker on DAZN. He had fear in his eyes, being stared down by Parker. From that brief meeting, it’s easy to believe he pulled out of the fight because of stage fright.

Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) will be favored to win, yet his reckless style leaves him wide open for a fast veteran counterpuncher. He marches forward behind a hard jab, which worked well for him against Jarrell Miller and Anthony Joshua. It’s going to take more than a jab to defeat Parker because he’s well equipped to neutralize that weapon.

If Parker gets inside and forces Dubois onto his back foot, Dubois tends to mentally crumble fast. Once Dubois hits the deck, he appears to give up on himself, looking at his corner for help.

Dubois has been through a lot of brutal fights since 2022, and we’ve all seen his chin give out when somebody survives his early bum rush and hits him flush, just like Oleksandr Usyk and Kevin Lerena did. You could see the look of resignation on Dubois’ face in those fights. He got lucky against Lerena when his opponent gassed out.

Parker (36-4, 24 KOs) is coming back after a year out since Fabio Wardley stopped him in the eleventh round in October 2025. He served a suspension, but chose not to take a tune-up. It makes sense because he wasn’t going to pass up this golden opportunity to relieve a vulnerable champion of his WBO belt,

“I almost feel like there’s a bit of me that thinks Joseph deserves it,” said Ade Oladipo on his YouTube channel.

It makes sense why Frank Warren is making this fight. He also promotes WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and IBF belt holder Filip Hrgovic. Matching the aging, soon-to-be 35-year-old Parker against Dubois removes the risk that would be there if he put him in against Kabayel or Hrgovic. Parker is a safer opponent on paper, and even if there is an upset, the WBO title still stays with Queensberry. Although Dubois did beat Hrgovic in the past, it would be risky putting him in with him now after Hrgovic’s win over Moses Itauma. The last thing Warren needs is for Hrgovic to beat Dubois.

Parker’s hunger still makes him a real threat to beat Dubois. If Parker is still standing past the midpoint of the fight, he could break Dubois down and make him quit like he did against Usyk and Joe Joyce. As the saying goes, once a quitter, always a quitter.

Sports.title: British Fans Rip Weak Fury vs. Joshua Undercard Lineup
Sports.content:
Turki Alalshikh revealed the full card for the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua event on December 11 at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and the fan reaction has been negative, particularly among Brits.

With the Fury vs. Joshua fight being billed as the biggest domestic heavyweight bout in years in the main event, fans are hopping mad that the undercard looks like it’s been thrown together without any care about quality.

Fans are finally realizing they’re basically paying for the Fury vs. Joshua fight and getting nothing else worth watching.

Virtually all the undercard bouts, including the co-feature pitting Deontay Wilder vs. Martin Bakole, have been bashed as pure 100% garbage. Fans who subscribed to Netflix just to see the event aren’t happy about it. I’m not surprised.

We saw the same thing with Floyd Mayweather Jr. vs. Manny Pacquiao and Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford. All the effort and dough went into the main events for those two mega-events, and man, did the undercards look like junk of the highest kind.

Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn got one of his fighters, former two-time super featherweight champion Joe Cordina, onto the card. The kicker is that Cordina, 35, has been placed on the preliminary portion of the card, fighting Mauricio Lara, out of sight, out of mind.

If Hearn thought this was Cordina’s big chance to win back the fans he lost when he was knocked out by Anthony Cacace in the eighth round in May 2024, he can forget it.

“What about Joe Cordina?” Hearn said when discussing the lineup. “What about a two-time world champion from Wales? Absolutely mental.”

Hearn had been banging the drum about wanting Cordina to fight on the main card against Manny Pacquiao, WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason, or Sam Noakes. Instead of fighting one of them in a highly visible fight, Cordina will be hidden away on the prelim card that will be shown on Netflix, TikTok, and The Ring social channels.

Hearn has got to be hopping mad, seeing his fighter fail to make the grade for the main card. I can totally understand the organizers’ decision to place the Cordina vs. Lara fight on the prelim card. Neither of these two fighters has beaten anyone halfway decent since losing. Cordina beat a fringe contender in Gabriel Flores Jr. and a lower-level fighter in Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz since losing to Cacace.

As for Lara, he’s won his last five fights against obscure opposition in confidence builders after fighting to a draw against Daniel Lugo in February 2024 and losing to Leigh Wood by a 12-round unanimous decision in May 2023.

The main card is just as abysmal, with Deontay Wilder facing replacement opponent Martin Bakole in the chief support bout after Jai Opetaia’s injury pullout, Zuffa heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter battling Michael Essomba, and Moses Jolly fighting Igor Adiel Macedo.

Hearn blasted Zuffa promoter Dana White and Zuffa’s influence for the poor undercard, and British fans are replying in droves to Turki’s undercard lineup, echoing Hearn’s thoughts. The people who paid good cash for tickets to see the event live in Cardiff are harping about the scarcity of UK fighters, the 1:30 a.m. local start time for the headliner, and the lack of quality fights beyond the Joshua vs. Fury fight.

The rest of the preliminary lineup is filled with obscure prospects and names that even hardcore boxing fans won’t recognize, aside from Tyson’s younger brother Roman Fury. If you’re tuning in on December 11, you don’t need to set your alarm until right before the main event.

Sports.title: WBA Sets 75-25 Split for Teofimo Lopez Against Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
It’s not looking good for Teofimo Lopez to dodge his mandatory obligations at welterweight. Today, the WBA called a purse bid for December 4 in Cypress, Texas, for a fight between WBA welterweight Super Champion Teofimo and Jack Catterall with a slanted 75/25 purse split.

Financially, that should make Teofimo happy. Even with three-quarters of the money guaranteed, he’s shown no eagerness to sign to fight the mandatory he inherited after his win over WBA champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero by majority decision on August 22. Lopez needs a special permit from the WBA to avoid Catterall (33-2, 14 KOs), but he may not get his wish. It’s understandable why Teofimo doesn’t want to fight Catterall. It’s a style that he’s struggled with, and it’s unlikely he would win.

Teofimo (23-2, 13 KOs) wants to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in what would be a lucrative unification, where even if he loses, he’d still do well financially. He needs the WBA title for purse negotiations more so than it being a valuable chip to create more interest in a fight with Ryan.

Teofimo’s title isn’t why fans are interested in seeing the fight. For him, it’s just a negotiation tool to get a better deal, because he lacks Ryan’s popularity to get an even split. Even with a title, you can argue that Teofimo doesn’t rate a 50/50 purse split.

Catterall Risk Explains Lopez Delay

If this were an easy mark, Lopez would be overjoyed at receiving a 75/25 gift split from the WBA. Catterall’s style is similar to Shakur Stevenson’s, which left Teofimo baffled and helpless in a unanimous decision loss over 12 rounds earlier this year at Madison Square Garden on January 31. Teofimo looked embarrassingly bad in that fight. The judges scored it 119 to 109 on all three cards, and he was outlanded 165 to 72.

Defensively, Catterall isn’t as sharp as Shakur, but he’s close enough to be the same kind of nightmare for Teofimo. On offense, Catterall is superior to Shakur, and coupled with his defensive ability, he would be a difficult problem for Teofimo to try and figure out. Besides all that, the pressure that Teofimo would be under would be severe if he needs to defeat Catterall to get to the lucrative payday fight against Ryan Garcia.

If he gets beaten by Catterall, he can forget about fighting Ryan for the time being. Unlike his loss to Shakur, Teofimo wouldn’t be given a straight title shot immediately after. He’d have to rebuild and get in line, which is what he should have had to do after losing to Stevenson instead of being given a crack at Rolly’s WBA title.

Catterall captured his WBA regular welterweight title by beating former mandatory Shakhram Giyasov by a wide 12-round unanimous decision last May. Giyasov was the mandatory challenger that Rolly was avoiding. Now, we’re seeing the new WBA champion Teofimo trying to give Catterall similar treatment. The WBA can stop this cycle by rejecting Teofimo’s request for a special permit.

It’s easy to predict what Lopez’s next move will be if the WBA rejects his appeal. Vacating the WBA belt will be the easiest way of getting Catterall out of his path to a fight with Ryan. Teofimo will still get a nice payday against Ryan, but probably not as nice as it would be if he still had his WBA title.

Sports.title: Brian Mendoza Replaces Keith Thurman in Weak Vergil Ortiz Jr. Co-Feature
Sports.content:
PBC and Golden Boy Promotions made it official today with Brian Mendoza replacing Keith Thurman as Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s opponent for his 10-round co-feature middleweight bout on December 5 at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona.

Ortiz Jr. and Mendoza will be fighting on the undercard of WBA and WBO cruiserweight champion David Benavidez’s unification bout against WBC champion Michal Cieslak on DAZN PPV and Prime Video.

The addition of Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) has received mixed views from fans. Many of them view the 32-year-old as a poor replacement, given his 1-3 record in his last four fights. That’s not exactly top shelf unless losing is the benchmark requirement used to get enlisted as a fill-in opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.

Back in Mediocrity Since Fundora

What Mendoza has got going for him is that he knocked out Sebastian Fundora in the seventh round in April 2023 in a huge upset at the time. Fundora was beating the living daylights out of Mendoza for the first six rounds until he got careless in the seventh and got clipped. Since then, Mendoza’s career has slipped back to what it was before that win. That was his textbook Cinderella night, where he got lucky in a fight that he was getting beaten up in.

What’s interesting is that fans online see this as an upgrade over 38-year-old Thurman, just because of his win over Fundora. If you look at Mendoza’s results since that upset, he’s a major downgrade, and that’s saying a lot because Thurman was not a great opponent. He’s not a middleweight, and definitely not young.

Tim Tszyu beat Mendoza by a wide 12-round unanimous decision in October 2023. That fight was an example of Mendoza being brought back down to earth. It wasn’t even slightly a close fight. It looked like Mendoza wandered into the ring from the crowd, and Tszyu took advantage by beating the stuffing out of him. Serhii Bohachuk did the same thing to Mendoza in a clash for the interim WBC junior middleweight title in March 2024.

The only win for Mendoza in the last three years came against journeyman Jesus Antonio Rojas (12-11-2, 10 KOs). It took that level of opponent for Mendoza to snap his two-fight losing streak. In Mendoza’s last fight, he returned to his losing ways, getting trounced by Yoenis Tellez by a one-sided 10-round unanimous decision in March 2026.

Basically, what we’re seeing here is not a dangerous threat being used as a replacement opponent for Ortiz Jr. (24-0, 22 KOs), who recently looked like pure gold in wins over Israil Madrimov, Bohachuk, and Erickson Lubin.

A Cheap Showcase for Ortiz Jr.

Yanking Mendoza out of his fight with Eric Priest enabled Sampson Boxing, TGB Promotions, and Golden Boy Promotions to save money on finding a quality opponent. It’s a showcase fight for Ortiz Jr. Ideally, they should have spent some money to enlist a quality middleweight contender like Yoenli Hernandez to put Ortiz Jr. in a sink-or-swim fight.

What Mendoza does have going for him is a strong chin, as he’s never been knocked out in his career. So if the idea is for Ortiz Jr. to get some rounds in to sharpen up after a year on the shelf, Mendoza is the guy for the job. However, the referee may step in and halt this fight anyway because of the likely one-sided nature of it.

Entertainment-wise, Mendoza eating hard shots from Ortiz Jr. is not fun to watch in a PPV co-feature slot. Fans want competitive fights, not slaughters.

Ortiz Jr. is 28 years old, making the move up to middleweight, and has still accomplished little in his career. It’s got to bug him that he sees fighters like Jaron ‘Boots’ Ennis taking the express route to superstardom, leaving him behind. The difference is, Ennis has been a risk-taker from day one, hasn’t feasted on weak opposition, and has stayed active. In contrast, Ortiz Jr. hasn’t fought the best, and he’s missed a lot of time in his career due to health and promotional issues.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Gets Worst Possible Replacement In Martin Bakole
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder is facing the worst possible replacement opponent for him in his December 11th fight in Cardiff against the heavy-handed Martin Bakole. It’s not the type of opponent that the 41-year-old Wilder’s legs can deal with at this stage of his career.

Boxing analyst Sergio Mora pointed out this week that Wilder no longer has the mobility at his age to avoid being walked down by a big puncher like Bakole. He feels that Wilder will have problems keeping Bakole off of him and will be forced to slug it out right off the bat from round 1 on December 11th.

“If you don’t fight him off the right way, he’s going to mow you down. And you got to have legs to do that,” said Mora on Chris Mannix’s podcast.

Wilder never really had great leg movement. If you look at his earliest fights against Harold Sconiers and Bermane Stiverne, he wasn’t a mover. He was winning by unleashing his right hand on them. Back then, before the two later shoulder surgeries on that side, Wilder’s right hand was lethal. It made up for his lack of mobility and boxing skills.

After his originally scheduled opponent, Jai Opetaia, dropped out due to a hand injury, the former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) wanted a rematch with Derek Chisora or a fight with Jarrell Miller. Neither was selected, which is good news for fans. Both are long in the tooth and don’t have the kind of power that could erase Wilder the way Bakole can.

For what Wilder is aiming for, a world title shot in his next fight, he should have to fight and beat the likes of Bakole to get his wish. It would look pathetic if Wilder is given a title shot after beating an old war horse like Chisora a second time or getting past Miller.

Why Bakole Is A Dangerous Gamble

Despite Bakole being held to a draw against Efe Ajagba in his last outing, and knocked out in the second round by Joseph Parker in a short-notice fight in 2025, Bakole still has power in both hands. He’s dangerous up close when he lands cleanly.

In those two fights, Bakole wasn’t in the best shape in terms of his weight. For this one, he’d been training to fight Solomon Adebayo on the December 11th undercard. Being in shape for this fight means Bakole will be a constant threat to Wilder in the early rounds.

If Wilder’s right hand is back to full strength, he could stop Bakole. However, Wilder hasn’t shown his once-devastating power since 2022, when he knocked out Robert Helenius in the 1st round. Mora and Mannix agreed that Jarrell Miller would have been the better choice to sell the matchup without carrying the same threat as Bakole. The organizers made the right choice because the card needed a high-drama matchup. We don’t see that in the main event or any of the undercard fights.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must replace high-stakes basic education examinations with a centralised online cumulative assessment system
Ghana News.content:
Dr Kofi Nseibo

A call for an inclusive, continuous and competency-based assessment system for progression from Basic 4 to Basic 9

Introduction: It Is Time to Rethink BECE

The ongoing debate in Ghana about preventing candidates from sitting the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) before reaching Junior High School (JHS) 3 presents an important opportunity to reconsider the country's approach to assessing learners and determining their progression into Senior High School (SHS).

While the proposed restriction may address concerns about candidates writing the examination prematurely, it does not necessarily address the more fundamental question: Is a single high-stakes examination at the end of basic education still the most appropriate way to assess learners and determine their readiness for senior high school?

Ghana should move beyond the debate about when students should write BECE and begin considering whether the country needs to retain the examination in its current form at all.

I propose that Ghana gradually replaces the BECE with a Centralised Online Cumulative Assessment System (COCAS), covering learners' academic progress and competencies from at least Basic 4 to Basic 9. This system would provide a more comprehensive, continuous and equitable basis for determining progression into senior high school.

This proposal draws on the concerns raised by Nseibo (2021) regarding examination-driven competition, school admission practices and the exclusion of children with disabilities from mainstream schools. It also speaks to the broader objectives of Ghana's inclusive education and standards-based curriculum policies.

The central argument is that Ghana's education system should assess what learners know, understand and can do over time rather than allow the outcome of a single examination to determine their educational progression.

The Current Policy Debate: Addressing the Problem Rather Than Punishing Early Candidates

On 23 November 2026, Ghana's Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, directed the Ghana Education Service to impose a two-year examination ban on pupils who attempt to sit the BECE before their designated examination year. The directive seeks to discourage the practice of advancing JHS 1 and JHS 2 pupils prematurely to write the examination. It will also clear doughs about how such candidates got their cumulative assessment for WAEC to determine the grades for them.

MyJoyOnline highlights: while the government's concerns about fairness, academic progression and examination integrity are understandable, a punitive restriction does not necessarily address the underlying weaknesses in the assessment and placement system.

Indeed, Africa Education Watch has raised concerns that enforcing the restriction without a reliable student-tracking system and unique learner identification could prove ineffective.

Another highlight by MyJoyOnline indicates that rather than focusing primarily on preventing children from writing BECE early, Ghana should invest in a national system that tracks learners' progress throughout their basic education.

The question policymakers should be asking is not simply how to prevent early BECE candidates, but why the country continues to depend so heavily on a terminal examination (summative assessment) when a more comprehensive assessment system is possible (formative assessment).

What Ghanaian Education Policies Already Tell Us

The proposal to replace BECE is not disconnected from Ghana's existing educational policy direction. In fact, several national policy instruments provide a foundation for this transition.

1. National Pre-Tertiary Learning Assessment Framework (NPLAF), 2020

Developed by the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), the NPLAF provides an important foundation for moving away from an assessment culture dominated by terminal examinations.

The framework advocates assessment of learners' knowledge, skills, values and competencies. It recognises school-based, district-level and national-level assessment and emphasises the importance of keeping accurate records and tracking learner achievement.

Importantly, the framework identifies assessment data as a basis for monitoring learner progress and making informed decisions about selection and placement into educational institutions and programmes.

There are Ghanaian policies that support centralised online cumulative assessment system that would therefore operationalise and strengthen several principles already established in this national framework.

2. National Pre-Tertiary Education Curriculum Framework

Ghana's National Pre-Tertiary Education Curriculum Framework promotes competency-based learning, creativity, critical thinking, communication, collaboration and problem-solving.

It also establishes performance standards and benchmarks to determine whether learners have achieved the competencies required to progress to subsequent levels of education.

This suggests that the assessment system should establish whether learners have attained the required standards rather than simply rank them against one another in a high-stakes examination.

3. Pre-Tertiary Education Act, 2020 (Act 1049)

The Pre-Tertiary Education Act, 2020, provides for free, compulsory and universal basic education. It also places responsibilities on the Ministry of Education and District Assemblies to ensure that the educational environment is accessible to persons with disabilities and children with special educational needs including the gifted children.

These provisions reinforce the importance of designing assessment and placement arrangements that do not create unnecessary barriers to educational participation.

4. National Standardised Testing and the Cohort-Based Assessment Proposal

Interestingly, the government has already announced an intention to introduce a cohort-based learning assessment model. Under the model announced by the Minister in July 2026, learners would be assessed at Primary 2, Primary 4, Primary 6 and JHS 2, with their progress monitored before the BECE.

According to Ghana News Agency, this is an important development. However, the proposal should go further.

Instead of using cohort-based assessment merely as an additional monitoring mechanism before BECE, Ghana should consider developing it into a comprehensive national cumulative assessment and placement system that can eventually replace BECE.

Proposed Alternative:

A Centralised Online Cumulative Assessment System (COCAS), Basic 4–Basic 9

I propose that Ghana introduces a Centralised Online Cumulative Assessment System (COCAS) to replace the BECE as the principal mechanism for determining progression into senior high school.

The system would establish a national digital platform through which learners' academic achievements, competencies and educational progress are recorded and monitored from Basic 4 through Basic 9.

Unlike the current arrangement, where a major national examination determines placement at the end of JHS, COCAS would provide a longitudinal picture of each learner's educational development over six years.

How would the system work?

Proposed six-year assessment pathway

Basic 4 – Entry and baseline assessment

Establish each learner's initial academic profile, foundational literacy, numeracy and learning competencies.

Basic 5 – Progress assessment

Record academic development, classroom performance, assignments and demonstrated competencies.

Basic 6 – Primary completion assessment

Conduct a nationally moderated assessment of foundational learning and readiness for JHS.

Basic 7 – JHS progression assessment

Monitor subject-specific development, critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving.

Basic 8 – Competency assessment

Evaluate academic progress, practical skills, projects, collaboration and independent learning.

Basic 9 – Final cumulative assessment and SHS placement

Generate a comprehensive learner achievement profile to guide progression and placement into SHS or TVET institutions.

Proposed outcome

A national learner achievement profile replacing dependence on a single terminal examination.

Key Features of the Proposed System

For COCAS to be credible, transparent and nationally accepted, I recommend the following features:

1. A unique digital learner identification number

Every learner in public and private schools should have a unique national education identification number. This would allow the Ministry of Education and GES to track learners' educational progress, even when they transfer between schools.

2. Centralised digital assessment records

Each learner should have a secure digital record containing academic results, continuous assessment scores, projects, practical activities and demonstrated competencies. Teachers would update records periodically through an approved national platform.

3. Nationally standardised assessment benchmarks

NaCCA should establish clear learning standards and performance benchmarks for every grade from Basic 4 to Basic 9. This would ensure that assessments conducted by different schools reflect nationally agreed expectations.

4. Independent moderation and quality assurance

To prevent manipulation of continuous assessment results, the system should incorporate independent verification, moderation and periodic national assessment exercises. Schools should not have unrestricted authority to determine their learners' final cumulative scores.

5. Inclusive assessment arrangements

The platform must accommodate learners with disabilities, including children with mobility, visual, hearing, intellectual impairments and the gifted/talented children. Reasonable accommodations, accessible digital interfaces and alternative assessment formats must be available.

6. SHS placement based on comprehensive learner profiles

SHS placement should consider cumulative academic achievement, demonstrated competencies, learner interests and programme requirements. The system should support appropriate placement into general secondary, technical and vocational pathways.

An important distinction is that centralisation should refer to the management, verification and storage of assessment records. It should not mean that every child must have access to a computer or internet connection to complete every assessment. Schools without adequate digital infrastructure should have secure offline assessment options with subsequent synchronisation.

Why Ghana Should Move Away from BECE

There are several compelling reasons to reconsider the continued dependence on BECE.

1. Reducing examination pressure, unhealthy competition and malpractices

High-stakes examinations can create excessive pressure on learners, parents, teachers and school administrators. They can also encourage schools to concentrate on examination preparation rather than the broader objectives of education.

A cumulative assessment system would encourage schools to focus on sustained learning and development rather than performance on one examination. This is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 4 which encourages lifelong learning.

2. Promoting inclusive education

This is particularly important for children with disabilities and gifted/talented.

Drawing on Nseibo (2021), concerns have been raised about how examination-driven competition can influence mainstream school head teachers' admission decisions, particularly where children with disabilties are perceived as potential threats to school examination performance.

When schools become preoccupied with examination rankings and institutional reputation, children who require additional educational support may be unfairly disadvantaged.

Replacing BECE with a comprehensive assessment system could help reduce these institutional pressures and encourage schools to recognise the individual abilities and achievements of every learner.

However, assessment reform must be accompanied by stronger enforcement of inclusive admission policies, teacher preparation and adequate school resources.

3. Recognising different learning abilities and giftedness/talents

Not all children demonstrate their abilities through written examinations. Some learners excel in practical activities, creativity, communication, innovation, problem-solving and technical skills.

A cumulative assessment system would provide opportunities to recognise these different competencies.

4. Encouraging teachers to teach rather than simply prepare candidates for examinations

The current examination-oriented culture can narrow teaching and learning to what is likely to appear in the final examination.

A continuous assessment model would encourage teachers to monitor learning, identify difficulties early and provide appropriate interventions throughout the educational journey.

5. Generating reliable national education data

A centralised assessment platform would provide the Ministry of Education with valuable information about learning outcomes, regional inequalities, school performance and learners requiring additional support.

Such information could guide educational planning, resource allocation, teacher development and curriculum improvement.

Support from Ghanaian Education Research

The call to reconsider BECE is not without support from Ghanaian education researchers and practitioners.

In June 2025, Graphic Online reported calls by former GES Director-General Professor Kwasi Opoku-Amankwa and Institute for Education Studies Executive Director Dr Peter Anti Partey for a review of BECE to align it with Ghana's standards-based curriculum.

Their concern was that the examination's traditional assessment approach was not adequately aligned with the competency-based expectations of the new curriculum. WAEC, however, defended the examination's continuing relevance while acknowledging opportunities to improve its assessment and placement arrangements.

This debate demonstrates that the question of BECE's relevance is already receiving attention within Ghana's education community.

NaCCA's 2023 clarification also maintained that BECE served as a placement examination and that its mode could be varied. This distinction is important: the placement function does not necessarily have to depend on a single terminal examination.

Recommendations to the Government of Ghana

I therefore call on the Ministry of Education, GES, NaCCA and other relevant stakeholders to consider the following:

1. Establish a national technical committee to examine the feasibility of replacing BECE with a centralised online cumulative assessment system.

2. Build on the government's proposed cohort-based assessment model and extend it into a comprehensive Basic 4–Basic 9 learner tracking and assessment framework.

3. Introduce a unique national learner identification system covering all public and private basic schools.

4. Pilot COCAS in selected districts across Ghana, ensuring representation of rural, urban, public, private and inclusive schools.

5. Develop national assessment benchmarks, moderation mechanisms and transparent procedures for SHS placement.

6. Ensure that the proposed system does not disadvantage children from rural communities, low-income households or children with disabilities.

7. Conduct an independent evaluation of the pilot before implementing a nationwide transition from BECE.

8. Engage WAEC, NaCCA, teacher unions, universities, parents, disability organisations and school leaders in developing the new assessment framework.

Conclusion: Ghana Must Move from Examination-Based Progression to Evidence-Based Educational Development

The current debate about banning early BECE candidates should be an opportunity for a more fundamental national conversation about the future of assessment in Ghana.

Preventing children from writing BECE before JHS 3 may address an administrative concern, but it does not necessarily improve the quality of assessment or address the limitations of relying on a single examination for educational progression.

Ghana has already invested in a standards-based curriculum, a National Pre-Tertiary Learning Assessment Framework and national standardised testing. The next logical step is to bring these initiatives together into a comprehensive assessment and learner-tracking system.

I therefore advocate for a gradual transition from BECE to a Centralised Online Cumulative Assessment System covering Basic 4 to Basic 9.

The purpose of education should not be to prepare children to pass one examination. It should be to support every child to develop knowledge, skills, competencies, creativity and the confidence to contribute meaningfully to society.

Ghana must move beyond the culture of examination competition and embrace an assessment system that recognises learning as a continuous process.

Let us assess learners' educational journeys, not just their performance on one examination. It is time to rethink BECE and make inclusive, competency-based and continuous assessment the foundation of progression into senior high school.

Ghana News.title: Airport confrontation: Gumah accuses Ablakwa of damaging his reputation by linking him to a 2021 shooting
Ghana News.content:
A member of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Prince-Kamal Gumah, who confronted Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa at an airport in the United States, has accused the Minister of linking him to a 2021 shooting incident in Parliament, an allegation he says damaged his reputation.

Mr Gumah claims the Minister displayed his photograph and accused him of involvement in the incident despite what he insists was no evidence establishing his involvement.

In a Facebook statement on Thursday, November 26, he said his lawyers subsequently wrote to Mr Ablakwa, providing documents including his flight ticket and photographs which he claimed showed he was at a campaign ground in Bantama in the Ashanti Region when the shooting occurred.

He alleged that the Minister refused to retract the accusation or offer an explanation despite the representations.

"Despite these representations, he refused to retract the allegation or offer the clarification I believed was necessary. The damage to my reputation had already been done. My face had been presented to the world in connection with a serious criminal accusation," he wrote.

"I have not forgotten that experience," he added.

The allegations against Mr Ablakwa have not been independently verified by MyJoyOnline. Mr Gumah did not provide copies of the parliamentary record or correspondence from his lawyers in his statement.

This is only the beginning

Mr Gumah's comments follow his admission that he was the man who approached Mr Ablakwa at an airport in Washington, United States, and questioned him over the GH¢16 million donated by businessman Ibrahim Mahama's Engineers and Planners towards Ghana's evacuation exercise in South Africa.

During the encounter, he demanded an account of the money and asked when Ghanaians would get it back.

Mr Ablakwa responded: "Your money is intact, your money is safe, we have accounted for it."

Mr Gumah, however, maintained that more explanations were required, declaring that the confrontation was only the beginning of his campaign for accountability.

Read Also: ‘This is just the tip of the iceberg’ – NPP’s Gumah declares after Ablakwa airport confrontation

"We will continue to ask questions. We will demand explanations. We will challenge public officials wherever necessary, through lawful, peaceful and democratic means. We will not allow political power to become a shield against public scrutiny," he said.

He added: "THIS IS JUST THE TIP OF THE ICEBERG. More to come."

Mr Gumah also referenced comments by NDC officials Malik Basintale and Mustapha Gbande concerning former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia's religious identity and ability to recite Surah Al-Fatiha.

He questioned the use of religious identity in political exchanges and cited previous confrontations involving Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko and Citi News journalist Sammens in Manhattan around 2017/2018.

He insisted that his actions were not motivated by a political vendetta but by a desire for transparency and accountability.

Evacuation expenditure under scrutiny

The confrontation centres on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa between May 27 and September 4, 2026, following renewed xenophobic attacks.

The exercise cost GH¢49.72 million, comprising GH¢33.72 million from government and a GH¢16 million donation from Engineers and Planners.

The Minority in Parliament has questioned aspects of the expenditure, including discrepancies in supporting documents and beneficiary payment records, and called for further scrutiny.

The Office of the Special Prosecutor announced on November 9 that it was examining allegations of corruption and corruption-related offences arising from the exercise, including discrepancies in payment records and inadequate supporting documentation.

Mr Ablakwa has denied financial wrongdoing, insisting that not a cedi is missing.

Ablakwa urges restraint

In a separate Facebook post on Thursday, Mr Ablakwa thanked Ghanaians at home and abroad for their support following the airport incident.

"When they get nasty, we must demonstrate we are different by exhibiting more grace, composure, compassion, integrity and respect for each other," he wrote.

The Minister expressed confidence that the independent institutions examining the evacuation expenditure would vindicate him.

"I am absolutely confident that the independent institutions looking into these matters shall vindicate me," he said, adding: "If God be for us, who can be against us."

He also announced that consular approval had been granted to several Ghanaian diplomatic missions to settle the medical bills of hospitalised Ghanaian domestic workers, facilitate their discharge and arrange their return home as the government prepares to introduce defined bans and restrictions.

Mr Ablakwa credited President John Dramani Mahama's leadership and support for the government's foreign policy achievements.

Meanwhile, Mr Gumah maintained that public officials must remain accountable to citizens, insisting: "Ghana belongs to all of us, and no public official is above accountability."

Ghana News.title: 35 officers assaulted, six killed in attacks by illegal loggers and miners in 5 years – Forestry Commission
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Wildlife Division of the Forestry Commission says at least 35 forestry personnel protecting the country’s forest reserves and wildlife have been physically abused in the last five years.

Dr Joseph Boakye disclosed that a significant number of these officers are now living with bullet pellets in their bodies after confrontations with illegal loggers and miners.

Meanwhile, six persons have lost their lives through attacks by the illegal operators, raising alarm over the safety of an institution mandated to protect the country’s forest resources.

In the last ten months, the country has witnessed a series of attacks and killings of some personnel of the Forestry Commission protecting forest reserves and wildlife.

59-year-old Senior Ranger with the Kakum Conservation Area, Nana Richard Otwey, was fatally shot by a suspected poacher during an anti-poaching patrol on August 22, 2026.

The incident adds to the official figures from the Forestry Service Division, which indicate that about 35 staff of the Commission have suffered various degrees of assault in the last five years.

In July this year, an irate mob assaulted officers, vandalised and set ablaze a newly built accommodation facility at a Forestry Commission timber checkpoint in the Bono East region.

These assaults were primarily instigated by illegal miners and chainsaw operators.

Speaking at the AGM of the Ghana Institute of Foresters (GIF), Dr Joseph Boakye bemoaned the threats and harm many foresters face in the wake of the assaults.

“There are some officers who go around their duties with bullet pellets in their bodies. This year alone, apart from the first one that happened in March, another officer was shot in the Tumu area there. The bullet pellets are still in his body. We had to move him to Tamale Teaching Hospital for an emergency operation. Some of the pellets were removed. Others are still there,” he recounted.

This year alone, the GIF has lost two colleagues, Raphael Ganyo and Richard Otwey, while protecting the forests.

Dr Boakye claims that these attacks are financially motivated and supported by powerful interest groups.

“We must honour their sacrifice by ensuring that their deaths lead to meaningful reforms in the protection of forestry personnel and enforcement of our laws,” he said.

He noted that the country must not treat these attacks as mere occupational safety concerns but as a threat to national security, environmental protection, and governance.

“Protecting forestry personnel is not merely an occupational safety concern. It is a national security, environmental governance, and sustainable development imperative. Our forests, wildlife, and other natural resources are national assets,” he said.

The 29th Annual General Meeting of the GIF focused on the theme: “Protecting Forestry Personnel and Resources through stakeholder collaboration and law enforcement”.

Elaborating on the theme, President of the group, Dr Abukari Nantogmah Attah, said the laxity of law enforcement is fuelling the increasing trend of violent attacks.

“If we have the mandate to protect the forest and someone who doesn’t have that mandate tells us not to get into the forest and nothing happens to them, that’s serious. People must face prosecution,” he said.

He said that although the commission's board has recommended enhanced, sophisticated weaponry for foresters, it is not enough to protect them, and he called for stricter law enforcement.

Beyond these attacks, the country’s forest resources, national parks, and other

protected areas continue to face serious threats from illegal logging, mining, agricultural expansion, wildlife trafficking, and other destructive activities.

The consequences of these threats extend far beyond the Commission, undermining biodiversity conservation, threatening water security, compromising climate resilience, affecting rural livelihoods, and weakening Ghana's commitment under international environmental agreements.

The foresters recommend that the government decouple the fight against illegal logging and mining from politicisation and take a pragmatic approach to fight the canker.

Ghana News.title: ‘Your record stinks’: Agalga fires at NPP over cocaine trade
Ghana News.content:
Majority Leader James Agalga has reignited the political controversy over cocaine trafficking in Ghana, accusing the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration of weakening port surveillance by excluding the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) from routine joint inspections.

He made the accusation in Parliament on Thursday, November 26, as he pushed back against the Minority’s criticism of the government over recent cocaine seizures and investigations involving Ghana.

Mr Agalga argued that the decision to remove NACOC from the routine inspection arrangement at the country’s ports created gaps that could be exploited by drug trafficking networks.

“It is the same NPP that dislodged the Narcotics Control Commission from our ports. Why did you dislodge them from the ports of entry? You dislodged them because you wanted to create a conducive atmosphere for cocaine to be smuggled into this country,” he alleged.

He warned the Minority against turning the cocaine issue into a political contest with the governing side, insisting that the NPP had little moral authority to accuse the current administration of the narcotics trade.

“I have always cautioned them; don’t attempt to engage us in any debate on cocaine because your record stinks,” he said.

The dispute centres partly on a 2018 decision by the Akufo-Addo administration to reduce the number of agencies conducting routine joint inspections at the ports from 16 to three.

A fact-check by GhanaFact established that the Ghana Standards Authority, Food and Drugs Authority and Customs were retained for the routine inspections, while NACOC and National Security were expected to participate when intelligence warranted it.

The arrangement has since become a major point of contention following the seizure in France of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a container of plastic waste shipped from Ghana.

The NPP has rejected claims that NACOC was completely removed from the ports. Assin South MP and former Interior Committee Ranking Member, Reverend John Ntim Fordjour, has argued that the 2018 reforms were intended to reduce delays and demurrage costs, not to prevent the Commission from carrying out its mandate.

The controversy has intensified following the September 10 seizure at the French port of Dunkirk. The cocaine, concealed in a container that arrived from Ghana, was estimated to have a street value of about €225 million, with part of the consignment reportedly destined for Antwerp, Belgium.

The case has triggered investigations and prosecutions in Ghana, with several people facing charges linked to the alleged exportation of the drugs.

NACOC has said its investigations are aimed at dismantling the network behind the shipment, while the proceedings against the accused persons are continuing.

A separate international investigation has also placed Ghana under scrutiny following the interception of a cocaine consignment at Beirut’s Rafic Hariri International Airport in Lebanon.

A Syrian national travelling from Accra was arrested on October 31 after 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine were discovered in his luggage. NACOC subsequently arrested three foreign nationals - a Syrian, a Tunisian and a Lebanese - in Ghana on November 3 as part of investigations into the suspected trafficking operation.

The latest cases have also raised questions about the conduct of investigations and the rights of people arrested in connection with suspected drug trafficking.

Ghana News.title: VIDEO: Mahama arrives in Barbados to deepen Ghana-Caribbean ties
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has arrived in Barbados for a five-day state visit aimed at strengthening Ghana’s historical, diplomatic and economic relations with the Caribbean nation.

The President arrived at the Grantley Adams International Airport this evening, Thursday, November 26, to begin engagements expected to deepen cooperation between the two countries and reinforce Ghana’s relationship with the wider African diaspora.

The visit comes at a significant moment for Barbados, which is preparing to mark 60 years of independence on November 30, and offers both countries an opportunity to translate their shared history into stronger diplomatic and economic partnerships.

A statement issued by the Presidency said the visit would recognise the historical connections between Ghana and Barbados, particularly their shared experience of the transatlantic slave trade, while celebrating the resilience and achievements of their peoples.

A major feature of the President’s programme will be meetings with Barbadian leaders, including President Jeffrey Davidson Bostic and Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley, to discuss areas of mutual interest and opportunities for closer cooperation.

Mr Mahama is also scheduled to address a joint session of the Barbadian Parliament tomorrow, Friday, November 27, in an engagement expected to focus on the historical bonds between Africa and the Caribbean and the prospects for stronger relations.

The programme will further take him to Speightstown for a twinning ceremony between the Barbadian town and Cape Coast in Ghana. The event will include the unveiling of a bust of King Cuffie, an enslaved African associated with a planned uprising against the colonial plantation system in Barbados in 1675.

The ceremony is expected to formalise closer cultural and historical engagement between the two coastal communities through a bilateral agreement.

Another significant engagement will be the opening of the Ancestral Memorial to the Enslaved at Newton, Christ Church, on Saturday, November 28. The memorial will honour Africans who were forcibly transported across the Atlantic and subjected to slavery in the Caribbean.

Mr Mahama is also expected to participate in cultural activities, including a tree-planting ceremony at the Botanical Gardens and a President’s Ball celebrating Barbadian heritage.

The visit will culminate in his participation in Barbados’ 60th Independence Anniversary parade on Monday, November 30, where he is expected to deliver a toast to the people of the country.

The trip follows the president's recent visit to Jamaica and forms part of his broader push to strengthen Ghana’s engagement with Caribbean countries and people of African descent across the world.

It also comes ahead of Ghana’s expected assumption of the African Union chairmanship in 2027, a responsibility the Presidency says Mr Mahama intends to use to advance stronger cooperation between Africa and the Caribbean, particularly in trade, investment and diplomacy.

The two regions share deep historical connections arising from the forced movement of Africans during the transatlantic slave trade. Ghana’s engagement with the Caribbean has increasingly included discussions on reparatory justice, cultural heritage and the need to build practical economic partnerships.

In June 2026, Ghana hosted a three-day Africa-Caribbean consultative conference in Accra, co-chaired by Mr Mahama and Prime Minister Mottley, which produced an outcome document setting out steps towards a coordinated approach to reparatory justice.

The Barbados visit is expected to build on those engagements and give fresh impetus to efforts to turn the historic relationship between the two regions into sustained cooperation.

Ghana News.title: Music is art, not a competition – Sarkodie
Ghana News.content:
Rap artiste, Sarkodie, has urged musicians to return to the essence of music as art, warning that the rush for instant chart success is killing authentic creativity.

In a statement shared on X, Sarkodie said some songs took him years to fully appreciate, yet the industry has normalised instant gratification.

“Let’s get back to the essence of what music is. It’s art, not a competition. Some songs took me years to fully appreciate, yet we’ve normalised instant gratification, and that’s killing authentic creativity,” he wrote.

“Don’t be in a rush to get your songs to number one at the expense of what they were truly meant to be. Create, express, and let the art breathe. Give it time.”

Sarkodie’s call adds to a growing chorus of Ghanaian musicians who have in recent times advocated collaboration and unity over rivalry and competition.

It will be recalled that Dancehall and Afrobeats star, Stonebwoy, has also rejected the idea of music as competition, particularly in the ongoing debate over Ghana’s supposed “Top 3” artistes.

Speaking in a recent interview, Stonebwoy described the “Top 3” label as a media-created description, insisting that Ghana’s musical success is the result of contributions from several artistes across different generations.

“My understanding of music is collaboration. Music is not a competitive sport. My understanding of it is that, in its making, instruments must come together,” he stated.

“That isolative mentality with music does not exist, but rather it is a collective, harmonious thing,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Graphic MD Ato Afful bows out after 8 years
Ghana News.content:
Ato Afful will officially end his eight-year, two-term tenure as Managing Director (MD) of Graphic Communications Group Ltd (GCGL) on December 5, 2026.

Speaking at his send-off ceremony in Accra, Mr Afful expressed profound gratitude for the opportunity to lead the iconic national brand.

"I am proud and privileged to be entrusted with such an iconic national character brand by the NMC, Board members, the teams and partner clients and stakeholders we collaborated with, and what little we could achieve every day," he said.

Reflecting on his leadership, he noted that steering GCGL through a rapidly evolving and fragmenting media landscape had been a career highlight.

"Leading GCGL has been one of the great privileges of my career. We have led and collaborated with an exceptional team and partner clients and audience members across our print and digital channels. I am proud of what we have been able to accomplish together," he stated.

"I leave confident that GCGL is well placed for the future in an engaging economy that is rapidly evolving, as it is fragmenting."

The outgoing Managing Director extended his appreciation to the staff, editors, and regional teams whose dedication made his mandate successful. He also acknowledged the continued trust of the company's clients and stakeholders.

"But our real responsibility is what comes next: to keep earning that trust and to keep raising the standard of the work and the impact we create together with the brand teams and stakeholders we work with," he added.

As he prepares to hand over the reins, Mr Afful offered a piece of advice to his successor.

"To my successor, I would humbly ask that after getting what you prayed for, pray for discipline to keep it, and wisdom to multiply it," he said, concluding his remarks with the Irish proverb, "May the road rise to meet you."

Below is his full speech;

End of Tenure at GCGL

On 05/12/2026, I will be ending my eight-year, two-term tenure as Managing Director of Graphic Communications Group Ltd, Ghana's foremost state-owned print, digital media and commercial press company.

I am proud and privileged to be entrusted with such an iconic national character brand by the NMC, Board members, the teams and partner clients and stakeholders we collaborated with, and what little we could achieve every day.

Leading GCGL has been one of the great privileges of my career. We have led and collaborated with an exceptional team and partner clients and audience members across our print and digital channels. I am proud of what we have been able to accomplish together. I leave confident that GCGL is well placed for the future in an engaging economy that is rapidly evolving, as it is fragmenting.

Thank you for the opportunity, and my gratitude to the teams at the head office, and across the regions, the editors and staff who enabled me to make this mandate work, as was done for the MD’s who preceded me.

To our clients who continue to place their trust in us, and to the diverse teams across GCGL who bring their talent, care and ambition to that trust every day. Thank you.

But our real responsibility is what comes next: to keep earning that trust and to keep raising the standard of the work and the impact we create together with the brand teams and stakeholders we work with.

It has been an honour to lead and collaborate with such a dynamic and resilient team.

To my successor, I would humbly ask that after getting what you prayed for, pray for discipline to keep it, and wisdom to multiply it.

May the road rise to meet you. (Irish Proverb)

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
