World.title: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
World.content:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has capsized off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

Elena Delgado, maritime captain of Valencia, told news agency AFP that a small slick that had formed around the boat had "disappeared".

"The situation is stabilised," she said, adding that further inspections would be carried out on Friday morning.

Earlier, regional emergencies director Pablo GÃ¡rriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, as had originally been reported. The vessel remains partially submerged.

The Med Emre capsized 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

World.title: Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape of actress in 2018, court rules
World.content:
French film actor GÃ©rard Depardieu is to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court has confirmed.

Arnould, who was 22 at the time, had reported the alleged rape several days after going to his house in Paris to rehearse a play.

She has waived her right to anonymity and her lawyer said Thursday's ruling was a "first" and the forthcoming trial would be historic.

Depardieu, 77, had contested his indictment on two counts of rape. In a letter published in Le Figaro in 2023, Depardieu strongly denied Arnould's allegations, saying "there was never any coercion or violence between us".

Depardieu was for decades a leading figure in French and international cinema for roles in Green Card, The Man in the Iron Mask and the Asterix films. He was awarded France's LÃ©gion d'honneur in 1996.

But in recent years a series of allegations have been made against him over his conduct on film sets and elsewhere in the wake of France's #MeToo movement, known as balance ton porc (call out your pig).

Last year, he was given an 18-month suspended jail term after he was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in Paris in May. He was also placed on the sex offenders register and ordered to pay compensation.

He dropped his appeal against the ruling last week and offered "sincere apologies" for his behaviour on the set of director Jean Becker's 2021 film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters).

Depardieu had been a friend of Charlotte Arnould's father and on 7 August 2018 she had gone to his home, where much of what happened was captured on the actor's own CCTV.

Arnould's case was initially dismissed for insufficient evidence, but after she filed a civil complaint, a judicial investigation was opened in the summer of 2020.

Speaking outside the Paris appeal court on Thursday, her lawyer Carine Durrieu Diebolt said the ruling was a victory for her client for whom it was "genuinely a relief".

The appeal court said that while Depardieu should stand trial for what took place on that day, he would not be tried for a further alleged rape at a hotel six days later.

Depardieu's lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski told reporters that court had partly ruled in his favour: "As soon as we get the ruling, we will look into the possibility of appealing to the Court of Cassation."

Meanwhile, Depardieu is under a separate investigation alongside French author Michel Houellebecq for "allegations of a sexual nature".

French authorities confirmed their inquiry last week, following reports of an alleged "gang rape" on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line.

World.title: Pregnant US inmate escapes in prison vehicle after medical appointment
World.content:
A pregnant inmate has escaped from custody in the US state of New Mexico, after taking control of a police vehicle while returning to prison from a prenatal appointment, the state's corrections department has said.

Rebecca Taylor, 26, took control of the Dodge Journey and drove away when the team transporting her and another inmate stopped to pick up food in Albuquerque, local media reported.

The New Mexico Corrections Department said that the vehicle and her prison jumpsuit were later recovered, but Taylor remains on the run.

She had been imprisoned for multiple theft and burglary charges, the department said in a Facebook statement.

Local media reported that another inmate, also travelling back from a prenatal appointment, was able to get out of the car as Taylor took control on Wednesday morning.

The corrections department has said that a multi-agency search for Taylor is under way. The BBC has approached it for an update.

The Albuquerque Journal reported that Taylor is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy. For this reason, she was not restrained during transportation, department spokesperson Brittany Roembach said.

"It is the understanding right now that one officer was with the vehicle but not inside of the vehicle when this occurred," she was quoted as saying.

All prisons in New Mexico went into lockdown following Taylor's escape, but it was lifted at 06:00 on Thursday.

However the prison where she was being held, the Western New Mexico Corrections Facility, will remain on "modified movement", and no visitors are currently allowed.

The public has been told not to approach Rebecca Taylor if they see her, and call police straight away.

World.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
World.content:
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.

Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".

Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.

It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.

Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.

The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.

On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.

Earlier, the country's armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi said "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by Iran.

Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.

Italy's foreign minister was quoted by Italian media as saying that investigations showed that the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.

The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.

Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.

"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.

"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

World.title: Egyptian authorities arrest motorist over tanker crash that killed 31
World.content:
Egyptian authorities have arrested a man accused of causing a tanker crash and massive fire that killed 31 people on a busy Cairo highway.

The public prosecutor's office said the motorist had confessed to driving at 110km/h (68mph) along a section of ring road, to the north of the old city centre, and clipping the tanker with the side of his car as he changed lanes.

Sources close to the investigation were earlier quoted by state media as saying a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the fuel truck, causing the driver to lose control.

Twenty-one others were injured in the crash in the Warraq neighbourhood on Wednesday evening, with hospitals treating patients for burns and smoke inhalation.

The public prosecutor's office said on Thursday that "upon questioning the suspect and confronting him with the findings of the investigation... he confessed to committing the act".

"He added that, while moving between traffic lanes and overtaking vehicles, the left side of his car collided with the right rear side of the tanker. This caused him to lose control of the steering wheel and his car veered to the far right of the road."

At the same time, one of the fuel tanker's tyres burst, causing it to veer into the highway's central reservation, hit the concrete barrier and overturn, spilling fuel and igniting a fire, the prosecutor's office said.

Egyptian authorities have not named the suspect accused of causing the fatal crash, but they said he had been travelling with his father at the time.

World.title: Temple, BOS Africa spotlight Nigeria’s sports business potential at Lagos event
World.content:
Sports industry executives, entrepreneurs and professionals have called for better funding, infrastructure, stronger partnerships and improved organisation to unlock Nigeria’s sporting potential and build a sustainable sports economy.

The call was made at KINETIC, an executive sports business mixer organised by the Business of Sports Institute (BOS) Africa in partnership with The Temple Company, in Lagos on Wednesday.

The event brought together professionals from different sectors of the sports industry, including finance, law, media, engineering, sports management, marketing, broadcasting and technology, for discussions on investment opportunities, collaboration and the commercial development of sports in Nigeria.

The gathering, held at The Temple Company, Victoria Island, was designed to encourage networking and connect people whose businesses and expertise could contribute to the sports industry’s growth.

Speaking at the event, Beverley Agbakoba-Onyejianya, founder and academic director of BOS Africa, said Nigeria’s sporting potential remained largely untapped because of gaps in capacity, funding, infrastructure, and a lack of sufficient opportunities for collaboration.

She said the country has the talent and enthusiasm for sports but has yet to develop an industry that can generate adequate employment and sustainable commercial opportunities for professionals across the value chain.

“We are a sporting nation, and we are a vibrant nation. We’re a footballing nation, actually. But we still don’t provide enough jobs. It’s just not a sustainable industry as it ought to be when you compare it to, say, England, France,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mrs Agbakoba-Onyejianya, however, said Nigeria should develop its sports industry in a manner that reflects its culture, identity and peculiar circumstances rather than merely attempting to replicate Western models.

She said KINETIC was conceived to bring professionals from different sectors together to encourage meaningful conversations, strengthen relationships and explore opportunities for collaboration.

“We want finance to talk to the agents. We want the agents to talk to the telecoms people. We want us all to communicate more so we can do more in this industry,” she said.

Sports business education

Mrs Agbakoba-Onyejianya said her motivation for establishing BOS Africa was the shortage of accessible and quality sports business education in Nigeria, particularly programmes that prepare people for commercially driven careers in the industry.

She said while some universities offer sports-related programmes, the country still lacks sufficient specialised training opportunities to meet the demands of its growing sporting ecosystem.

The initiative, she said, was intended to provide a flexible, accessible and affordable platform for people seeking to develop careers in sports business.

Mrs Agbakoba-Onyejianya, a sports lawyer with more than two decades of professional experience spanning Nigeria and the United Kingdom, founded Lagos Tigers Football Club, a grassroots football academy, and contributed to the development of Nigeria’s National Sports Policy.

She is also a FIFA mediator and serves on international sports dispute-resolution and governance panels.

She said the mixer showed the value of bringing professionals together outside their usual business environments, and expressed hope that the initiative would grow into a regular platform for industry engagement.

“Imagine having this platform on a massive scale, where media, finance, broadcasting, engineering, legal and other sectors come together, connected by sports. That way, we grow the economy, contribute to the GDP, do more projects through collaboration and literally create a domino effect,” she said.

Nigeria’s sporting potential

During a panel discussion moderated by Telema Davies, managing partner of DMPartners, participants expressed differing views on whether Nigeria could be regarded as a serious sporting nation, despite its abundance of talent.

Aderoju Ope-Ajayi, chairperson of the Lagos State Aquatic Association and head of strategy and business transformation at MTN MoMo PSB, questioned Nigeria’s commitment to developing its athletes, pointing to the country’s inability to consistently identify, nurture and adequately represent promising talents.

She said she was often amazed by the level of talent available, particularly among young athletes who break national records but do not receive the support needed to progress to international competitions.

“Nigeria is not a serious sporting nation. We have so much potential, but we are just not doing enough”, she said.

Ms Ope-Ajayi also highlighted the challenges of accessing sporting facilities, noting that the shortage of suitable infrastructure had forced some organisers and development programmes to depend on privately owned schools and other facilities.

She said sponsorship was also difficult to secure, with some companies supporting sporting initiatives out of goodwill rather than through clearly defined long-term commercial objectives.

Folake Shasanya, managing partner of Aesura Group, a strategic capital advisory firm, agreed that Nigeria’s sporting potential was undermined by inadequate structures.

She said young athletes often demonstrate exceptional ability but lack the systems needed to sustain their development and translate their performances into success at major international competitions.

Ms Shasanya cited Nigeria’s recent achievements at the Youth Olympic Games as evidence of the country’s potential, arguing that greater attention to athlete development, organisation and investment could help produce more consistent performances across sporting disciplines.

Jouko Gorissen, founder of Next Level Global Recruiting, said Nigeria could be described as a sporting nation in terms of its population, talent and enthusiasm but has yet to establish the structures needed to make sports a sustainable business.

He said countries such as the United States had developed stronger sports systems through investments in facilities, coaching, education, safeguarding and commercial opportunities.

Mr Gorissen said Nigeria’s sports industry remained overly dependent on athletes as its principal commercial assets, a model he described as unsustainable in the long term.

He argued that the country needed to develop the professionals, institutions and businesses that support athletes and sporting competitions, rather than focusing almost exclusively on the players.

Infrastructure, investment and commercial opportunities

Opeyemi Babalola, an engineer who also serves as founder and managing director of Webber Engineering, said Nigeria had the talent to compete internationally but was held back by politics, inadequate infrastructure, and poor management of sporting facilities.

He said government ownership of many facilities created challenges for commercial operators, particularly when political activities or other government priorities affected access.

The discussion also examined the commercial potential of sporting facilities, including opportunities for private investment, improved management and alternative revenue streams.

Mr Babalola argued that naming rights, a common commercial arrangement in international sports, could provide additional revenue for facilities, but said Nigeria sometimes missed such opportunities by prioritising commemorative naming conventions.

He suggested that sports infrastructure could be better positioned to attract commercial investment through naming rights and other sponsorship arrangements, while still recognising national figures and sporting heroes.

Seun Akinbolu, founder and co-founder of The Athletics School Games and Pan-Africa School Games, also highlighted funding and infrastructure challenges facing sports development.

She said establishing individual facilities could be expensive and difficult to sustain, suggesting partnerships as a more viable route for organisations seeking to expand sporting opportunities.

The concerns raised at KINETIC mirror wider challenges identified in Nigeria’s sports development plans, including inadequate investment, infrastructure deficits and the need for greater private-sector participation.

Nigeria’s National Development Plan has identified limited funding, uneven access to facilities and poor infrastructure as constraints to the sector’s growth, while emphasising the need for public-private partnerships to unlock its economic potential.

The federal government has also been exploring alternative financing models for sports infrastructure, including plans announced in October by the National Sports Commission to mobilise a N1 trillion fund to rehabilitate facilities and attract private investment.

Terfa Tilley-Gyado, President & CEO, The Temple Company & Ogidi Studios, said the partnership with BOS Africa was driven by the belief that African sports needed more than talent and passion to thrive.

He said the continent’s athletes were increasingly competing worldwide but remained underrepresented by African professionals in areas such as management, agency, sports nutrition, law, and other specialist services.

He said KINETIC was an attempt to begin building the relationships and professional networks necessary to address the gap.

“This is just the first, as Amaka said. And there will be many more,” he said, encouraging participants to explore BOS Africa’s training programmes and opportunities to develop their expertise in the sports industry.

The organisers said KINETIC was expected to become a recurring gathering, providing a platform for professionals to connect, exchange ideas and develop partnerships capable of strengthening Africa’s sports business ecosystem.

World.title: How ISWAP uses drones, satellite technology to sustain insurgency in Lake Chad – Report
World.content:
Nearly two decades after the Boko Haram insurgency began in Nigeria, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) has transformed into a resilient, tech-enabled organisation driven by an adaptive ecosystem of commercial drones, satellite communications, and localised weapons fabrication.

That is the core finding of a major new research report published today by the Institute for Security Studies (ISS), titled “Wiring the insurgency: Inside ISWAP’s adaptive technology programme.”

Drawing on interviews with ex-Boko Haram fighters, who recently defected and security insiders, the report, launched in Abuja on Thursday, reveals how the insurgent group has systematically modified ordinary commercial and digital tools to enhance its intelligence gathering, propaganda operations, and combat capabilities.

Unlike other insurgent groups backed directly by foreign states, ISWAP relies on the broader Islamic State global network for technical guidance and financial backing. Equipment and funds reach the group through transnational supply lines, the report found.

Cash and items such as Starlink and Thuraya satellite communication devices – initially registered in Dubai – are channelled from the United Arab Emirates through currency exchange operators in Kano, Nigeria, and secondary routes in N’Djamena, Chad.

Highlighting the scale of these communications, an ex-fighter noted: “We have our own laptops, and we use Thuraya and Starlink … the number of the Thuraya is uncountable.”

These supplies are smuggled into Lake Chad Basin territories hidden inside bundles of fabrics and food via transit hubs like Geidam, according to the report.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

ISWAP’s manufacturing capacity has evolved from an early, improvised tradition sparked by the 2013 raid on the Government Technical College in Bama, where equipment was looted to build initial workshops, into purpose-built workshops on Lake Chad islands that produce specialised explosives and fit commercial DJI drones with IEDs.

To protect these operations, the group enforces strict operational security measures, including banning local SIM cards across its bases, restricting smartphone use among fighters, and utilising satellite Wi-Fi to bypass government telecom shutdowns.

The report contrasts ISWAP’s structured approach with its rival faction, Jama’tu Ahlis Sunna Lidda’awati wal-Jihad (JAS). While ISWAP maintains a disciplined, professionalised organisation backed by IS central, JAS operates via a comparatively loose structure.

Pointing to the stark organisational gap between the two factions, an ex-fighter dismissively described JAS’s media as “nothing organised.”

Furthermore, while ISWAP focuses heavily on military base attacks to capture weapons through its ghanimah pricing system, which pays fighters for weapons captured from the military and surrendered to the group, JAS relies more heavily on civilian predation and older illicit camel-riding arms corridors running from Sudan.

The research also underscores ISWAP’s sophisticated organisational structure, including the Ilan, a media department that coordinates real-time propaganda and manages back-channel messaging with journalists. At the community level, the group relies on the rijal–awam network, embedding covert agents into civilian populations to gather intelligence, handle logistics, and project parallel governance.

While state militaries and the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) have increasingly deployed counter-drone measures, such as handheld jammers and specialised radar training, the report warns that slow procurement processes and reactive strategies continue to hamper national and regional security responses.

Furthermore, the study cautions that while empirical evidence of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) adoption as operational infrastructure remains unconfirmed, ISWAP’s rapid innovation cycle means counterinsurgency planners must look ahead before AI becomes an active threat.

“This work is an output of our Disrupting Armed Groups’ Operational Governance project, which seeks to draw on primary research to reveal core elements of ISWAP’s enabling ecosystem as evidence to inform understanding and responses by counterinsurgency planners,” said the author Taiwo Adebayo.

The report urges a multi-stakeholder response, recommending that counterinsurgency actors systematically use defector intelligence, strengthen amphibious and naval operations in the Lake Chad Basin, clamp down on transnational currency exchange networks that facilitate illicit financing, and engage satellite communication providers to monitor device diversion in conflict zones.

World.title: NAFDAC raids Abuja market, seizes prohibited goods worth over ₦300 million
World.content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has raided Zuba International Market in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, seizing prohibited alcoholic beverages and other products estimated at over N300 million.

During the operation on Thursday, more than 160 shops were screened by the agency’s enforcement team.

The operation, conducted in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force and operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), forms part of the agency’s efforts to curb the circulation of counterfeit, substandard and unwholesome products, particularly ahead of the festive season.

Speaking with PREMIUM TIMES, the Head of the Investigation and Enforcement Division, North-Central Zone, Babatunji Omoyeni, said the raid followed intelligence reports on the sale and distribution of prohibited sachet alcohol, counterfeit products and unregistered wines in the market.

“We have been on this, I will tell you, for some time. But this morning, with the cooperation of our sister agencies, the Nigerian Police Force, Department of State Security, we got to this area very early in the day,” he said.

Mr Omoyeni said the operation was aimed at safeguarding public health and protecting children from exposure to alcoholic beverages.

He also expressed concerns about the health complications associated with the consumption of counterfeit products, including kidney damage.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Enforcement of sachet alcohol ban

In January, NAFDAC began enforcing a ban on alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and PET bottles below 200 millilitres, following the expiration of a five-year moratorium granted to manufacturers to phase out the products.

Mr Omoyeni maintained that the ban remained in force, adding that the agency would continue to monitor the distribution and sale of prohibited alcoholic beverages.

“For the past five years or more, we have been asking producers to stop producing alcoholic beverages less than 200ml. We will continue to sanitise the system and make sure that the distribution chain is not bastardised with these merchants of nonsense,” he said.

Speaking earlier on Thursday at the 10th Annual Health Conference of the Association of Nigerian Health Journalists (ANHeJ) in Abuja, an official of NAFDAC’s Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, Musa Godiya, disclosed that the agency had commenced the second phase of enforcement of the ban.

Mr Godiya explained that while the first phase focused on manufacturing facilities, the second phase targeted markets, retail outlets and other distribution points to remove prohibited products from circulation.

“We have concluded the first phase of the ban, which involved visiting manufacturing factories. We are now going to markets and streets for a total mop-up and enforcement action on sachet alcohol,” he said.

In August, PREMIUM TIMES reported that NAFDAC directed manufacturers to recall prohibited alcoholic beverages nationwide and destroy them under the agency’s supervision.

The ban is aimed at reducing underage drinking, alcohol abuse and access to highly concentrated alcoholic beverages in small, inexpensive containers.

During Thursday’s raid, Mr Omoyeni said the enforcement team uncovered large quantities of prohibited alcoholic beverages across several warehouses, alongside other consumer products, some of which had expired.

“We got to this warehouse. We have gone into several warehouses, and we have seen different alcoholic beverages below 200ml. You can see this is a warehouse, a story building warehouse. The ground floor here is mind-boggling; I will describe it that way,” he said.

NAFDAC urges vigilance ahead of festive season

The agency also urged Nigerians to exercise caution when purchasing food, drinks and other consumer products during the festive season.

Mr Omoyeni said NAFDAC Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye had directed the enforcement directorate to intensify surveillance and enforcement activities as commercial activities and consumer demand increase.

He encouraged members of the public to report individuals and locations suspected of manufacturing, storing, distributing, and selling counterfeit and unwholesome products.

Mr Omoyeni said individuals found to have violated relevant regulations would be prosecuted after investigations concluded.

He explained that the agency would ensure it gathered sufficient evidence and properly documented it before instituting legal proceedings against suspected offenders.

“Before we make any decision, we conduct investigations and ensure that all the necessary evidence has been gathered. This is to ensure that whenever we appear before a competent court of jurisdiction in Nigeria, we have sufficient facts and evidence to present,” he said.

He also commended the police and DSS for their support during the operation, emphasising the importance of collaboration among enforcement agencies.

World.title: 2027: Why North will vote for Tinubu, By Uba Sani
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has declared that each presidential candidate should campaign based on his past record as the era of making promises is over.

The Governor noted that all the leading presidential candidates have held positions in the past, arguing that they should state what they have done for the north before seeking for its votes.

He advised politicians to avoid campaigning based on sentiments, adding that the north will put all candidates on scale, to determine what they did for the region when they were in power.

Governor Uba Sani gave this advice at a programme organised by Arewa Think Tank, a pro-northern political organisation, which endorsed President Bola Tinubu and Governor Uba Sani’s re-election in 2027.

Speaking at the event, he said that the north has every reason to vote for the president in 2027 because of the development that the region has witnessed in the last three and half years.

The Governor disclosed that the president approved N600 billion for the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway which was abandoned, adding that the road will be completed soon.

He disclosed that the federal government has ‘’embarked on constructing 1,300 km of road projects in the North West, 1,400 km of road in the North East, 1,200 km of roads in the North Central, put together, this is unprecedented in Northern Nigeria.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘’And in the North West, 348 kilometers of roads have been completed. In the North East, almost 400 completed, the highest in the region. And in the North Central, almost 355 kilometres have been completed.

‘’The rest of the roads are near completion or around 60%, 70%, 80% completion. How can anyone tell us not to vote for a man like that?’’, he posed a rhetorical question.

The Governor pointed out that President Tinubu has established the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to make tertiary education more accessible to Nigerians, at a time when some northern elites built private universities.

‘’Today, as we are speaking, I have just looked at the scorecard of NELFUND before coming to this event; 63% of the people that benefited are from northern Nigeria,’’ he said.

According to him, 70% of the beneficiaries of the Technical and Vocational Education Training(TVET) are from the north, adding that the programme is aimed at developing young people with skills-based education.

Governor Uba Sani maintained that ‘’President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has done a lot for us, and we will come out on 16th January 2027 to repay him with our votes in Northern Nigeria.’’

He said that the northern political elite should start developing a blueprint after Tinubu’s re-election, so that it will be implemented when power returns to the region in 2031.

The Governor promised that ‘’no presidential candidate will even have 25% by the grace of God in Kaduna State, apart from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. We are giving Asiwaju 80%, the rest can share the remaining 20%.’’

Justifying why Kaduna State will vote for Tinubu, the Governor said that all that he has achieved in the health, education and agriculture as well as transport sectors, was made possible by the president.

He also listed the ongoing N178 billion Mando to Birnin Gwari and the Zaria, Soba, Pambegua road projects which are being executed by the federal government, as well as the upcoming Kaduna Light Rail Project.

According to the Governor of Kaduna State, the ground breaking of Jema’a to Kwoi road project will be performed next week.

He said that Kaduna State has never had it so good because the Minister of Defence and Minister of Environment are from the state, adding that the Chairman of National Sports Commission, who is also from Kaduna State, occupies a cabinet position.

World.title: Ogun East: Abiodun vows to champion Ijebu-Remo State creation, offer effective representation
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has pledged to make the creation of Ijebu-Remo State a major legislative priority if elected to represent Ogun East Senatorial District in the 16 January 2027 elections, promising to deploy his experience in governance and engage relevant stakeholders to advance the aspiration at the National Assembly.

Abiodun, who made the commitment on Wednesday at the commissioning of his senatorial campaign office in Ijebu-Ode, said the proposed state would be viable, given the area’s rich human resources, economic potential and natural endowments.

He declared that he would take an active leadership role in mobilising support among federal lawmakers and other relevant institutions to advance the constitutional process for the creation of the proposed state.

“By the grace of God, when I get to the Senate, I will be at the vanguard of pursuing the creation of Ijebu-Remo State,” he promised.

The governor explained that state creation requires legislative action and the fulfilment of constitutional requirements, assuring that he would work with other senators, members of the House of Representatives and relevant stakeholders to translate the aspiration into reality.

He commended President Bola Tinubu for embarking on economic reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidy and the floating of the naira, which he said were necessary to reposition the Nigerian economy.

According to him, failure to remove the fuel subsidy would have further weakened the nation’s economy, noting that the subsidy regime was costing the country about N4 billion monthly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

While acknowledging the economic difficulties Nigerians have experienced following the reforms, Abiodun said the Federal Government was taking steps to cushion their effects, particularly on vulnerable citizens.

He cited the Federal Government’s N75,000 monthly support programme for vulnerable Nigerians, disclosing that about 400,000 beneficiaries in Ogun State had benefited from the initiative. He also noted that students in tertiary institutions were benefiting from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).

The governor disclosed that his administration had also introduced a support scheme under which 10 beneficiaries in each polling unit received N15,000, with plans to increase the amount to N45,000. He said about 15,000 people had so far benefited from the programme across Ogun East Senatorial District.

He added that his administration had distributed transformers, solar-powered streetlights, solar-powered boreholes and road graders to support communities and improve rural infrastructure.

Abiodun said his administration had undertaken extensive development projects across the state, including the construction of roads, housing units, medical centres, hospitals, schools and the Gateway International Airport, while preparations were ongoing for the commencement of the Ogun State Deep Sea Port project in Ogun Waterside.

He disclosed that 26 roads had been constructed in Ijebu-Ode, describing the intervention as unprecedented, while noting that his administration had also constructed about three roads in Ogun Waterside, an area he said had not witnessed government road construction for 16 years.

He listed other benefiting areas to include Ijebu North, Ijebu North East, Ijebu East, Odogbolu, Sagamu, Ikenne and Remo North, adding that the proposed Deep Sea Port would further unlock the economic potential of the district.

The governor appreciated the All Progressives Congress (APC) for giving him the opportunity to serve as governor and for providing the platform to contest the Ogun East senatorial seat.

He explained that the newly commissioned campaign office had been equipped to serve as a functional constituency office, not only for his senatorial activities but also as a resource centre for the governor, members of the House of Representatives and the President during visits to the district.

Abiodun assured constituents that the office would provide an accessible channel for communicating their needs, priorities and concerns.

“All the things you want me to do as a senator, all your priorities, you will bring to this office where I can get your needs and complaints and address them timely,” he said.

Expressing confidence in his ability to provide effective representation, the governor said his experience in public administration had prepared him for the responsibilities of the Senate.

“With all sense of modesty, I am tested and proven. By the grace of God, I will provide the required representation that Ogun East deserves. From day one when I resume office, I will hit the ground running, and so help me God,” he assured.

Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council, Senator Lekan Mustapha, commended Abiodun’s efforts towards positioning Ogun State as an oil-producing state, following the discovery of oil in Ogun Waterside and other parts of Ijebuland.

Mustapha noted that the creation of a new state was a constitutional responsibility involving the federal legislature, stressing the importance of having experienced representation at the National Assembly to pursue the aspiration.

Also speaking, Otunba Rotimi Paseda described the governor’s development projects as significant contributions to the state, urging residents of Ogun East to participate in the forthcoming senatorial contest.

The Chairman of the Ogun State Elders Advisory Council, Chief Olu Okuboyejo, also expressed confidence in Abiodun’s capacity to represent the interests of Ijebu and Remo at the Senate, citing his experience as governor over the past seven and a half years.

World.title: Ex-Minister Agunloye set to file no-case submission as EFCC closes case
World.content:
Former Minister of Power and Steel Olu Agunloye has told the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court that he intends to file a no-case submission in his ongoing trial over the controversial $6 billion Mambilla Power Project contract.

Mr Agunloye, who is being prosecuted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), made this known through his lawyer, Adeola Adedipe, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), on Thursday after the anti-corruption agency closed its case.

“The defence is filing and applying to make a no-case submission pursuant to the enablement under Section 302 and Section 303 of ACJA, 2015,” Mr Adedipe told the court.

He asked the trial judge, Jude Onwuegbuzie, to grant the defence 21 days to file its submission and allow the EFCC time to respond.

The judge granted the request and fixed 3 February for the lawyers to adopt their arguments on the no-case submission.

Details of charges

Mr Agunloye faces seven charges, including disobedience to a presidential directive, conspiracy, forgery and receiving gratification.

The charges relate to his role in awarding the $6 billion Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project contract to Sunrise Power and Transmission Company Limited (SPTCL) in May 2003.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The project was a proposed 3,050-megawatt hydroelectric facility in Kakara village, Taraba State, which was never completed.

The EFCC accused Mr Agunloye of disobeying a presidential directive issued during a Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting in May 2003 concerning the contract.

The agency alleged that he violated the directive by signing a letter to SPTCL, purportedly conveying “the approval of the Government of the Federal Republic of Nigeria for the construction of the 3,960 megawatts Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station.”

The EFCC also accused him of conspiring with Leno Adesanya, the major promoter of SPTCL, who the agency said was at large, to falsify a document titled “Construction of 3,960MW Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Station on a Build, Operate and Transfer Basis” in 2003.

Other allegations include receiving more than N5 million in gratification from SPTCL and Mr Adesanya.

Mr Agunloye has denied all seven charges.

An arbitration tribunal recently exonerated Nigeria in the dispute over the project after finding that the award of the contract to SPTCL was tainted by bribery.

EFCC closes its case

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that former Minister of Power and Steel, Liyel Imoke, testified against his predecessor in the case.

On 19 October, Mr Imoke, a former governor of Cross River State, told the court that Mr Agunloye awarded the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project contract without FEC approval.

During Thursday’s proceedings, Mr Imoke testified further under re-examination by the EFCC’s lawyer, Abba Mohammed. He said he attended the 17th FEC meeting held on 23 July 2003.

On 2 November, Mr Adedipe had challenged the witness’s recollection of the council’s adoption of the minutes of the 21 May 2003 meeting.

Mr Imoke confirmed that the 21 May 2003 meeting was the last FEC meeting held during former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s first term in office.

He also acknowledged that he was not present when the council adopted the minutes of the meeting because he was not a minister or FEC member at the time. He was appointed minister in July 2003, during Mr Obasanjo’s second term.

The testimony marked the end of the EFCC’s case against Mr Agunloye.

EFCC’s case

The EFCC arraigned Mr Agunloye in January 2024 over the Mambilla power project contract.

The agency amended the original charges less than a month later and re-arraigned him on 3 February 2024. It arraigned him again on 18 September 2025 following another amendment to the charges.

After Mr Agunloye pleaded not guilty, the EFCC called six witnesses to establish its case.

They included the Investigating Police Officer (IPO), Assistant Commissioner of Police Umar Babangida, who told the court that the contract award letter dated 22 May 2003, allegedly issued by Mr Agunloye, was forged.

However, Mr Babangida also acknowledged that Mr Agunloye reduced the federal government’s proposed equity participation in the project from 25 per cent to not more than 10 per cent.

He agreed that the reduction represented a difference of $900 million but maintained that it was made without presidential approval.

Another witness, Ugochukwu Okoli, who testified in April, said the copy of the FEC meeting minutes tendered in court originated from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

Mr Agunloye’s suits

Mr Agunloye also filed a suit against the EFCC, accusing the agency of violating his fundamental rights.

In March 2024, the Federal High Court in Abuja dismissed the suit.

However, in October, the former minister won a libel case against the EFCC over the agency’s portrayal of his trial in a publication.

In the case, FCT High Court Judge Peter Kekemeke found the commission liable for defaming Mr Agunloye in an article published about his trial.

The judge awarded N10 million in damages against the EFCC for publishing the libellous article on its social media platforms.

Controversial contract

The Mambilla project was first awarded to SPTCL in 2003 under the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. The contract has since been at the centre of a decades-long legal dispute.

An arbitration tribunal in Paris recently ruled in favour of Nigeria and against SPTCL, which had accused the Nigerian government of breaching the contract.

In 2023, Mr Obasanjo accused Mr Agunloye of fraudulently awarding the contract to the company without approval.

The former minister denied the allegation, saying he was being used as a scapegoat to shield others from sanctions by the arbitration panel in Paris over the abandonment of contractual obligations on the project.

The project was designed to generate 3,960 megawatts of electricity and was to be executed on a build, operate and transfer basis.

World.title: Fountain of Life faults bench warrant against Jimmy Odukoya, says he was not served
World.content:
The Fountain of Life Church has faulted the bench warrant issued against Jimmy Odukoya, arguing that he was not duly served with the court processes that required his appearance.

The church also insisted that Mr Odukoya remained its senior pastor and chairperson of the Board of Trustees, despite the ongoing legal dispute over its leadership.

It stated its position in a statement published on its official Instagram page on Thursday, hours after Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin of the Lagos State High Court issued the warrant and subsequently withdrew from the case.

The judge issued the warrant after Mr Odukoya failed to appear before the court to respond to contempt proceedings arising from an earlier order restraining him from acting as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

However, the church said the proceedings raised questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice.

“The Fountain of Life Church expresses grave concern over the judicial proceedings of today, 26 November 2026, before the Honourable Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin of the High Court of Lagos State, which culminated in the issuance of a bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, and the subsequent recusal of the presiding judge,” the statement read.

‘Not duly served’

According to the church, Mr Odukoya’s lawyers maintained that he had not been duly served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through the substituted means authorised by the court.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It alleged that the court’s directives concerning service, contained in its orders of 18 and 23 November, had not been fulfilled.

The church further said Mr Odukoya’s lawyers had filed a notice of appeal and two motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings.

It also alleged that the matter was not on Thursday’s cause list and that journalists were directed to leave the courtroom before the warrant was issued.

“The bench warrant was issued without first determining the outstanding applications, following which the presiding judge recused herself,” the church said.

It noted that the developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December, the date initially fixed for the matter’s mention.

‘Not a conviction’

In an additional clarification posted in the comment section, the church said the warrant did not amount to a conviction or determine the substantive dispute over its leadership.

“For clarity, the issuance of a bench warrant does not constitute a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute,” it said.

“The Church maintains its position, based on the advice of its legal representatives, that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya remains its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. This position forms part of the matters being pursued through the judicial process.”

The church said it would exhaust all appropriate legal remedies available within the Nigerian judicial system.

It urged its members, friends and the public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that its commitment to the ministry’s founding principles and spiritual mandate remained unchanged.

‘I heard, but I have not been served’

The dispute over service had surfaced during the church’s Sunday worship, when Mr Odukoya addressed reports of the injunction restraining him from presenting himself as senior pastor.

“I heard there was an injunction against me, but I have not been served,” he told the congregation.

“There is no Fountain without you. You are the Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.”

Mr Odukoya attended the service despite the injunction and received an enthusiastic welcome from worshippers.

About 10 police vehicles and more than 20 officers were deployed around the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, while worshippers underwent security checks before entering the auditorium.

Contempt proceedings

Justice Adewunmi-Oshin had ordered Mr Odukoya to appear in court on Thursday to show cause in the contempt proceedings instituted by the Incorporated Trustees of the church.

The court had, on 23 November, authorised the service of Form 48 and other processes through newspaper publication, electronic means and by pasting them at a conspicuous part of his last known address at 12 Industrial Estate Road, off Town Planning Way, Ilupeju.

The address is also the headquarters of The Fountain of Life Church.

Form 48 is a formal notice warning a person about the possible consequences of disobeying a court order. Its issuance does not, by itself, constitute a finding of contempt.

The proceedings arose from an ex parte order issued on 18 November restraining Mr Odukoya, whether acting personally or through representatives, from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

The court also restrained him from interfering with or obstructing the church’s governance, activities and other affairs.

Following Thursday’s proceedings and the judge’s withdrawal, the matter is expected to be returned to the administrative judge for reassignment.

Leadership dispute

The court proceedings form part of an escalating struggle over the leadership of the church founded by Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya in 1992.

Some members of its Board of Trustees had announced Mr Odukoya’s removal and named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

They also released a purported succession video in which the late founder was heard naming Adekunle Areogun as his preferred successor while assigning Mr Odukoya an administrative role.

Mr Odukoya and church officials supporting him rejected the trustees’ position and maintained that he remained the senior pastor.

He subsequently approached the Federal High Court in Lagos to challenge his removal, naming his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and several trustees as respondents.

That suit seeks to invalidate resolutions passed by the trustees and secure a declaration that his removal failed to comply with the church’s constitution.

World.title: Lawal strengthens Zamfara Forest Guards, reaffirms decision not to negotiate with bandits
World.content:
Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has reiterated his administration’s firm stance against negotiating with the bandits terrorising the state.

On Thursday, the governor attended the graduation ceremony for the Zamfara Forest Guards at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, in Gusau.

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu launched the armed forest guard initiative on 24 May 2025 to train residents to protect forests and other ungoverned areas nationwide.

More than 1,000 forest guards in Zamfara received training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement, and the rule of law.

At the event, Governor Lawal thanked President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the Forest Guards initiative.

He commended the security agencies, the training coordinator, and the instructors for preparing the cohort for service.

He said, “To the families of our graduates, thank you for the support and encouragement you have given them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists.

“This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services.

“Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods.”

Governor Lawal emphasised that his administration has spent substantially on state security agencies over the past three years, providing equipment, transport, surveillance and logistical support.

“We have provided over 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 pick-up operational vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles, more than 1,000 specialised motorcycles, and additional vehicles and motorcycles for the Homegrown Community Protection Guards.

“We have also supplied surveillance drones, including an 80-metre endurance model that covers up to 50 kilometres and operates continuously for eight hours, improving reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain.

“I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals terrorising our state.”

World.title: Ramaphosa hosts Obasanjo, AFC delegation for Africa infrastructure talks
World.content:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has met with former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and a delegation from the African Finance Corporation (AFC) to discuss infrastructure development and investment opportunities across the continent.

The meeting, held at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, was led by AFC President and Chief Executive Officer, Samaila Zubairu.

Discussions focused on the forthcoming Africa We Build Summit, scheduled to take place in Johannesburg from April 28 to 30, 2027.

A statement from the presidency reads in part, “The summit is expected to highlight infrastructure development at a time when African countries are pursuing an ambitious pipeline of cross-border projects aimed at strengthening regional connectivity and economic integration.

“Through the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), 69 priority projects are currently at various stages of implementation across the continent.

However, advancing the projects requires sustainable and predictable financing, alongside stronger partnerships between governments, development finance institutions and private investors.”

The discussions between Ramaphosa, Obasanjo and the AFC delegation underscored the importance of mobilising investment and strengthening cooperation to translate Africa’s infrastructure ambitions into tangible development outcomes.

The Africa We Build Summit is expected to provide a platform for stakeholders to explore financing opportunities, strengthen partnerships and accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure projects across the continent.

World.title: 2027: Ebonyi CP warns parties against electoral violence
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police, Hope Urunwa Okafor, has warned political parties and their leaders against violence, thuggery and hate speech ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Okafor gave the warning during a meeting she convened with leaders and representatives of political parties in the state to discuss strategies for ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the elections.

The meeting was attended by representatives of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party.

The police commissioner reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force remained apolitical and impartial in the discharge of its duties.

She assured the party leaders that the command was prepared to provide adequate security for campaign activities, protect lives and property, and maintain law and order across the state.

Okafor stressed that no society could thrive in an atmosphere of violence, urging political parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric, hate speech, personal attacks and other forms of communication capable of inciting violence.

She charged party leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by ensuring that their words and actions promoted peaceful political engagement.

The commissioner also urged them to demonstrate zero tolerance for violence among their supporters, rather than merely preaching peace.

She called on the political parties to exercise restraint in their public statements and campaign activities and provide the command with timely information on their campaign schedules and other political engagements to enable adequate security arrangements.

In their separate remarks, the party representatives commended the commissioner for convening the meeting, describing it as timely and necessary ahead of the 2027 elections.

They appealed to the police command to provide adequate security during campaigns and other political activities.

The party representatives also requested that candidates contesting various elective positions be invited to similar engagements to strengthen collective efforts towards peaceful elections.

World.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
World.content:
The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order.

In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case.

The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court.

It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled.

According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings.

The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued.

It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself.

“These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said.

The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice.

It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal.

Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute.

The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process.

It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system.

World.title: PDP vows to reclaim Ebonyi in 2027
World.content:
..Odii receives party flag, promises economic revival

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara, has expressed confidence that the party will reclaim Ebonyi State in the 2027 governorship election through its candidate, Chief Ifeanyichukwuma Odii.

Mohammed stated this in Abakaliki during the party’s campaign flag-off and presentation of flags to Odii and other PDP candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He said Ebonyi had remained a PDP-controlled state since 1999 until the party lost power, alleging that its mandate was taken away by the ruling party.

The PDP chairman further claimed that the party won the last governorship election in the state but was denied victory, insisting that it would recover its mandate in 2027.

He appealed to residents to vote massively for the PDP to change the state’s economic fortunes.

Speaking after receiving the party’s flag, Odii criticised Governor Francis Nwifuru’s spending priorities and promised to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, agriculture and infrastructure development if elected.

The governorship candidate accused the Nwifuru administration of failing to translate increased federal allocations into improved living conditions for residents.

He said despite the increase in federal allocations to the state since 2023, poverty, inadequate electricity, poor healthcare, sanitation challenges and limited economic opportunities remained major concerns.

Odii cited a national poverty assessment which, according to him, indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 Ebonyi residents lived in multidimensional poverty.

He also questioned the state government’s expenditure priorities, alleging that it spent N19.78 billion on donations, entertainment and refreshments by the third quarter of 2026, while allocating N9 billion to education and healthcare combined.

He further alleged that the government spent below its approved healthcare budget in 2025, while no expenditure was recorded for textbooks and teacher training. He also claimed that agriculture received less than two per cent of the state’s 2025 budget.

The businessman said his experience in business and philanthropy had prepared him for the task of governing the state.

He disclosed that his foundation had built more than 150 homes for less privileged families, awarded scholarships to over 2,500 Nigerians and provided relief materials to more than 40,000 families.

According to him, the foundation has also supported over 1,000 farmers annually with agricultural inputs and empowered 3,000 entrepreneurs through grants and seed capital, alongside rural electrification and road projects.

Unveiling his development agenda, Odii promised to promote agricultural mechanisation, irrigation, access to finance and agro-processing facilities to improve farmers’ productivity and earnings.

He said his administration would pursue an integrated infrastructure programme covering roads, electricity, water, housing and digital connectivity, while encouraging private sector investment in power generation and renewable energy.

On education, he promised to improve school infrastructure, strengthen teacher development, expand technical and vocational education and promote youth entrepreneurship.

He also pledged to equip primary healthcare centres, provide essential medicines and recruit qualified medical personnel, particularly in underserved communities.

Odii further promised reforms in the civil service, land administration and justice system, as well as stronger security coordination and mechanisms for resolving communal disputes.

To ensure accountability, he said his administration would establish delivery units to monitor projects, introduce periodic performance assessments for ministries, departments and agencies, and publish regular reports on government performance.

Earlier, Mohammed expressed confidence that the PDP would win the 2027 governorship election, urging residents to support the party’s candidates in the National Assembly, governorship and State Assembly elections.

He called on the electorate to vote for PDP candidates in the National Assembly elections scheduled for January 16, 2027, and support Odii and other State Assembly candidates on February 6.

“History will repeat itself in Ebonyi State come February 6. I want to use this opportunity to call on all the people of Ebonyi. We have candidates for Senate and House of Representatives. Please, on January 16, come out in your numbers and vote for our candidates,” he said.

He urged residents to mobilise support for Odii and other PDP candidates, describing the party as one that understood the needs and aspirations of the people.

The PDP chairman commended the party’s leadership for providing a platform to strengthen its political activities in the state, particularly acknowledging the role of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike.

He described the reception accorded the party during the campaign flag-off as evidence of its continued strength in Ebonyi.

Mohammed expressed optimism that the party would emerge victorious in the governorship election, promising that the national leadership would return to the state to celebrate its victory.

He urged residents to vote for Odii on February 6, 2027, to ensure the emergence of a PDP government in the state.

World.title: Messi, Ronaldo could play together for first time at Tevez testimonial
World.content:
Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them.

The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United.

Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires.

Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid.

If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side.

Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand.

World.title: 2027: Ogun ADC accepts Supreme Court ruling, backs Ogundipe as guber candidate
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accepted the Supreme Court ruling affirming Biodun Collins Ogundipe, popularly known as BCO, as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections.

The party also called on aggrieved members to close ranks and work together for the success of the party at the polls.

The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Executive Committee, local government area (LGA) chairmen, party leaders, elders and other stakeholders held on Thursday.

The meeting, presided over by the State Chairman, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, considered the Supreme Court judgment alongside a letter dated November 23, 2026, from the party’s National Legal Adviser, which, according to the state chapter, reinforced the need for the party to operate within the provisions of the law.

In a communiqué issued at the end of the meeting, the Ogun ADC said it had resolved to accept the apex court’s decision without prejudice and recognise Ogundipe as the party’s duly affirmed governorship candidate in the state.

The party described its position as a demonstration of respect for the rule of law and the need to preserve the party’s unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections.

The development is expected to provide a fresh direction for the party’s preparations in Ogun State, particularly against the backdrop of leadership and governorship candidacy disputes that had generated disagreements among members.

The communiqué further disclosed that Otunba Jimi Adebisi Lawal (JAL) and members of his campaign council had pledged their commitment to supporting the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, as well as all the party’s candidates in Ogun State.

According to the communiqué, the party leadership has resolved to mobilise its entire political structure across the state to ensure victory for its candidates in the forthcoming elections.

It said the mobilisation drive would extend across all levels of the party, including the state, local government, ward and polling unit structures.

The party also reaffirmed its commitment to working collectively for the success of its candidates contesting the presidential, governorship, senatorial, Federal House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections.

It added that political activities would be intensified in the months ahead to strengthen the party’s grassroots structures, expand its support base and consolidate its electoral prospects ahead of 2027.

Speaking on the need for reconciliation, Soluade appealed to party members, leaders and stakeholders to put aside their differences and unite behind the party’s collective ambition.

He urged party loyalists and political stakeholders to shun bickering, divisive tendencies and unnecessary internal disagreements, emphasising that unity and cooperation were essential to the ADC’s success.

The Chairman stressed that the party could only effectively pursue its political objectives and secure electoral victories through collective commitment, mutual understanding and a united front.

The communiqué reaffirmed the Ogun ADC leadership’s determination to work with all stakeholders, irrespective of previous disagreements, towards achieving a common political objective.

It urged members to close ranks, strengthen party cohesion and redirect their energies towards mobilising support for the ADC and its candidates in the 2027 general elections.
