World.title: AC Milan rally from two goals down to beat Olympiakos
World.content:
Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos.

Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knock-out phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Joao Silva’s 49th-minute strike.

But Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the former Ipswich winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute.

Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth, breathing life into the seven-time European champions’ campaign.

Belgians Union Saint-Gilloise are fifth in the standings, one point behind Leverkusen, Ferencvaros and Benfica, after preserving their unbeaten record, also coming back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Lech Poznan.

– Clashes in Georgia –

The Turkish Football Federation condemned “unacceptable” scenes as Georgian police clashed with Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner.

The Istanbul team’s game against Hapoel was being played in Batumi due to security reasons.

“We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the UEFA Europa League match between our representative Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia,” the club said.

A Turkish ministry source said Turkey’s top diplomat, Hakan Fidan, had spoken with his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili.

“Officials from the Turkish Embassy in Tbilisi and the Consulate General in Batumi are at the stadium,” the source said.

“All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights.”

There were also violent clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters during the Ligue 1 club’s 1-0 win in France.

Brighton moved second in the Conference League table by swatting aside Universitatea Craiova of Romania 4-0.

Ghana international Ibrahim Osman scored his first goals for the high-flying Premier League club with a double, with Maxim De Cuyper and Charalampos Kostoulas also on the scoresheet.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side are two points behind leaders Monaco, who edged out Hearts 3-2 at Tynecastle courtesy of Folarin Balogun’s 94th-minute winner.

World.title: Europa: Bournemouth extend winning run with comeback win over Celta Vigo
World.content:
Ten-man Bournemouth fought back to maintain their 100-percent record in the Europa League with a 2-1 victory at Celta Vigo on Thursday.

The fifth round of matches was overshadowed by clashes between Georgian police and Besiktas fans which caused the Turkish club’s match against Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi to be temporarily suspended.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth notched a 10th successive win in all competitions despite finding themselves a goal and a man down in Spain.

The Premier League club, playing in Europe for the first time, now sit three points clear at the top of the 36-team table from second-placed Bayer Leverkusen, who won 2-0 at Dinamo Zagreb.

Bournemouth could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica on Thursday, in two weeks’ time.

Celta struck first in the 19th minute as Bournemouth allowed Iago Aspas time and space in the box, with the 39-year-old making them pay with an excellent left-footed finish to score his first goal since August.

The visitors were dealt another blow just three minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off following a VAR review for a tackle on Couhaib Driouech.

But the Cherries pulled themselves level two minutes after half-time as Alvaro Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli’s cross.

The 10 men completed a remarkable turnaround with 12 minutes to play when Rayan slotted home Marcus Tavernier’s square pass to cap a quick counter-attack.

Celta thought they had snatched a point late on but Ferran Jutgla’s effort was ruled out for offside.

Vanguard News

World.title: Warri Kingdom Matters Arising My Take
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

I have carefully examined the recent outburst and the concerns articulated by a rather insignificant number of members of the Warri Royal Family regarding the leadership of His Royal Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatse III, the Olu of Warri. Having considered the issues raised, the circumstances surrounding the petition and, more importantly, the broader implications for our kingdom, I believe it is necessary to articulate my personal position and make an appeal to all concerned parties in the overriding interest of the Warri Kingdom.

Let me state from the outset that this intervention is neither an attempt to dismiss the concerns expressed by any individual or group nor an endorsement of every position taken by the parties involved. Rather, it is a sincere reflection by a son of the Warri Kingdom who recognises the importance of our traditional institution and firmly believes that our collective interests, unity, peace and long-term development must transcend individual disagreements.

Over the years, some of the petitioners have made commendable contributions to the growth, preservation and advancement of our kingdom. Their commitment, passion and concern for the welfare of our people are acknowledged and appreciated. Indeed, the affairs and future of the Warri Kingdom should be of legitimate interest to every Itsekiri son and daughter. No one should be made to feel that their opinions, grievances or aspirations are unworthy of consideration.

However, the right to express concerns and demand accountability must equally be exercised within a framework that preserves the dignity, integrity and sanctity of our traditional institution. The person occupying the revered throne of the Olu of Warri, His Royal Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatse III, deserves our utmost respect, and that respect is non-negotiable, just as the institution itself deserves our collective protection. These positions are not mutually exclusive.

In the chequered history of the Warri Kingdom, it is difficult to recall any Olu of Warri who has enjoyed the depth, breadth and spontaneity of affection that the incumbent monarch commands among his people. The love, loyalty and commitment he inspires are remarkably organic. Indeed, the emotional attachment of our people to Ogiame Atuwatse III is such that every Itsekiri man and woman would readily go to extraordinary lengths in his defence.

Ogiame Atuwatse III is, without exaggeration, the aspiration of many traditional kingdoms in Nigeria and beyond. His carriage, charisma, poise, gait, intellectual disposition and majestic approach to issues are exceptional. He represents a remarkable blend of traditional values, contemporary sophistication, cultural consciousness and progressive leadership.

We can listen to our brothers and sisters, acknowledge their concerns and encourage constructive engagement without diminishing the authority or dignity of the throne.

Our throne is sacred. Its significance transcends ordinary considerations of leadership and succession. His ascension carries, in the consciousness and spiritual heritage of our people, a profound sense of divine providence, covenant with Almighty God and ancestral continuity. It is an institution that must never be subjected to the whims, grievances or transient ambitions of a few individuals.

Indeed, if anyone considers his enthronement a mistake, I dare say that the Itsekiri nation would rather live with that so-called mistake for eternity than contemplate undoing what has become a source of immense pride, affection and inspiration to our people.

We love him, and we love him unconditionally.

This is particularly personal to me. I belong to the prominent Pinnick family, whose roots and historical connections to the Warri Kingdom run deep. My late father, Chief Oritsetimeyin Japhet Pinnick, occupied the revered traditional position of Olu Orere, while my late mother, Madam Rebecca Ayomike, hailed from the prestigious Ayomike family. My relationship with the kingdom therefore extends beyond ancestry; it is anchored in family heritage, traditional responsibilities, service and enduring personal relationships.

It is against this background that I consider it important to speak at this time. The Warri Kingdom has a rich history, a distinguished traditional heritage and an identity that generations before us have laboured tirelessly to preserve. Whatever our individual differences, we must be careful not to allow present disagreements to undermine the unity and institutional foundations upon which our collective future depends.

My dear brothers, Prince Bernard Emiko and Prince Yemi Emiko, and others who may feel aggrieved, I sincerely appeal to you to retrace your steps. There is absolutely no shame in reconsidering one’s position, extending an olive branch, seeking forgiveness where necessary and embracing reconciliation.

Our kingdom is bigger than all of us. There is room for everyone, and I firmly believe that the Warri Kingdom will always be willing to welcome its sons home and accord them the respect, recognition and esteemed positions they deserve within the traditional institution.

Let us not allow disagreements to become permanent divisions. History will judge us not merely by the positions we take today, but by what we do to preserve the unity, dignity and enduring heritage of the Itsekiri nation.

The throne must remain respected. The kingdom must remain united. And our collective heritage must remain sacrosanct.

Long live Ogiame Atuwatse III!

Long live the Warri Kingdom!

Long live the Itsekiri nation!

Amaju Melvin Pinnick OFR ROI

Chairman,GCEO Brownhill Group

Deputy Chair, FIFA Men’s Competitions Committee

Presidential Advisor to the CAF President

World.title: Saraki Threatens to Sue Abdulrazaq over Defamatory Statements, Says ‘Your Immunity Expires In May 2027’
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has threatened to institute legal action against Kwara State Governor, Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq, over alleged defamatory statements linking him to the Offa robbery case.

Saraki, in a statement issued on Thursday by his Media Office, said he had mandated his lawyers to serve a pre-action notice on the governor, giving him an opportunity to withdraw the alleged defamatory statements.

The statement, signed by Yusuph Olaniyonu, said the governor made the remarks on Wednesday during a meeting with traditional rulers from Kwara South, where he allegedly made spurious allegations against the former Senate President concerning the Offa robbery case.

It described the governor’s comments as “utterly defamatory, malicious, unwarranted, and lacking in any fact or basis.”

Saraki’s media office accused Abdulrazaq of hiding behind the immunity from prosecution guaranteed by Section 308 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to make what it described as reckless allegations.

It further described the governor’s conduct as “a crass abuse of power and misuse of the platform entrusted to him by the people.”

The statement also accused Abdulrazaq of engaging in character assassination, alleging that he had resorted to “gutter politics” because he had no tangible achievements to campaign with.

On the Offa robbery case, Saraki’s media office maintained that the matter had already been investigated by the police, with reports submitted to the Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation and a criminal case filed against the indicted person.

It accused the governor of assuming the roles of investigator, prosecutor and judge in the matter, while making what it called “false magisterial pronouncements.”

The statement added that Saraki would respect the governor’s constitutional immunity while he remains in office but warned that he would face legal consequences after leaving office.

“However, we need to remind him that by May 29, 2027, his immunity will lapse. He will become an ordinary citizen,” the statement said.

It further warned that “By June 1, 2027, he will face the full legal consequences of his defamatory statements in a court of law.”

World.title: Nigerians Need Tinubu-Shettima Till 2031, Borno Women Declare
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

…As Betta Edu women’s mobilisation directorate leads first lady’s economic empowerment outreach to Monday market, UMTH

Women across political divides in Borno State have declared their support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima, expressing optimism that continuity in leadership beyond 2027 would translate into greater economic opportunities, empowerment and prosperity for Nigerian women.

The women made their position known at a stakeholders’ meeting organised by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, through the Directorate of Women Mobilisation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the Government House, Maiduguri.

The event, which attracted thousands of women from across the state, featured the wife of the Vice President, Her Excellency, Hajia Nana Shettima, and the First Lady of Borno State, Professor Mrs Zulum, as special guests.

One of the participants, Hadiza Biu, who disclosed that she was not a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC), led a group of women from different political and social backgrounds in declaring support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket beyond 2027.

Speaking with journalists, she said the interventions of President Tinubu and the First Lady, particularly through economic empowerment initiatives targeting women, widows, and vulnerable Nigerians, had influenced their decision.

“I am not a member of the APC, but what President Tinubu has done for women and widows in Borno State and across Nigeria through the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has made a difference. I and my group, alongside women across the 27 local government areas of Borno State, are expressing our support for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket beyond 2027,” she said.

The stakeholders’ meeting attracted a massive gathering of women, widows, and community representatives. Also in attendance were the wife of the Vice President, Hajia Nana Shettima, and wives of the governors of Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, and Taraba States.

Earlier, the First Lady’s economic empowerment team, led by the Directorate of Women Mobilisation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, visited the popular Monday Monday Market in Maiduguri, where hundreds of women benefited from the initiative.

At the market, hundreds of women, including small-scale entrepreneurs and petty traders, received cash support of ₦100,000 each, alongside other empowerment incentives aimed at strengthening their businesses, boosting household incomes and improving their livelihoods.

The humanitarian outreach also extended to the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH), where the delegation visited patients receiving treatment in various wards, including the Accident and Emergency Unit and other departments.

During the visit, the team interacted with patients and hospital officials, while financial assistance was provided towards the settlement of medical bills of some beneficiaries.

The Chief Medical Director of UMTH, Professor Farouk Buba, and members of the hospital management expressed appreciation to the First Lady for the intervention, describing the support as timely relief for patients and families facing financial difficulties.

Similarly, the Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre, Nguru, Yobe State, Professor Hadiza Usman, and her management team acknowledged the humanitarian initiative and offered prayers for the First Lady, commending her commitment to supporting vulnerable Nigerians.

The beneficiaries also offered prayers for Senator Oluremi Tinubu, expressing gratitude for the financial assistance and other humanitarian interventions.

Speaking during the engagements, Dr Betta Edu said the outreach reflected the First Lady’s commitment to economic inclusion, social welfare, and improved living conditions for women, petty traders, widows and other vulnerable Nigerians.

She noted that economic empowerment and humanitarian interventions remained critical components of efforts to support communities, particularly women, who constitute a significant segment of Nigeria’s informal economy.

Edu also commended the women of Borno State for their massive participation in the stakeholders’ engagement and acknowledged the support of the wife of the Vice President, Hajia Nana Shettima, as well as other political and community stakeholders.

Borno State occupies a significant position in Nigeria’s electoral landscape. According to electoral figures supplied for this report, the state has 27 Local Government Areas, 312 electoral wards, and 5,071 polling units.

The state also has 2,765,165 registered voters, underscoring the significance of its electorate and the need for sustained grassroots political engagement across its three senatorial districts.

World.title: FG Vows To Eliminate Noma, Says No Family Should Sell Land To Save A Child’s Face
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Federal Government has restated its commitment to eliminate Noma in Nigeria, with a renewed push for prevention, early detection, surgical rehabilitation and social reintegration of survivors, declaring that no family should be forced to sell its land to pay for reconstruction.

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, gave the assurance on Thursday in Sokoto at the Biennial Meeting and Scientific Conference of the Nigerian Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (NAOMS), held at Karma Guest Inn, where he spoke on behalf of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare.

Represented by the Chief Medical Director, Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Kware, Dr. Suleiman Abubakar Baguda, Salako described the conference theme, “The Role of the Maxillofacial Surgeon in the Treatment of Noma,” as apt and deeply human, saying it reflects the choice of surgeons to put their scalpel where the pain of the nation is felt most, in the service of children whose faces and futures are threatened by a preventable disease.

He described Noma as a disease of poverty, malnutrition, poor oral hygiene and weak health systems, which begins as a simple gum infection in a malnourished child aged 2 to 6 years and within two weeks can destroy the lips, cheeks, nose and jaw, noting that globally 90 per cent of children who develop acute Noma die if not treated early, while survivors are left with severe disfigurement and a lifetime of stigma.

Salako said Nigeria bears one of the highest burdens in the world, particularly in Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Borno and other states in the North, but recalled that following advocacy by the Federal Ministry of Health and stakeholders, including NAOMS, the World Health Organisation in December 2023 recognised Noma as a Neglected Tropical Disease, a victory Nigeria must now translate from listing to elimination.

He said government has strengthened the capacity of frontline healthcare workers and community health actors to recognise early signs of Noma, facilitate timely referrals and improve community awareness, a strategy that has paid off as most victims now know where to obtain help, while stressing the need to move beyond isolated interventions to a coordinated, adequately supported and sustainable national programme.

He disclosed that the Federal Government recently launched the National Oral Health Strategic Plan 2026-2030, with commitment to integrate oral healthcare into primary healthcare, train primary oral health workers for preventive care and deploy integrated PHC oral health care in every LGA, so that Noma will be detected and treated early.

Salako described maxillofacial surgeons as central and indispensable in Noma management, noting that while early detection can prevent progression, survivors of advanced Noma often require highly specialised reconstructive surgery to restore facial structures, improve oral function and address complex deformities.

He announced that Noma care, from early detection to post-operative follow-up, will be included in the Basic Health Care Provision Fund package and NHIA benefit package, while surveillance has been strengthened through integration into IDSR and DHIS2, and plans are underway to open the National Noma Registry and Research Centre to provide Nigerian data on outcomes, recurrence and best flap techniques.

Declaring that “Noma is NOT contagious. Noma is NOT a curse. Noma is preventable,” Salako charged young residents not to run away from Noma surgery, describing it as difficult, long and not lucrative, but the most rewarding surgery they will ever do, adding, “Nigeria needs you. The child in Shinkafi needs you.”

He challenged NAOMS to produce a National Clinical Practice Guideline for Noma Management in Nigeria before its next Biennial Conference to standardise care from PHC to tertiary level, while acknowledging partners supporting prevention, treatment and rehabilitation and pledging continued support for the Noma Survivors Association.

Salako added that through early detection, timely treatment, specialised surgical intervention, rehabilitation and sustained community engagement, Nigeria can significantly reduce the burden of Noma and restore dignity to affected individuals.

In his remarks, the President of the Nigerian Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (NAOMS), Prof. Olalekan Micah Gbotolorun, charged members of the association to strengthen capacity against Noma, which he said spreads rapidly and is very devastating.

He stated that Noma is preventable and implored health providers from primary to tertiary levels to detect Noma early for possible treatment, while enjoining them to intensify advocacy on the causes and prevention of the disease.

On his part, the Commissioner of Health, Sokoto State, Dr. Faruk Umar Abubakar, thanked the association for giving Sokoto the hosting right,

Represented by Dr. Adamu Abubakar, Director of Medical Services in the state, Faruk said Sokoto State has done enough and equipped the Noma hospital to render effective service delivery.

He urged participants to be attentive and focused to enable them benefit from the programme, as the highlight of the event was the presentation of a lecture by Dr. Henry Leonhardt, Consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon from Dresden University Clinic, Germany.

World.title: Tinubu Announces Financial Compensation, House for Each Family of Igbokoda Air Mishap Victims
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Linus Aleke in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has announced financial compensation and a house for each family of the 25 victims of the tragic Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State.

The gesture is aimed at supporting the bereaved families and honouring the memory and sacrifices of those who lost their lives in the unfortunate incident.

The President announced the gesture during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR-42 aircraft crash.

He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were on board the aircraft.

Tinubu described the housing allocation as a demonstration of the nation’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the fallen personnel.

“As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of three-bedroom flats in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident.

“No home can ever replace the one you have lost, but they gave their lives for Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home,” he said.

The President added that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft.

He further disclosed that he had approved financial compensation of N100 million for each of the bereaved families of the military personnel.

He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony.

According to him, “In addition to the flats, these officers’ families will receive N100 million each from this government.

“Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen.”

The President also assured Nigerians that the 5 October aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety.

“I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said.

Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and the provision of better equipment.

“A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added.

The President urged the bereaved families to remember the deceased for their service and contributions to the country, assuring them that their sacrifices would remain etched in the nation’s memory.

World.title: Shun Political Isolation, Strengthen Your Role in National Affairs, Shettima Tell South-east
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said that the people of the South-east are too important to Nigeria to isolate themselves from national affairs.

Shettima said the South-east remained an integral part of the national conversation and must continue to participate in shaping the country’s future, instead of cocooning themselves in a corner at a time when their voices ought to be heard clearly.

The vice-president stated this Thursday in Ekwulobia, Orumba North Local Government Area of Anambra State, where he inaugurated three key projects — a flyover, tower of light and a shopping mall — built by the Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo.

He said: “The Igbo are hardworking and resourceful people whose enterprise, determination and adaptability had earned them recognition across the world.

“I commend the South-east looking beyond political divisions and embracing active participation in national affairs. Such engagement is necessary for the region to reclaim and strengthen its place in Nigeria’s political mainstream.”

Shettima said the inaugurated projects addressed both the social needs and commercial aspirations of the state, insisting that the flyover would ease the movement of people and goods, while the shopping mall would create opportunities for commercial growth, and the Tower of Light and other ancillary structures would contribute to the urban renewal of Ekwulobia.

He commended Soludo for prioritising infrastructure that improves how people live, travel and conduct businesses, describing the projects as practical demonstrations of the economic benefits of good infrastructure.

Earlier, Soludo described the location of the flyover as a former centre of chaos and gridlock, saying his administration had demonstrated the courage to transform the area into a more orderly environment.

He appreciated the vice-president for returning to Anambra State, barely one week after his previous visit for political campaigning, to inaugurate the projects.

The vice-president’s visit also formed a basis for political campaigns, showcasing the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC), as members of both parties wielded flags to depict their support for each other.

The event was also attended by several ditaries, including the Deputy Governor of Anambra State, Dr Onyeka Ibezim; Senator Uche Ekwunife; members of the federal delegation; businessman, Sir Emeka Offor; former Director-General of the Budget Office, Ben Akabueze; Cardinal Peter Okpaleke; and other captains of industry.

World.title: NSCDC: CSOs Pass Vote of Confidence in Audi, Hail Reforms, Professionalism
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

***Coalition commends improved personnel welfare, Safe Schools Initiative, Mining Marshals, human rights compliance, intelligence-led operations

A coalition of civil society organisations (CSOs) under the Joint Council of Civil Society Coalitions and Advocacy Movement in Nigeria (JOCCAMIN) has passed a joint vote of confidence in the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, and the entire leadership of the corps, describing his administration as a period of significant institutional reforms and professional development.

The coalition, comprising major organisations representing a wider civil society advocacy movement, made the declaration during a world press conference on Thursday in Abuja.

Speaking on behalf of the coalition, Rev. Solomon Semaka said the endorsement followed an assessment of the corps’ institutional development, operational initiatives, personnel welfare and contributions to Nigeria’s internal security architecture.

Semaka said Prof. Audi had demonstrated commitment to repositioning the NSCDC through reforms focused on human rights, discipline, professionalism, accountability and respect for the rule of law.

According to him, “Under Prof. Audi, human rights is no longer a slogan in the NSCDC, it is a doctrine.”

The coalition also commended the emphasis on lawful rules of engagement and the reported disciplinary action against 66 personnel for various offences, including dismissal, compulsory retirement, demotion and warnings, following established disciplinary procedures and approvals by the Civil Defence, Corrections, Fire and Immigration Services Board (CDCFIB).

On personnel welfare, JOCCAMIN commended efforts to address inherited salary and promotion arrears, ensure prompt payment of salaries and allowances, implementation of the new minimum wage and incorporate applicable allowances into monthly emoluments.

It also highlighted the reported enrolment of personnel in the Employees’ Compensation Scheme administered by the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), as well as the payment of N87,455,217 in Group Life Insurance benefits to beneficiaries of deceased and injured officers, adding that: “Welfare is not charity, it is strategy; and Audi has used it to build a motivated corps.”

The coalition further acknowledged the administration’s promotion reforms, citing a recent exercise in which approximately 22,000 personnel participated, with about 17,000 senior officers reportedly promoted after meeting the relevant requirements.

It described the exercise as an important step towards addressing career stagnation and improving morale, adding that: “Promotion is no longer about who you know. It is about what you have done, how you have served, and how you have performed.”

On school security, the organisations commended the NSCDC’s role in the Federal Government’s Safe Schools programme, particularly the establishment of the National Safe Schools Response Coordination Centre at the Corps’ headquarters in Sauka, Abuja, which was flagged off on February 13, 2023.

They also acknowledged the reported nationwide vulnerability assessment identifying more than 81,000 schools with varying levels of security risks.

The coalition described the initiative as a critical intervention in protecting Nigeria’s educational future, declaring that: “Every child deserves the opportunity to acquire an education without fear of kidnapping, violence or insecurity.”

The coalition also described the establishment of the Mining Marshals, under the command of Assistant Commandant-General John Onoja Attah, as a significant intervention against illegal mining and the criminal exploitation of Nigeria’s mineral resources.

It said the specialised formation had undertaken operations involving arrests, closure of suspected illegal mining sites and efforts to disrupt criminal networks. The organisations urged the unit to sustain intelligence-led enforcement while respecting human rights and due process.

JOCCAMIN equally commended the creation of the Special Female Squad, describing it as an important step towards gender inclusion and specialised security operations, particularly in the protection of schools, children and vulnerable communities.

It noted that the deployment of trained female officers had expanded opportunities for women in frontline security operations. “Audi did not just talk about gender inclusion, he armed it, trained it, and deployed it,” the coalition stated.

On the protection of critical national assets and infrastructure, the organisations acknowledged the corps’ anti-vandalism operations, efforts against crude oil theft and illegal refining, and the activities of the Commandant-General’s Special Intelligence Squad.

Citing figures attributed to the corps’ operational briefings, the coalition said the squad had recorded “more than 2,000 arrests, destroyed over 400 illegal refineries, prosecuted more than 1,000 suspects and secured several convictions”.

It also recognised the contributions of the Agro-Rangers in protecting farmers and agricultural communities, alongside technology-driven initiatives such as the N-Alerts system for reporting sexual and gender-based violence.

The organisations welcomed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s renewal of Audi’s appointment for another five-year term, effective February 27, 2026, describing it as an opportunity to consolidate the reforms and strengthen the corps’ contribution to national security.

In its resolutions, the coalition called on the Federal Government “to provide the NSCDC with adequate funding, modern equipment, technology, logistics and improved personnel welfare”, while urging Nigerians and community leaders to cooperate with security agencies in protecting lives and property.

The coalition, however, clarified that its endorsement did not amount to a waiver of its responsibility to demand accountability, transparency and respect for human rights.

It urged public commentators to verify information before publication, while maintaining that constructive criticism remained essential to public accountability.

The organisations concluded their declaration by stating: “We stand with the NSCDC. We stand with Prof. Audi. We stand with professionalism, human rights and national security.”

The organisations that jointly issued the declaration include the Centre for Human Rights and Accountability; College of Bishops, Imams and Clergy Councils; Save Nigeria Movement; Freelance Journalists Federation; Centre for Transparency and Good Governance; Society for Peace and Human Rights Advocacy; and Conference of Harmonised Civil Society Organisations in Nigeria.

World.title: Shettima Mourns Pete Edochie, Says Africa Has Lost A Custodian Of Cultural Memory
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has expressed deep sorrow over the passing of veteran broadcaster and legendary Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing his death as a profound loss to Nigeria and the African cultural community.

According to him, the late actor, who passed away at the age of 79, belonged to a generation of African storytellers

who understood the importance of preserving the identity, history and moral consciousness of a people through the arts.

In a condolence message issued on Thursday, Shettima extended his sympathies to the Edochie family, the government and people of Anambra State, the Nigerian creative industry and millions of admirers across the world.



He said, “Every civilisation depends on its storytellers to preserve its memory and transmit its wisdom from one generation to another. Chief Pete Edochie was one of those extraordinary custodians of African memory.



“His unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart came at a significant moment in our cultural history, when Africa was asserting its right to tell its own stories and define itself before the world.

“Through his commanding voice, profound use of proverbs and remarkable interpretation of African traditions, he brought dignity to our indigenous knowledge and made generations of Africans appreciate the richness of their cultural inheritance.”



The Vice President noted that Chief Edochie’s remarkable journey from broadcasting, which he began in 1967, to becoming one of Africa’s most recognisable actors mirrored the evolution of Nigeria’s creative industry into a global cultural force.

He observed that the emotional attachment millions of people developed to the late actor over the decades explained why his passing would feel deeply personal, even to those who had never met him.



“For decades, Pete Edochie was a familiar presence in our homes, a voice that evoked memories of childhood, family gatherings and the wisdom of our elders.



“While the nation mourns an iconic actor, we must remember that a family has lost a beloved husband, father and grandfather. No amount of public admiration can adequately compensate for the absence of a loved one in the intimate and ordinary moments of family life,” the Vice President added.



Shettima urged younger generations of Nigerian filmmakers and actors to draw inspiration from the late thespian’s mastery of his craft and commitment to authentic African storytelling.



He prayed for the peaceful repose of Chief Edochie’s soul and for Almighty God to grant his family and all who mourn him the strength and comfort to bear the painful loss.

World.title: Lost in translation? Nando’s has a message for France
World.content:
Nando's has poked fun at France ahead of the Nations Championship finals this weekend. Images via X

Nando’s has made a cheeky dig at France ahead of the Springboks’ performance in the Nations Championship finale, which takes place on Sunday, 30 November.

The clash will mark the second time the countries have faced each other in recent weeks, following their showdown in Paris earlier this month, which South Africa lost.

This weekend, the rugby rivals will compete for the inaugural title at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.



NANDO’S MOCKS FRANCE WITH SPRINGBOKS SUPPORT

On its Instagram and Facebook pages, Nando’s showed its loyalty and support to the Springboks when it posted: “France, Uya kusiqonda ngeCawe”,

The Xhosa statement was a message to the French rugby team, translated as: “You will understand us on Sunday.”

It was also an ode to Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick, who addressed a media conference earlier this week in his mother tongue, Xhosa. The move was frowned upon by international media, despite Xhosa being one of South Africa’s official languages.



It is believed to have been made in a bid to avoid misunderstanding, particularly on the back of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus’s matchday suspension following his comments about the duties of match officials during the match against France in Paris earlier this month.

MATCH DETAILS

The Springboks will face France in the inaugural Nations Championship final on Sunday, 29 November 2026, at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, London.



Kick-off is scheduled for 18:40 South African time.

South African viewers can watch the match live on SuperSport Rugby, which is open to all DStv subscribers as part of its OpenTime promotion.

Meanwhile, Springbok coach Rassie will host another watch-along party, which will stream from his hotel room.

World.title: ‘I’m a size 34’: Miss SA Tiyani responds to body-shamers
World.content:
Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu has responded to social media trolls who have criticised her appearance with body-shaming comments about her weight.

The 27-year-old PR and Corporate Communications graduate was crowned earlier this month in a pageant finale at the Sandton Convention Centre.

Many critics questioned the new management, new direction of the pageant and even its makeshift crown, which quickly went viral on social media.



MISS SA TIYANI MAKAMU RESPONDS TO BODY-SHAMERS

Speaking to SABC talk show, Daily Thetha, Miss SA Tiyani Makamu spoke about being body-shamed on social media after her crowning.

She shared: “Now I’m a size 34…I’m a 27-year-old woman, and I’ve dealt with a lot of my insecurities, and there is no conversation people can have outside of me that I haven’t had with myself.

“Going onto the Miss SA platform, I was fully aware of what I was opening myself up to. There was a lot of self-counselling, unspoken conversations I’ve had with myself”.

Tiyani, who revealed that she was severely underweight as a teen, continued: “It’s not to say that when I go through things that it doesn’t sting a little, but I need to go back to higher ground and understand that I’m here now.

“There’s also caution now because of the platform that I hold”.

VIEWS ON THAT CROWN

Tiyani Makamu also shared that she was unfazed about the social media backlash to the Miss SA crown



According to pageant organisers, the item placed on Tiyani’s head during the finale was “temporary”, as they have planned to invite designers to contribute towards the finished product.

World.title: Tatjana Smith embraces ‘new family’
World.content:
Tatjana Smith on representing the Netherlands. Images via IG

Tatjana Smith has shared her excitement about representing the Netherlands as a professional swimmer, given her Dutch ancestry.

Earlier this month, the Olympic swimmer revealed that she would be representing the European country, to which she has dual citizenship.

The gold-medallist shared that finances, sustainability and support were key motives for switching her sporting nationality.



TATJANA SMITH EXCITED ABOUT DUTCH SPORTING CHAPTER

In an Instagram post, Tatjana Smith shared her excitement at her new chapter, joining Team Netherlands.

In a clip, the 29-year-old introduced herself to her new Dutch followers, sharing a look at her own Dutch upbringing and heritage.

Tatjana revealed that she had deep roots in the Netherlands, where her father, Rene Schoenmaker, was born and raised.

She shared: “Joining a new team and becoming part of a new swimming family is something I dont take for granted”

A few days earlier, Tatjana shared a post about how her Christian faith had affirmed her career move.

“Grateful for where I’ve been, at peace with where I am, and trusting Him with everything that’s still ahead”, she shared.



NOT ‘RUNNING AWAY’

Not long after announcing her decision to switch sporting nationalities, Tatjana Smith reflected on representing South Africa as a professional swimmer. She also responded to her critics who questioned her new allegiance to the Netherland.

Posting a montage of her career highlights on her social media platforms, Tatjana shared: “11 years being part of Team SA. One flag. Countless sacrifices. Four Olympic medals. World Championship medals. Commonwealth medals. African Championship medals.

“Years of dedication, commitment and pride in wearing the green and gold”

She continued: “Giving up when things get difficult doesn’t produce a journey like this. And running away when things get tough? I think 11 years tells a different story”.

Tatjana – whose gold and silver Olympic medals will remain SA accolades – added: “Forever grateful for the privilege of representing South Africa”.

FIRST RACE AFTER NATIONALITY SWITCH

Tatjana Smith will make her debut for the Netherlands at the World Aquatics Short Course Swimming Championships in Beijing, China, from 1–6 December 2026.

Instead of wearing green and gold, she will be wearing as she swims alongside her former South African colleagues.

World.title: Table Mountain introduces online-only ticketing ahead of festive season
World.content:
Visitors to Table Mountain can no longer buy the standard and Fast Track Cableway tickets from the onsite ticket office. Image: Pexels

The Table Mountain Aerial Cableway Company (TMACC) has made changes to the way visitors can buy tickets.

With the festive season just around the corner, those who visit the popular Capetonian landmark will have to purchase tickets online rather than buy them from the Lower Station Ticket Office. Through this switch, this will drastically reduce visitor queue lengths.

Let’s unpack this new change:

TABLE MOUNTAIN: NEW TICKETING RULES

From Tuesday, 15 December 2026, you can no longer buy the standard and Fast Track Cableway tickets from the onsite ticket office.



Instead, you will need to buy these tickets via authorised online booking channels before you arrive.

These channels include:

Webtickets

The Webtickets WhatsApp service

City Sightseeing South Africa

Tickets that are not purchased through these channels will not be accepted.



WILL THE TICKET STATION BE CLOSED?

No, the Lower Station Ticket Office will not be closed.

Per Cape Town News, South African pensioners, students and Wild Card holders can continue to purchase discounted tickets from the ticket office.

Additionally, qualifying South Africans can obtain free tickets during their birthday month from the office.



TABLE MOUNTAIN: FESTIVE TREAT

Since the cableway’s inauguration in 1929, more than 33 million people have visited the summit of Table Mountain. Here, they are afforded stunning views of the city below and of Mother Nature at her most beautiful.

If you’re looking for ways to spend time with your family or treat yourself this festive season, taking a trip up to the mountainous tabletop is certainly something you should add to your to-do list.

For the latest ticket prices, be sure to take a look here. And remember to buy them online before your arrival.



Otherwise, let us know in the comments section below about whether or not you agree with TMACC’s decision to make ticket-buying an online-only option.

World.title: ‘Why am I alive?’: Derick Hougaard shares emotional update
World.content:
Former Springbok Derick Hougaard has shared an emotional update about his state of mind. His Facebook post comes a few months after the rugby player, fondly known as the “Liefling van Loftus”, revealed that he was in “big trouble” and facing financial hardships.

Since then, fans have rallied to show him support with kind words and by donating to his GoFundMe campaign.

Since hanging up his boots in 2015, Derick has suffered significant personal setbacks, including substance addiction, failed relationships and a series of health issues.



On his Facebook account, Derick Hougaard posted a lengthy message reflecting on his life. This included going through significant lows, in which he relied on his Christian faith to guide him through

“But God, you stayed with me through the night. In the hospital all night alone. I was weak and full of fear. But a faithful voice was always there. Your grace carried me home when I could not stand alone. Through the storms and the darkness, You led all the way. Grace held my hand. When I couldn’t understand…Through it all, You never left my side.

“There were seasons of confusion where my prayers were lost in spaces… When the world said I was hopeless… You rewrote my whole story and showed me where I belong”.



Derick Hougaard also hinted at a 2023 biography of his life.

He continued: “There was even a book written about me that I didn’t have a say or input. And not everything is true. Will I ever have the guts to tell my side of my life, or will I forgive and go to the grave with it?

“Jesus, why am I alive? You have a plan for me greater than what many people see. Because you saved me when I could have been dead.



Derick ended the post on a positive note, hinting at a “comeback”.

“Thank you to the person who stands by me. You know who you are. You don’t want credit, and I respect that. For everyone who relishes in another’s sorrow, I just want to say: the further you fall, the greater the comeback. And bigger is your testimony in Jesus’ name.

“Thank you to everyone who believes in me and prays and made me who I am today. See you soon in a town near you”.



RUGBY HERO TO BOOZE AND PILL ADDICT

Derick Hougaard’s stint as a Springbok player was cut short due to multiple head injuries. He had just 8 test caps for the national team.

However, the flyhalf had a decorated career as a Bulls player – where he was known as the “Liefling van Loftus” – playing over 100 matches in total, including 43 Super Rugby caps and 68 Currie Cup appearances for the team between 2002 and 2008.

In 2003, the star athlete suffered a significant blow to the head during the Rugby World Cup. This, after he was knocked out by Samoa’s Brian Lima in a brutal yet legal tackle, according to SA Rugby.



In the 2023 KykNET docuseries Hougaard: Liefling van Loftus, Derick admitted to heavy drinking and dependency on sleeping pills and pain medication.

He also claimed he had spiralled into a deep depression after his rugby career was cut short.

In the self-titled 2023 biography Derick Hougaard, author Brendan Nel wrote about the player’s long history of addiction.



An excerpt from an interview in the book reflected on Derick’s struggle to adapt to life after rugby.

He said, “This is one of the biggest gaps in my life. I always knew rugby was my passion, yes. But you don’t realise how big a role it plays in your life until you lose it. You don’t realise how big a void it will cause when you are no longer actively involved in it.”

Derick then again admitted to his addiction struggles: “It takes a man to ask for help or to admit that you need help. There are ugly and difficult times behind me, especially when I mix the pills and booze.”

World.title: Carling Knockout Cup final: Pirates, Chiefs off to Durban!
World.content:
The Moses Mabhida Stadium will host the 2026 Carling Knockout Cup final despite concerns surrounding a major rugby fixture scheduled in Durban on the same day.

The iconic Durban venue was among the options being considered by the PSL to host the highly-anticipated final between Kaizer Chiefs and Orlando Pirates on Saturday, 12 December 2026.

However, the scheduling presented an interesting challenge, with the Hollywoodbets Sharks also set to host Welsh outfit Scarlets in an EPCR Challenge Cup encounter at Kings Park Stadium on the same evening.



The encounter between The Sharks and Scarlets is at 19:30 while the Pirates and Chiefs match is scheduled for 15:30.

The two venues are approximately two kilometres apart, raising potential concerns about traffic congestion, crowd movement and security arrangements.

Carling Knockout Cup final between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs in durban

Despite the potential logistical headache, Moses Mabhida Stadium was always in the conversation as the PSL considered the best venue for what promises to be one of the biggest football matches on the South African sporting calendar.



The situation had also attracted interest from Cape Town, with DHL Stadium expressing its willingness to host the Soweto Derby final.

The City of Cape Town had reportedly backed its bid with an estimated R4 million.

However, hosting the final in Durban would give local football supporters another opportunity to witness the country’s biggest football rivalry at a stadium that has previously staged more than one Soweto Derby game.



Interestingly, South African sporting authorities have previously adjusted major fixtures to avoid clashes with other events.

In April 2026, the Soweto Derby between Chiefs and Pirates was moved from 25 to 26 April because of the Ultra Music Festival at Nasrec.

With two major sporting events potentially competing for space in Durban on 12 December, the PSL’s final decision is regarded as crucial.

World.title: The cheapest metros to buy property in South Africa
World.content:
City skyline of three South African metros. Image: Pexels

Property prices in South Africa’s metros vary greatly.

In Cape Town, the average price for a flat in the city’s central business district (CBD) is upwards of R1 million.

In Johannesburg, you can get a city centre flat for R200 000.



But Johannesburg is not South Africa’s cheapest metro.

South Africa’s 6 most affordable major cities

South Africa has 8 metros across 5 provinces.

These are South Africa’s economic hubs, which can make them a good investment.



But just because property is cheap there doesn’t mean it’s worthwhile.

To determine whether affordable property is worth your money, we’ve analysed other economic markers, including unemployment rates and residential property growth.

Durban

To live in Durban’s CBD, a buyer will need at least R280 000 for a studio flat.



The average sale price in the city centre is R420 000.

But outside the city centre, the average sale price is R920 000, making Durban the cheapest metro to buy property.

eThekwini, the municipality in which Durban is located, also struggles with unemployment.



According to data from Statistics South Africa (Stats SA), the municipality’s expanded unemployment rate is 39.2%, as of the third quarter.

Average Sale Price: R920 000

R920 000 Unemployment Rate: 22.2%

22.2% Expanded Unemployment Rate: 39.2%

39.2% Property Growth (2021 – 2025): 5.1%

Germiston

Germiston is the City of Ekurhuleni’s municipal seat. It is also the cheapest metro to buy property in the city centre.

The average sale price in Germiston Central was R305 000 at the end of 2025.



Currently, the cheapest property on sale in Germiston Central is a 1-bedroom flat with a R220 000 asking price.

Beyond the city centre, the average home sells for R990 000.

Property price growth has been fair.

Over the last five years, property prices have risen 7.6%.



However, unemployment in Ekurhuleni sits at 37.7%, and the expanded unemployment rate is 45.5%, according to Stats SA’s most recent data.

Average Sale Price: R990 000

R990 000 Unemployment Rate: 37.7%

37.7% Expanded Unemployment Rate: 45.5%

45.5% Property Growth (2021 – 2025): 7.6%

Johannesburg

Johannesburg Central has the second-cheapest CBD housing in the country.

The average sale price in Johannesburg Central at the end of 2025 was R337 500.



Today, the cheapest flat listed on the market has a R120 000 asking price.

Johannesburg’s property market has been flat for some time.

The average sale price in the rest of the city is R1.1 million, no change from 2024.



Average Sale Price: R1.1 million

R1.1 million Unemployment Rate: 34.9%

34.9% Expanded Unemployment Rate: 38.2%

38.2% Property Growth (2021 – 2025): 4.76%

Pretoria

Buyers can get a flat in Pretoria for as little as R50 000. That’s the going rate for a 1-bedroom flat that is currently up for auction.

However, in Pretoria Central, the average sale price is R417 500.

In the broader city, sectional titles sell for an average of R989 000, up 9.9% from 2024.



Over the last five years, prices are up 16.82%.

Average Sale Price: R989 000

R989 000 Unemployment Rate: 34.5%

39.3% Property Growth (2021 – 2025): 16.8%

Gqeberha

Among the coastal metros, Gqeberha has the potential to rival Cape Town’s rental market.

Not because of massive property price increases, but because of consistent demand and declining unemployment rates.



Currently, the cheapest property in Gqeberha Central is 10% of Cape Town’s average sale price.

Beyond the city centre, the average sale price is R925 000, up 5.11% from 2024.

Average Sale Price: R925 000

37.8% Property Growth (2021 – 2025): 15.6%

Bloemfontein

Bloemfontein, in Mangaung, is one of only three metros where the average city centre property is above R500 000.



At the end of 2025, the average sale price for a home in Bloemfontein Central was R570 000.

In broader Bloemfontein, the average sale price was R1 million at the end of 2025.

World.title: Number Of The Day | R17.70c | 26 November 2026
World.content:
Beyond R17.70: Why A Better Credit Rating Does Not Guarantee A Stronger Rand

South Africa could find itself in the uncomfortable position of receiving international recognition for improving its financial fundamentals while watching its currency lose ground. The rand's recent decline to R17.70 against the US dollar, its weakest level in a year, illustrates an important distinction between improving a country's financial position and building confidence in its economic future.

A credit rating upgrade would be welcome news, but it would not necessarily mean that the broader economy has turned a corner. Financial markets assess more than a government's ability to repay its debts. They also respond to expectations about growth, political stability and whether economic reforms can deliver lasting results.

The Limits Of Dollar Strength

Exchange rates are relative measures. A weakening rand does not automatically indicate that something has gone wrong in South Africa. Sometimes, the explanation lies in what is happening elsewhere.

Expectations of higher US interest rates, for example, can make dollar-denominated investments more attractive. International investors weighing opportunities across different markets may find fewer reasons to accept the additional risks associated with emerging economies when returns in the United States become more competitive.

South Africa is particularly exposed to these shifts in global sentiment. Movements in commodity prices, international investment flows and the dollar can influence the rand independently of domestic economic developments.

The more difficult question arises when the rand continues to weaken even as the dollar loses ground. That does not prove that domestic conditions are responsible, but it provides a reason to look more closely at the risks within South Africa's borders.

The Difference Between Financial Stability And Economic Recovery

An improving sovereign credit rating primarily reflects a country's creditworthiness. It signals greater confidence in its ability to meet financial obligations, potentially improving the conditions under which government can borrow.

However, a healthier public balance sheet is not the same thing as a healthier economy.

South Africa's debt outlook, discussed in the latest Number of the Day episode, points towards stabilisation below 75% of gross domestic product (GDP). Improvements in electricity provision, greater policy certainty and economic reforms also offer reasons for optimism.

Yet persistently high unemployment remains a fundamental constraint. A country can improve its debt outlook without generating sufficient employment, expanding household purchasing power or creating enough opportunities for businesses to grow.

The distinction matters because debt stabilisation creates room for economic progress, but it cannot substitute for that progress. Without stronger economic activity, the foundations supporting an improved fiscal position may themselves become increasingly vulnerable.

Political Stability Is An Economic Consideration

The emerging coalition arrangements in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni introduce another dimension to the debate about investor confidence.

Municipal governance might appear distant from international currency markets, but the quality and predictability of local government have direct implications for economic activity. Businesses depend on functioning infrastructure, reliable services and administrative decisions that allow them to plan beyond the next political cycle.

Coalition government is not inherently incompatible with economic stability. The more important consideration is whether political arrangements produce administrations capable of making decisions, implementing budgets and maintaining continuity.

When political uncertainty threatens those functions, it can complicate investment decisions. The possibility of political gridlock, highlighted alongside South Africa's broader economic challenges in the episode's discussion of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), therefore deserves attention beyond the immediate contest for municipal power.

What The Rand Cannot Tell Us On Its Own

For households and businesses, the consequences of currency weakness extend beyond financial market headlines. A weaker rand can increase the cost of imported goods and production inputs, creating additional pressures for businesses already navigating difficult operating conditions.

But the exchange rate alone cannot provide a complete diagnosis of South Africa's economy. Nor can a credit rating upgrade.

Both are important indicators, measuring different aspects of a much larger picture. The real test is whether improvements in financial stability can translate into productive investment, employment and more dependable governance.

South Africa's challenge is not simply to persuade investors that it can repay its debts. It is to demonstrate that the economy behind those debts has the capacity to grow.

That is a considerably bigger question than whether the rand strengthens or weakens tomorrow.

World.title: Missing Mathibestad granny found alive in Durban
World.content:
PRETORIA - Missing Mathibestad granny, Selina Buyani Peete, has been found in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, 10 days after she went missing.

The 83-year-old was found admitted to the Victoria Mxenge Hospital.

Peete went missing on 16 November, while on a trip with other elderly women she regularly plays soccer with in the town near Hammanskraal.

She reportedly went missing before the group could check into the Albany Hotel. They had allegedly disembarked their transport and gone to the beach before checking in.

While on their way from the beach to go check in, Peete disappeared. The group searched for her to no avail.

Her grandson and a Moretele Local Municipality councillor, and others went to Durban to look for her. They searched parks, hospitals and places of worship.

On the last day of the search, they got word that an elderly woman fitting Peete's description was at the hospital, where she was found.

Moretele Mayor Francinah Tsoku welcomed the fact that Peete's family was finally reunited with their relative.

She has also thanked the public for their support and search for the octogenarian.

"We are relieved and grateful that Koko Peete has been found and back with her family," said Tsoku.

"The past 10 days have been difficult for those closest to her and for many people in our community who followed her story and hoped for her safe return," she added.

World.title: Funeral preparations underway in eXesi for Mlambo-Ngcuka
World.content:
EXESI, Eastern Cape - The late former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka will be laid to rest this weekend.

She died on Friday, aged 71, after complications from a medical procedure.

Family, friends and dignitaries are expected at Anne Shaw, in eXesi, formerly Middledrift, in the Eastern Cape.

In eXesi, funeral preparations are underway.

Her brother-in-law says he expects people from across the Eastern Cape to come and pay their respects.

On Thursday, family members and religious leaders travelled to King Phalo Airport in KuGompo City to receive her remains.

Many say that while Mlambo-Ngcuka may have been a leader and a politician, she also played a major role in uplifting communities, and that is how she will be remembered.

President Cyril Ramaphosa will be joining other dignitaries at the funeral, where he's expected to deliver the eulogy.

eNCA's Ronald Masinda reports in the video above.
