World.title: Chilanga Council commits to forming collaboration
World.content:
Chilanga Town Council Chairperson, Buumba Mulunda, has reaffirmed the council’s commitment to strengthening stakeholder partnerships and driving sustainable development in the district.

Mr Mulunda stated that the council remains committed to creating an enabling environment for investment and ensuring that development initiatives respond to the needs of communities.

He noted that decentralisation, inclusive governance and environmental sustainability are essential to achieving meaningful development.

Mr Mulunda stressed that women, youths and persons with disabilities must have opportunities to participate in shaping the future of their communities.

He noted that the call by President Hakainde Hichilema for local authorities to attract investment, promote entrepreneurship, improve infrastructure and utilise their districts’ economic potential, speaks directly to the responsibility carried by local leaders.

“I believe that through shared responsibility, cooperation and accountable leadership, we can build stronger local institutions and deliver sustainable development,” said Mr Mulunda.

He called on all stakeholders to work together in making local government a driving force for economic opportunity, better service delivery and improved livelihoods for the people of Chilanga.

World.title: Chief Chibale wants construction of his palace expedited
World.content:
Chief Chibale of the Lala people of Serenje District of Central Province has called on the government to expedite the construction works of his palace.

Speaking when Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge, paid a courtesy call on him at his palace, the traditional leader observed that the works on the palace has been slow and a source of concern.

“The house is currently incomplete, electrical connections are pending, the boundary wall has not been constructed, and several interior fittings remain to be installed,” he said.

He said the government’s decision to build chiefs modern palaces is a welcome initiative that supports their welfare and enables them to live in dignity while discharging their administrative duties diligently.

Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge, assured the chief that government remains eager to complete the remaining works and pledged to engage the relevant authorities to ensure that works resume.

Ms Mibenge called on the traditional leader to engage his community and encourage residents to benefit from ongoing government programmes and initiatives

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 26, 2026
World.content:
Fuel Tanker Explosion on Cairo Highway Kills 31 People

At least 31 people were killed and 21 others injured when a fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on a busy highway in Cairo, Egypt. The fire in the Warraq neighborhood, which also burned several nearby cars, left victims suffering from burns and smoke inhalation. The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, was on the highway when a high-voltage cable fell on its path, and the driver lost control. The incident is being investigated by authorities. Emergency services have since cleared the wreckage and reopened the highway. The health ministry deployed 39 ambulances to assist victims, while hospitals treated those injured in the fire.

South African President Ramaphosa Wins Phala Phala Court Battle

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal challenge against a parliamentary independent panel report that found he had a case to answer over the theft of $580,000 from his Phala Phala farm. The Western Cape High Court declared the report unlawful and set it aside in its entirety, ruling that the panel had exceeded its mandate and made legal errors. The decision effectively removes the basis for the current impeachment process. However, the opposition parties may challenge the verdict. The judgment does not find any wrongdoing. The scandal, which emerged in 2022, has continued to hang over Ramaphosa's presidency despite several investigations clearing him of any wrongdoing.

Nigeria Seizes 1.5 Tonnes of Meth in Cartel-Linked Lab Raid

Nigerian authorities have arrested five Mexican nationals and a local businessman following the discovery of an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State. More than 1.5 tonnes of the drug, valued at $227 million, were seized. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency said that the operation followed a seven-month international investigation. The suspects are allegedly linked to a wider drug trafficking network involving Mexican cartel specialists and Nigerian collaborators. Nearly seven tonnes of chemicals and industrial equipment were also recovered. This marks the fourth suspected cartel-linked meth laboratory uncovered in Nigeria in recent months. The agency said the latest arrests bring to 10 the number of suspected Mexican meth production specialists detained in the country in recent months.

EU Extends Mozambique Military Mission to 2028

The European Union has extended its Military Assistance Mission in Mozambique until December 2028. It has allocated €17.17 million to support the country's fight against Islamist insurgents in Cabo Delgado. The funding will cover the period from January 2027 to December 2028, under a decision adopted by the Council. The mission will continue training, mentoring and advising Mozambican armed forces in military planning, intelligence, logistics and operational readiness, but will not participate directly in combat. The extension aims to strengthen the country's ability to independently plan and sustain military operations while promoting human rights and civilian protection. The renewed mandate follows a September strategic assessment that found continued EU support necessary to build sustainable capabilities within Mozambique's armed forces.

Egypt, Sudan Agree on Post-War Reconstruction

Egypt and Sudan have agreed to prioritise Sudan's post-war reconstruction, expand economic cooperation and strengthen coordination on Red Sea security. During talks in Cairo, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and Sudanese Prime Minister Kamal Idris reaffirmed their support for Sudan's sovereignty and rejected attempts to militarise the strategic waterway. They insisted that its governance belongs to coastal states. The two sides also underscored the importance of respecting freedom of navigation in the Red Sea while rejecting attempts to "militarize the waterway or take unilateral actions that infringe on the sovereignty of its coastal states." The discussions also covered the voluntary return of Sudanese nationals, the repatriation of prisoners and efforts to restore Sudan's participation in African Union institutions. Idris also called for an inclusive intra-Sudanese dialog to build national consensus, address humanitarian concerns and lay the groundwork for reconciliation.

Close 

AI Fears Mount Ahead of Nigeria's 2027 Elections

Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated images and other irregularities in the country's preliminary voter register, ahead of the 2027 general elections, raising concerns about electoral credibility and preparedness. The irregularities reported included manipulation of facial features, duplicated identities, and dead voters' names. The Independent National Electoral Commission has established a special unit to monitor AI-related threats and deepfakes, as experts warn artificial intelligence could fuel disinformation, manipulate voters and erode public trust in the electoral process. Concerns were heightened by the history of online misinformation during elections in Nigeria and a record-low voter turnout of 27% in 2023.

World.title: South Africa: More Arrests Expected in Tembisa Hospital Scandal - South African News Briefs - November 26, 2026
World.content:
press review

More Arrests Expected in Tembisa Hospital Corruption Scandal

The Special Investigating Unit (SIU) has said that further arrests are expected in the alleged R2 billion Tembisa Hospital corruption scandal, involving businessmen accused of siphoning funds from the facility, reports EWN. The update comes as businessman Hangwani Maumela seeks to recover his Ferrari, which was preserved by the SIU. The State's curator sold the car for R10.1 million. The SIU is also engaging with alleged syndicate member Rudolf Mazibuko. Businessman Stefan Govindraju and his alleged accomplices are set back in court in February 2027.

Ramaphosa Extends TRC Cases Inquiry to 2027



President Cyril Ramaphosa has extended the term of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) Cases Inquiry to March 31, 2027, reports SABC News. The deadline to submit its final report to Ramaphosa has also been extended to May 31 next year. The Presidency said that the third extension is necessary to allow more witnesses to testify before the inquiry, chaired by Justice Sisi Khampepe, concludes its work. The inquiry is investigating alleged efforts to obstruct the prosecution of apartheid-era crimes.

ConCourt Weighs Alternatives to Medical Negligence Payouts

The Constitutional Court is considering whether victims of state medical negligence should be allowed alternatives to once-off lump-sum compensation payments, reports EWN. The Eastern Cape Department of Health and other applicants are challenging a Supreme Court of Appeal ruling that overturned an order allowing victims to receive healthcare services instead. The department argued that large payouts place pressure on public healthcare finances. The court is set to hear arguments opposing the appeal.

World.title: Uganda: 15,000 Young People Acquired HIV in 2023, 80 Percent of Them Girls, Parliament Warns
World.content:
Uganda's ambition to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030 could be undermined by inadequate HIV prevention awareness and limited access to services among young people, Parliament's Committee on HIV/AIDS and Related Matters has warned.

The warning follows the committee's assessment of learning institutions in northern Uganda, where it found that many young people aged 15 to 24 still lack adequate knowledge about HIV prevention.

The committee, led by its chairperson, Stephen Kisa, the MP for Luuka South County, said the information gap, coupled with stigma and inadequate prevention services, threatens progress in the fight against HIV.

"Many young people lack adequate knowledge about HIV prevention. If we do not close this information gap now, we risk losing the gains we have made," Kisa warned.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

At UNITE Unyama Campus, Dean Pario Lot Ewaku told the committee that HIV prevalence among the institution's approximately 600 students is below five per cent.

The institution works with nearby health facilities, maintains confidentiality and uses trained peer educators to promote HIV awareness.

However, Ewaku identified inadequate funding, deep-rooted stigma and a lack of clear intervention guidelines as persistent challenges.

Stigma also discourages some students from testing and seeking information or services, raising concerns about whether existing interventions are reaching those who need them.

At Gulu University, students and health workers cited staff shortages, inadequate condom supplies and the location of the HIV service unit as barriers to accessing prevention and care.

The concerns point to gaps not only in awareness but also in the availability and accessibility of services within learning institutions.

At Gulu Senior Secondary School, head teacher Irene Mwaka said the school works with partner organisations and student clubs to promote HIV awareness among its more than 3,000 learners.

However, she called for increased funding, noting that the school's day-school arrangement limits its ability to monitor learners beyond school hours.

Student leader Moses Okello said peer-to-peer engagement was essential in encouraging open discussions about HIV/AIDS and breaking the silence surrounding the epidemic.

He also called for continuous teacher training to equip educators to support learners seeking guidance without judgment.

The concerns raised in northern Uganda come against the backdrop of national figures showing that young people continue to account for a significant number of new HIV infections.

Uganda AIDS Commission estimates indicate that approximately 15,000 people aged 15 to 24 acquired HIV in 2023, with adolescent girls and young women accounting for about 80 per cent of infections in this age group.

Close 

Preliminary results from the 2025 Uganda Population-Based HIV Impact Assessment (UPHIA) put HIV prevalence among young people aged 15 to 24 at 1.5 per cent, compared with 2.0 per cent among young women and 1.0 per cent among young men.

The figures highlight the disproportionate burden of HIV among young women and the need to strengthen prevention interventions targeting this population.

Despite the challenges, Kisa said Uganda could still achieve its 2030 target if investment in awareness campaigns and accessible, youth-friendly HIV services is prioritised.

The committee's findings point to the need for learning institutions to strengthen prevention education, improve access to HIV testing and other services, address stigma and equip teachers and peer educators to guide young people.

For Uganda, the challenge is to ensure that the national ambition to end AIDS as a public health threat is matched by practical interventions in the schools and universities where young people spend much of their time.

World.title: Kenya: President Ruto Signs Law Outlawing Traditional Settlements of Sexual Offences
World.content:
Nairobi — President William Ruto has signed into law legislation barring the use of traditional dispute resolution mechanisms to settle sexual offence cases, requiring such cases to be handled through the formal court system.

The new law invalidates agreements reached outside the judicial process, including settlements through traditional practices such as maslaha, amid concerns that informal arrangements allow perpetrators to escape prosecution while victims are denied justice.

The Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act, 2025, sponsored by Garissa County Woman Representative Udgoon Siyad Kuno, also requires sexual offence cases to be heard on a day-to-day basis and concluded within six months from the date a plea is recorded.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The legislation further prohibits the withdrawal of sexual offence complaints through coercion, intimidation or inducement of victims, while barring courts from discontinuing proceedings solely because parties have reached an out-of-court settlement.

The law follows concerns that traditional dispute resolution arrangements have been used to resolve serious criminal offences, including rape and defilement, outside the formal justice system.

During the presentation of the Bill at State House, government officials said the measure was intended to prevent perpetrators from evading accountability through informal settlements.

"Things like maslaha, which are largely practised in part of Kenya, are now outlawed," an official said while explaining the legislation to the President.

He added that the Director of Public Prosecutions would not be able to withdraw sexual offence cases on the basis that parties had reached an agreement through traditional dispute resolution.

The National Council on the Administration of Justice (NCAJ), chaired by the Chief Justice, backed the legislation, arguing that alternative dispute resolution in sexual offence cases could allow offenders to escape justice while exposing victims to further victimization.

Officials said the six-month timeline was intended to address delays in the determination of sexual offence cases, which can prolong the suffering of survivors and undermine access to justice.

The legislation is anchored on the constitutional right to expeditious administration of justice under Article 50 and the provisions governing the administration of justice under Article 159.

The President also assented to the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Bill, 2023, which introduces measures to strengthen public awareness and prevention of sexual offences.

The law requires nationwide public education and awareness campaigns on sexual offences and available legal remedies, while directing the education sector to establish programmes protecting the right to education of survivors, including girls who become pregnant following sexual violence.

Close 

The measures seek to ensure that victims are not excluded from education because of sexual violence or its consequences.

President Ruto said the two laws would promote a better understanding of the provisions and limitations of the law and strengthen the country's response to sexual offences.

World.title: Africa: CAS Verdict Puts CAF Leadership Under Pressure As Experts Demand Accountability
World.content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) decision to reinstate Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations has triggered strong reactions from Nigerian football administrators and stakeholders, with some describing the ruling as a major embarrassment for the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and a defining test of its credibility.

Former chairman of the Gombe State Football Association, Ahmed Shuaibu Gara Gombe, said the verdict had far-reaching implications for both CAF and CAS, warning that the continental body's leadership could face questions over the controversial decision to strip Senegal of the title.

Speaking with LEADERSHIP Sports, Gara Gombe described the ruling as a defining moment for CAS, arguing that its authority, neutrality and credibility as the highest adjudicating body in global sports would depend largely on its ability to enforce its decisions.



He noted that international institutions often faced challenges when their decisions conflicted with the interests of member countries, adding that the Senegal-Morocco dispute would test the willingness of football authorities to respect the jurisdiction of CAS.

"If this stands, that means the authority in global sports affairs as the policeman or the Supreme Court of global sports affairs is then assured and sealed, because this is a serious test case for CAS," he said.

Gara Gombe warned that any failure to enforce the ruling could undermine the court's legitimacy and credibility in international sports administration.

Turning his attention to CAF, he described the development as an embarrassment for the continental governing body, insisting that the decision to overturn the outcome of the final could have serious consequences for its leadership.

He argued that if CAF's decision to award the title to Morocco had been overturned, those responsible should be held accountable, adding that calls for resignation, including at the presidential level, might not be out of place.

Also reacting, former General Secretary of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Ambassador Fanny Amun, criticised the haste with which the decision to reverse Senegal's victory was taken, describing it as a controversial precedent for football administration.

Amun, who spoke with LEADERSHIP Sports, said football administrators must exercise caution when making decisions with far-reaching consequences, particularly after a match has been concluded and a winner declared on the pitch.

He argued that although there might have been lapses during the final, CAF should have handled the matter more carefully rather than take a decision that generated widespread controversy.

"Some decisions you don't take in haste. The reversal of the AFCON victory is controversial forever. This one is not a good reference point," he said.

The former NFF scribe maintained that Senegal had already secured victory on the pitch and celebrated as champions before the subsequent administrative decision to hand the title to Morocco.

He likened the controversy to football moments that become permanent reference points in the history of the game, arguing that administrators should understand the implications of overturning decisions after matches have been concluded.

Amun added that the experience should serve as a lesson to football administrators on the need to avoid hasty decisions, irrespective of their perceived competence or authority.

Meanwhile, chairman of the Advocacy for Nigeria Football Reform Initiative, Prince Harrison Jalla, described CAF's initial decision to award the trophy to Morocco as a shameful development that had embarrassed African football.

Jalla said African football stakeholders and supporters had widely condemned what he described as boardroom politics, insisting that Senegal were the rightful champions based on the outcome of the match.

Close 

He maintained that the CAS ruling had reinforced the principle that decisions taken by referees during football matches should be respected.

"It's a shame and embarrassment to CAF as a continental body, but African football stakeholders and fans outrightly condemned the CAF shameful decision to hand the AFCON trophy to Morocco in their boardroom politics. Senegal are the true champions on the field of play," he said.

On whether Morocco would be required to return the trophy following the CAS verdict, Jalla expressed uncertainty, questioning whether Senegal had returned the trophy to CAF after the initial decision.

The reactions come amid renewed scrutiny of CAF's handling of the dispute, with the CAS ruling restoring Senegal's status as 2025 AFCON champions and raising fresh questions about decision-making and accountability within African football administration.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Open Fire At Peter Obi's Rally in Edo
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi in the midst of the people of Edo State in Benin City

The latest attack comes a few days after gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed six people, including a former state lawmaker, at an NDC rally in the neighbouring Delta State.

The police command in Edo State says it has intensified efforts to apprehend three gunmen who opened fire during a rally by presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Benin on Wednesday.

The command said the assailants, who arrived in a black Toyota Hilux, opened fire on people at the scene after encountering police operatives stationed at the Benin airport exit gate.

Eno Ikoedem, the command's spokesperson, disclosed this in a statement in Benin.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Ms Ikoedem, an assistant superintendent of police, said the gunmen made a U-turn after sighting the police operatives and opened fire before fleeing the scene.

She said one person, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was rushed to hospital, where he was receiving medical attention.

According to the spokesperson, the Commissioner of Police in Edo, Patrick Daaor, visited the scene and later went to the hospital to assess the victim's condition.

She said Mr Daaor also deployed additional personnel to the rally venue and hospital to prevent further attacks.

Ms Ikoedem added that tactical operatives had been mobilised, while strategic locations were alerted to track and apprehend the fleeing suspects.

"The commissioner has directed the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of the State Criminal Investigation Department to conduct a thorough investigation in collaboration with eyewitnesses.

"The command condemns the shooting and warns individuals and groups against actions capable of threatening public safety or disrupting the peace of the state, particularly during the ongoing political activities," she said.

Ms Ikoedem, however, urged residents to remain calm, continue their lawful activities and provide credible information that could assist the investigation.

She assured the public that all necessary measures were being taken to apprehend those responsible for the attack.

The latest attack comes a few days after gunmen suspected to be political thugs killed six people, including a former state lawmaker, at an NDC rally in the neighbouring Delta State.

World.title: Kenya: Ruto Orders Study Into Link Between Drug Economy and National Security
World.content:
Nakuru — President William Ruto has directed the National Defence University-Kenya to undertake a comprehensive study into the relationship between the illicit drug trade and national security.

Ruto wants the institution to establish how drug trafficking networks operate, their financing mechanisms and how they sustain organised crime and substance abuse across the country.

Speaking during the university's fourth graduation ceremony in Lanet, Nakuru County, on Thursday, the President said the findings would inform a coordinated, evidence-based government response to the drug and alcohol abuse menace.

He directed the University to work with the National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse, the National Intelligence Service and the Ministry of Interior in undertaking the research.



"We must understand how these networks operate, how they are financed, how they sustain organised crime and perpetuate substance abuse," Ruto said.

The President identified the drug economy as one of four emerging defence and security challenges that require urgent attention.

The other areas include climate-induced conflicts, security threats facing the urban informal economy, and the implications of artificial intelligence and cyber-security for national sovereignty.

Ruto said the research should generate practical solutions to strengthen the country's capacity to address emerging security threats.

Ruto further directed the National Defence University-Kenya to spearhead research into artificial intelligence and cybersecurity as part of efforts to safeguard national sovereignty and strengthen the country's technological independence.

Ruto has tasked the university's College of Defence Technology, working with relevant stakeholders, with developing a National Defence AI and Cyber Resilience Strategy to protect critical infrastructure and strengthen Kenya's technological capabilities.

Speaking during the institution's fourth graduation ceremony in Lanet, Nakuru County, on Thursday, the President said Kenya must develop its own capacity to create, deploy and regulate emerging technologies in line with national interests.

"We must build our own capacity to develop, deploy and govern emerging technologies in the service of our national interests," he said.

The President further directed the Ministry of Defence, through the National Research Fund, to allocate 100 million shillings to the university to support research into four emerging defence and security challenges.

World.title: Uganda: 10 Dead As Truck Plunges Into River in Zombo
World.content:
At least 10 people have been confirmed dead and four others seriously injured after a truck carrying cassava flour and passengers lost control and plunged into River Nyagak in Zombo District, marking the second fatal accident at the same spot in nine months.

The accident occurred at about noon on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at Nyagak Bridge in Mathawele Village, Oyeyo Parish, Nyapea Sub-county.

The truck, a white Fuso registration number UBF 816R, was travelling from Arua towards Lira when it reportedly suffered brake failure at the bridge.



The driver lost control, causing the vehicle to overturn and plunge into the river with its passengers and cargo.

Police said the truck had left Loro Market in Oyam District on Wednesday, November 25, carrying animals to Arua. On its return journey on Thursday, it passed through Zombo District loaded with bags of cassava flour, assorted items and passengers.

Police responded to the scene, documented the accident and evacuated the four seriously injured survivors, comprising two men and two women, to Nyapea Hospital and other health facilities for treatment.

The bodies of the 10 deceased were taken to Nyapea Hospital mortuary for postmortem examinations and further management.

The deceased have been identified as Fuambe Jennifer, Makwonga Kane, Olumu James, Oryema Valente, Judy Adubango, Jurama, Odongo from Palei, Odongo from Patek, Fosca Akumu and Okwir, the driver.

Divers were still searching for more bodies and possible survivors who could have been trapped underwater, with the truck remaining submerged in the river.

Preliminary investigations point to suspected brake failure as the cause of the accident. Inquiries are ongoing under Zombo District TAR 83/2026.

Second fatal accident at the same spot

The latest accident recalls a similar incident on February 23, 2026, when at least six people died after a commuter taxi, registration number UBJ 956G, plunged into the same river at Nyagak Bridge.

The Toyota Drone taxi was travelling towards Zombo/Alangi from the Hoima, Masindi and Bweyale area when it reportedly lost control while negotiating a sharp curve on the steep, rough approach to the narrow bridge.

Preliminary police investigations, registered under Zombo TAR 25/2026, pointed to suspected brake failure and loss of control.

The six fatalities included eight-year-old Sarah Akello, whose body was recovered on February 25; John Adriko; the conductor, Joshua; Kasamba; an unidentified woman; and a UPDF officer identified as Mungukende, whose body was recovered on February 28.

Close 

Local divers, sand miners, police and rescue teams from Nyapea Hospital helped retrieve victims and rescue injured occupants, several of whom were admitted to Nyapea Hospital. The driver and at least one other person were reported missing during the recovery operation.

West Nile Regional Police spokesperson SSP Josephine Angucia cautioned vehicle owners and drivers against using vehicles that have not been properly serviced.

"As inquiries continue, we urge owners of business motor vehicles and drivers to do proper services on their motor vehicles including repairs to the brake system before being used on the road, to prevent such deadly accidents," Angucia said.

World.title: Chris Van Hollen gains celebrity donor backing as Fonda, De Niro and more support ditching Schumer in letter
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A group of about 35 Hollywood stars and Democratic donors signed a letter Tuesday supporting Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., over Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for Senate Majority Leader.

"The Senate Democratic leader will be chosen behind closed doors, by secret ballot," the letter said, according to The New York Times. "No senator will ever have to tell voters, or us, how they voted. We believe a decision this consequential deserves public accountability."

Jane Fonda, Robert De Niro, Chelsea Handler, Marisa Tomei, Padma Lakshmi and David Mandel are among the signatories of the letter, the Times reported.

SCHUMER'S FORMER ALLY MOUNTS LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE AS DEMOCRATS FACE RARE INTERNAL POWER STRUGGLE

Morris Pearl, a former BlackRock executive, and V, born Eve Ensler, the author of "The Vagina Monologues," also signed the letter, according to the Times. Both had donated to Schumer in the past.

They say they donated or helped to raise about $23 million for Democratic candidates in House and Senate races this election cycle. Van Hollen announced he would challenge Schumer earlier this month.

The donors and celebrities argue that re-electing Schumer was not what the Democratic electorate wanted, according to the Times.

"This is an opportunity. This is a window," Handler said, according to the Times. "We need to, like, get the ball and run with it. And I don’t believe that Chuck Schumer is going to do that."

MARK RUFFALO DOUBLES DOWN ON CALL TO OUST SCHUMER OVER 'ENTRENCHED RELIGIOUS BELIEFS AND LOYALTIES'

Schumer's office did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The group of donors expressed frustration over Schumer's constrained support for progressive candidates in the midterm elections, the Times reported.

"Americans voted for the change necessary to fight the corruption, cruelty and policies of Trump and his Epstein-class cronies," De Niro said in a statement to the Times. "That’s why I’m supporting change in Senate leadership."

De Niro also called Van Hollen a "fierce fighter."

SCHUMER FACES MUTINY FROM NEWLY ELECTED SENATE DEMS AS PARTY PREPARES TO SEIZE POWER

The race for majority leader will be contested for the first time in three decades, and both Schumer and Van Hollen believe they have or can get the 28 votes needed to claim the mantle of Democratic leader and become majority leader.

Neither senator has publicly locked down enough support to eclipse the magic number.

BERNIE SANDERS SAYS HE WON'T BACK SCHUMER AS PUSH FOR NEW LEADERSHIP GAINS STEAM

Van Hollen has the support of Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., Peggy Flanagan, D-Minn., and Troy Jackson, D-Maine, as well as Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., and Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-Ore.

Slotkin announced last week she would be backing Van Hollen.

I'm encouraged that people like Chris Van Hollen got in the race, and because I've been clear that I wasn't supporting Schumer, I will be supporting Chris Van Hollen," Slotkin stated in a video posted to social media.

World.title: MAC admits that officials incorrectly cost Kent State touchdown with blown call against Eastern Michigan
World.content:
Officiating in college football has become a major, major problem.

Earlier this season, the Michigan Wolverines miraculously escaped against Western Michigan thanks to a controversial second being added to the game clock due to incorrect replay review procedures. While the MAC initially accepted the results, they then issued a statement criticizing how the situation was handled.

The Big 12 Conference admitted to several officiating mistakes, most of which benefited the BYU Cougars. During their game against Notre Dame, the referees failed to notice that the Irish should have had one second left to try and pull off a comeback win.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY: NCAA SAYS OFFICIALS BOTCHED REPLAY PROTOCOL IN MICHIGAN'S WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN

"Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," they explained in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."

Then there was the inexplicable handling of the end of the BYU-UCF game, where a facemask penalty flag was picked up, and the Knights were incorrectly assessed a 10-second runoff at the end of regulation. Amazingly, the next week, the Cougars were given a touchdown on a fumble recovery that should not have been allowed thanks to a blown whistle.

In the SEC, the Texas-Missouri game featured several contentious calls that went the Longhorns' way, including the most absurd, awarding Arch Manning and Texas a first down on a fumble, though his arm was clearly moving forward. Analysts were so critical of the officiating in that game that they drew a rebuke from Greg Sankey afterward.

Notre Dame-Miami came down to what looked to be a massive touchdown catch for the Irish, waved off as incomplete. Those are just a few examples. And now we have another one. This time, ironically, involving MAC officials.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

During some recent late-night MACtion, a Kent State appeared to come down with a walk-off touchdown catch to beat Eastern Michigan. After an insane five-minute review process, the officials overturned it, based on, well, not much, and handed the win to the Eagles.

THE ABSOLUTE WORST CALL OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON HAPPENED LAST NIGHT WHILE YOU WERE SLEEPING

On Wednesday, the conference admitted that the officials erred in making the call and that Kent State should have won the game.

In a statement, they acknowledged that there was "insufficient video evidence to overturn the ruling on the field."

"The video evidence did not meet the clear and obvious standard required to overturn the ruling on the field," they added. "The decision to overturn the touchdown was incorrect, and the original ruling should have been upheld. The Mid-American Conference recognizes the significance of this error and regrets its impact on the outcome of the game. Our student-athletes, coaches, institutions and fans deserve the highest standards of officiating. The Conference remains committed to those standards and to maintaining the competitive integrity of our contests."



Kent State head coach Mark Carney told ESPN that he was "heartbroken" by the outcome.

We are extremely proud of the way our young men represent Kent State, our football program, and themselves."

Man, it doesn't get worse than that. Having the outcome of a game be directly affected by the officials making the wrong ruling. You have to feel terrible for Kent State players, fans, and coaches. And frustrating that officiating continues to be such a disaster when there's no excuse for it to be. Gotta be better and let the MACtion dictate the outcome, not the refs.

World.title: ‘Charlie Brown’ voice actor received zero residuals for nearly 50 years due to banned ’70s contract
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Good grief — it turns out the voice of Charlie Brown didn't even make peanuts in residuals.

Todd Barbee was just 10 when his father's connection to producer Lee Mendelson landed him the iconic role of Charlie Brown in 1973's "A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving." Generations grew up watching his performance on network TV, yet Barbee, now 63, revealed to host Joseph Sibilia on his podcast, "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia," that he didn’t receive residual checks until about six years ago.

"Aside from the bountiful residuals I'm sure you've collected for the last 50-plus years, what has been the most rewarding part of being a part of the 'Peanuts' legacy?" Sibilia asked Barbee.

‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS

"Well, let me correct you on one front," Barbee replied. "... We were actually under an old contractual relationship from the '70s that is no longer allowed by Screen Actors Guild and AFTRA, which is American Federation of Television and Radio Artists. The contract was a buyout, and that is not allowed by the unions anymore. I think it was overturned in the '80s."

"So, we did not receive any residuals at all," Barbee noted. "In fact, I didn't receive a single residual until about six years ago."

The initial gig paid "pretty handsomely" at the time "in 1970 dollars." He used his paycheck to help his mother buy the house that she still lives in to this day after his parents divorced. However, he didn't see any residual checks, no matter how massive the special became as a holiday tradition.

WATCH: CHARLIE BROWN VOICE ACTOR TODD BARBEE WENT DECADES WITHOUT ‘PEANUTS’ RESIDUALS

"Peanuts" made its debut on Oct. 2, 1950. The travails of the "little round-headed kid" Charlie Brown and his pals eventually ran in more than 2,600 newspapers, reaching millions of readers in 75 countries.

According to Barbee, everything changed after union renegotiations around streaming rights following Apple TV's acquisition of the "Peanuts" catalog. The streaming service obtained the exclusive rights to the "Peanuts" catalog in 2020, including the widely beloved "A Charlie Brown Christmas."

"... During the big strike, writers' strike and everything that happened about five or six years ago ... Screen Actors Guild renegotiated some of these things," said Barbee. "And they determined Apple TV right now actually has the entire 'Peanuts' catalog. And what Screen Actors did [was say], 'Look, that doesn't have anything to do with these old contracts. That was for broadcast television. You're a streaming service. And as such, you need to pay these people current residuals.'"

"So now, I do make some money every year off all the specials," said Barbee. "It's not giant amounts of money, but you know, it's significant. And I look forward to getting that check every year."

Fox News Digital reached out to SAG-AFTRA, Apple and Peanuts Worldwide for comment.

From 1972 to 1974, Barbee voiced several "Peanuts" characters across five different TV specials. Because producers insisted on authentic kids' voices rather than adults imitating children, every young actor received what Barbee called a "Dear John" letter.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"One of the things that's very interesting about all the characters in 'Peanuts' is you got a 'Dear John' letter the moment your voice changed," he told Sibilia.

"... They were looking for kids whose voices hadn't changed. They really ... had an idea about the intonation and the character of the voice, and it needed to be a kid's voice. And so, there was an audition. They wanted to do a number of specials at the same time, one after the other. They were talking about Thanksgiving and Easter and others."

"I was about 10 then, maybe a little bit more than 10 years old," Barbee reflected. "And the next thing you know, they had me voice for Charlie Brown and they selected me."

After leaving acting behind, Barbee pivoted to graphic, commercial, and site design in the San Francisco Bay Area. In a fitting nod to "Peanuts" creator Charles Schulz, an avid hockey fan who built a famous ice arena in Santa Rosa, Barbee's design work includes the site plan for Fisherman's Wharf's observation wheel and its inaugural seasonal outdoor ice-skating rink.

For decades, Barbee kept his "Peanuts" past under wraps.

"People that were in the know knew about it," said Barbee. "But many of the people that I've known throughout the years, I never talked about it. It was just not a big thing for me. It was just kind of a funny insider thing. And if you really got to know me, you either found out, maybe I dropped it or a friend mentioned it."

Today, Barbee says the greatest reward is knowing his voice still brings holiday cheer into homes across America half a century later.

"... I get this fan mail with frequency still to this day," said Barbee. "And that just always puts a smile on my face because I realize how this character has influenced so many people's lives over the course of, you know, half a century. And there's something very, you know, very special about that. So, it's cool to be involved in that."

World.title: Aaron Rodgers vs Mike McCarthy: Timeline of beloved Super Bowl duo's descent into baffling NFL soap opera
World.content:
Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy made divorce the theme of this Thanksgiving.

Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, skipping team activities and harboring resentment over his 2018 firing in Green Bay, even claiming he had covered for his coach for years. McCarthy denied holding a grudge against Rodgers.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

But long before their reunion in Pittsburgh imploded, the two men shared a complicated 21-year history that included an NFL Draft rejection, a Super Bowl triumph, public confrontations and seemingly heartfelt reconciliations.

April 23, 2005 – The draft

Before Rodgers ever played a snap in the NFL, McCarthy helped deny him a childhood dream.

McCarthy was the San Francisco 49ers' offensive coordinator in 2005 and helped evaluate Rodgers, a Northern California native and lifelong 49ers fan who starred at nearby Cal. But San Francisco selected Utah quarterback Alex Smith with the No. 1 overall pick, leaving Rodgers to endure an infamous, hours-long wait in the NFL Draft green room on national television before Green Bay selected him 24th overall.

Former 49ers head coach Mike Nolan acknowledged McCarthy's influence on the decision in Ian O'Connor's 2024 biography of Rodgers, saying McCarthy was the most knowledgeable member of the group when it came to quarterbacks.

"It was my first head coaching job, and Mike was the guy who was most knowledgeable on quarterbacks of the group, and as a group that's what we decided. … He had a lot to do with picking the other one (Smith), and in the end he got the one (Rodgers) that he didn't pick, and it elevated his career," Nolan said in the book.

McCarthy was quoted in the book giving his side of that story, saying "I was the offensive coordinator, and I did express my opinion. But those selections are made by a group of people, and ultimately a lot of information goes into that. I thought both quarterbacks were very young, talented guys who you could win with."

April-August 2008 – The quarterback decision

Three years after passing on Rodgers in the draft, McCarthy publicly admitted he had misjudged the quarterback.

"Aaron is extremely athletic," McCarthy said. "I've said it before, I did not evaluate him properly in the movement phase at quarterback coming out of college. I did not see the athletic ability that I have been able to witness since we've worked together."

McCarthy had spent the previous two seasons developing Rodgers and was preparing him to take over as the Packers' starting quarterback following Brett Favre's retirement.

But when Favre came out of retirement that summer, Rodgers suddenly found himself facing the possibility of having to compete for the job he had waited three years to inherit.

Rodgers was met with boos from some Packers fans during the team's annual Family Night scrimmage on Aug. 3, the night Favre returned to Green Bay.

"They're booing all of us, probably me mostly. So, yeah, I take it personally," Rodgers told reporters that night.

McCarthy met privately with Favre for several hours the following evening. The meeting ran so long that the Packers canceled a scheduled press conference, and a team spokesman said McCarthy had not spoken to Rodgers that day, according to The Washington Post.

But McCarthy ultimately stood by Rodgers, publicly defending the young quarterback amid the controversy.

"He's done everything right to this point, so why would I put him through any more than he needs to go through?" McCarthy told reporters Aug. 5.

Favre was traded to the New York Jets the following day.

2010-11 – The Super Bowl

Around 2010, Rodgers and McCarthy began meeting privately on Thursday afternoons after practice.

"Some about football, but a lot about life. Lessons, thoughts and dreams," Rodgers recalled in December 2018, shortly after McCarthy was fired.

McCarthy reminisced about those meetings during a 2019 interview with NFL.com, acknowledging how much he missed those conversations. In November 2022, McCarthy revealed how those encounters would typically end.

"And it always ended with a hug and, 'I love ya,'" McCarthy told reporters.

Their partnership reached its pinnacle on Feb. 6, 2011, when the Packers defeated, ironically, the Pittsburgh Steelers 31-25 in Super Bowl XLV.

Rodgers was named Super Bowl MVP the following night. Neither man has won another Super Bowl since.

Jan. 1, 2012 – 'A bright future in coaching'

McCarthy briefly handed his play-calling duties over to Rodgers during the Packers' 2011 regular-season finale against the Detroit Lions.

With Rodgers resting ahead of the playoffs, McCarthy tasked him with calling the offensive plays for backup quarterback Matt Flynn throughout the first half. Flynn went on to set franchise records with 480 passing yards and six touchdown passes in a 45-41 victory.

"He's got a bright future in coaching," McCarthy joked to reporters the following day.

McCarthy expanded Rodgers' play-calling responsibilities in 2012 before scaling them back in 2013, determining he had put too much responsibility on his quarterback.

Sept. 22, 2013 – The sideline incident

The tension between Rodgers and McCarthy spilled onto the sideline on national television during a Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Rodgers had been stopped at the 1-yard line on a third-down scramble in the second quarter, prompting the Packers to settle for a field goal. An animated Rodgers confronted McCarthy on the sideline over his play-calling, and Fox's television cameras captured defensive tackle B.J. Raji extending an arm between the two men as they argued.

The Packers went on to squander a 16-point second-half lead, losing 34-30. Rodgers threw multiple interceptions in a regular-season game for the first time in nearly three years.

McCarthy downplayed the confrontation after the game, even suggesting Rodgers' willingness to express his frustration was something he admired about his quarterback.

"He's competitive, man. That's what I love about him. I don't think it's that big of a deal," McCarthy told reporters.

Rodgers confirmed the argument was over play-calling but refused to disclose the specifics of what was said between them.

Two days later, Rodgers addressed the incident again on his ESPN Milwaukee radio show, insisting the two had resolved their disagreement and emphasizing their history of success and mutual respect.

"There's a lot of competitiveness and passion on both sides, and every now and then that passion collides," Rodgers said.

Jan. 6, 2015 – 'Two alphas going at it'

As Rodgers and McCarthy prepared for another playoff run after a 12-4 regular season, some of Rodgers' teammates revealed how intense the relationship between the two men could get behind the scenes.

Former Packers backup quarterback Seneca Wallace told NFL.com that McCarthy would become frustrated when Rodgers independently called plays without his knowledge, sometimes prompting the coach to blurt out, "What the f---? What is he calling?"

Wallace estimated Rodgers could call 40 of the team's 70 offensive plays in a given game.

"Coach McCarthy always talks about alpha dogs — well, they're like two alphas going at it," Packers linebacker and close friend of Rodgers, A.J. Hawk, told NFL.com.

Rodgers suggested their occasional confrontations had only strengthened their relationship.

"But I think we both know each other well enough that the last thing that either of us want to do is disrespect each other," Rodgers said.

January 2016 – The interviews

Speculation about tension between Rodgers and McCarthy became so widespread among Packers fans that the two agreed to give separate interviews to Green Bay Press-Gazette reporter Pete Dougherty to address their relationship.

The Packers had just finished their worst regular season in total offense since Rodgers became the starting quarterback.

"This is the most frustrated I've ever seen him," McCarthy said of Rodgers.

McCarthy suggested he was uniquely positioned to challenge Rodgers, while the quarterback maintained their disagreements had always been constructive and rooted in mutual respect.

Just two days after the interviews were published, television cameras captured Rodgers and McCarthy sharing playful moments on the sideline during a 35-18 playoff victory over Washington.

McCarthy acknowledged the significance of those images amid the speculation about their relationship.

"I enjoy our relationship. I guess it's good everybody got to see good clips," McCarthy told reporters the following day.

Sept. 24, 2017 – 'Stupid f---ing call!'

Four years after their heated sideline confrontation in Cincinnati, another game against the Bengals produced an awkward moment between Rodgers and McCarthy.

CBS cameras captured Rodgers looking toward the Packers' sideline and appearing to mouth, "Stupid f---ing call!" twice after taking a sack late in the third quarter.

When Rodgers arrived for his individual meeting with McCarthy the following week, the head coach already had footage of the incident pulled up on a screen, according to a November 2018 Sports Illustrated report.

McCarthy had worked with Rodgers early in his career on controlling his body language when frustrated. More than a decade into their partnership, the two reportedly revisited those lessons.

The Packers ultimately won the game 27-24 in overtime.

February 2018 – The QB coach

Alex Van Pelt, who played quarterback at the University of Pittsburgh while McCarthy was a graduate assistant there, had served as Rodgers' quarterbacks coach since 2014.

But McCarthy brought in a new quarterbacks coach after Van Pelt's contract expired following the 2017 season.

Rodgers publicly expressed his displeasure during an appearance on ESPN Radio's "Golic and Wingo" during Super Bowl week.

"Well, my quarterback coach didn't get retained," Rodgers said. "I thought that was an interesting change, really without consulting me."

McCarthy had previously characterized Van Pelt's departure as a mutual decision, as the assistant had aspirations of becoming an offensive coordinator.

However, several sources close to the Packers later told Sports Illustrated they believed McCarthy had come to view Van Pelt as a threat because of his close relationship with Rodgers.

Van Pelt ultimately took another quarterbacks coaching job with the Cincinnati Bengals.

December 2018 – The birthday surprise

Rodgers was celebrating his 35th birthday on Dec. 2, 2018, when he learned McCarthy had been fired.

"I was at home with my folks in town for my birthday. When I found out, I was as shocked as many of you were, I'm sure," Rodgers said.

The Packers had fallen to 4-7-1 after an embarrassing 20-17 home loss to the Arizona Cardinals earlier that day, prompting the franchise to abruptly end McCarthy's tenure after nearly 13 seasons.

Fox Sports' Terry Bradshaw suggested Rodgers was responsible for McCarthy's firing, an assertion Packers president Mark Murphy publicly disputed the following day.

Rodgers also pushed back against speculation about their deteriorating relationship, revealing that he and McCarthy had actually spent more time talking to each other during the 2018 season than in previous years.

But it was a chance encounter outside Lambeau Field in the days after the firing that made the separation particularly surreal for Rodgers.

While driving to work one morning, Rodgers looked across an intersection and spotted McCarthy sitting in his truck. Rodgers recounted the encounter to reporters four years later.

"It was a really weird feeling," Rodgers said, recalling the moment it finally sank in that McCarthy was no longer his head coach.

April 2019 – The report

Four months after their separation, an extensive Bleacher Report investigation exposed alleged dysfunction between Rodgers and McCarthy dating back to the early years of their partnership.

The report alleged McCarthy would miss team meetings to receive massages in his office, while Rodgers had privately questioned his coach's football intelligence and harbored resentment dating back to the 2005 NFL Draft.

McCarthy denied the massage allegations, calling them "utterly absurd."

But perhaps McCarthy's most prominent defender was Rodgers himself.

During an April 8 appearance on ESPN Wisconsin's "Wilde and Tausch," Rodgers characterized the report as a "smear attack," defended McCarthy's character and revealed he regretted publicly criticizing his coach's game plan after the Buffalo game the previous September.

"I love Mike McCarthy. He's a great man, he has a huge heart," Rodgers said.

Rodgers also pointed to his decision to sign a four-year, $134 million contract extension in August 2018 as evidence against the notion that he disliked playing for McCarthy, arguing he had anticipated spending the remainder of his career with him.

Rodgers even made a personal plea to Packers fans in Green Bay, where McCarthy and his family still lived.

"If you see Mike, shake his hand. Tell him thanks for the memories. Tell him thanks for the coaching job that he did," Rodgers said.

Nov. 13, 2022 – Opponents

Four years after their separation, McCarthy returned to Lambeau Field to face Rodgers as opponents for the first time, with McCarthy coaching the Dallas Cowboys.

The two men had been communicating more frequently over the previous year, according to Rodgers, and exchanged compliments publicly in the days leading up to the game.

Television cameras captured Rodgers and McCarthy sharing an embrace during pregame warmups. But Rodgers later revealed the two had arranged a private meeting well before kickoff, away from the cameras.

"We had a really beautiful conversation before the game. Just really thankful for that time," Rodgers told reporters.

Rodgers then led the Packers to a 31-28 overtime victory, overcoming a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit and spoiling McCarthy's return to Green Bay.

After the game, an emotional and visibly frustrated McCarthy was less inclined to discuss the sentimental significance of his homecoming.

"I'm not trying to be rude, (but) I'm humble pied out," McCarthy told reporters.

January-May 2026 – The reunion

Rodgers played a role in bringing McCarthy back to the NFL.

Following Mike Tomlin's resignation in January, Rodgers encouraged Steelers general manager Omar Khan to interview McCarthy, later admitting he had not expected the franchise to seriously consider his former coach.

During a March 4 appearance on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show," Rodgers learned that McAfee had also vouched for McCarthy after working with him as a regular guest on the show throughout the 2025 season. McAfee specifically praised McCarthy's preparation and work ethic.

Rodgers agreed with McAfee's assessment and expressed enthusiasm about McCarthy returning to his hometown to coach the Steelers.

Meanwhile, McCarthy returned to Lambeau Field on March 23 for a tribute to former Packers president Bob Harlan. When asked about potentially coaching Rodgers again, McCarthy said, "Yes, it would be a great story."

Rodgers officially re-signed with Pittsburgh on May 18, committing to playing his final NFL season under McCarthy.

Rodgers revealed two days later that sitting in McCarthy's first morning meeting had transported him back to being a 22-year-old quarterback in Green Bay.

"It's like a pinch-me moment," Rodgers said.

However, Rodgers acknowledged that McCarthy had changed aspects of his offense during their eight years apart and indicated there were certain elements of his coach's play-calling terminology he would push back on.

Nov. 25, 2026 – The implosion

Just six months after describing his reunion with McCarthy as a "pinch-me moment," Rodgers publicly aired grievances against his longtime coach that dated back more than a decade.

The Steelers announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos in favor of Mason Rudolph. Rodgers claimed he learned of the decision during a phone conversation with teammate Pat Freiermuth, not from McCarthy himself.

During an explosive appearance on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show" the following afternoon, Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings, missing walkthroughs and failing to adequately prepare for games.

Rodgers said one of the breaking points came during halftime of Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, when McCarthy mistakenly broke down the team's huddle by saying, "One, two, three, Packers."

But Rodgers' allegations extended well beyond their brief reunion in Pittsburgh. The quarterback claimed similar issues had persisted throughout much of their time together in Green Bay.

"I covered for him for a lot of years and we worked around it," Rodgers said.

Rodgers also alleged McCarthy had privately expressed resentment over his firing in Green Bay eight years earlier, believing Rodgers was responsible for it.

Ultimately, the relationship came to a head over the same issue that had repeatedly generated friction between the two men over the previous 15 years: play-calling.

Rodgers said he told McCarthy the Steelers would be better off with someone else calling offensive plays and asked to be released if the team was unwilling to make that change.

The Steelers officially released Rodgers on Wednesday afternoon.

McCarthy subsequently told reporters the quarterback had issued an ultimatum that was "clearly out of his job description." He acknowledged the embarrassing halftime incident in Philadelphia but denied harboring a grudge against Rodgers over his departure from Green Bay.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

After 21 years, two franchises and a Super Bowl championship together, McCarthy was once again the coach who decided to move forward without Aaron Rodgers.

World.title: UK shields fighter jets, contacts reservists in Cold War-scale push amid Russia threat
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The United Kingdom is bolstering its military readiness amid growing threats from Russia, contacting former service members to assess its reserves as the Royal Air Force reportedly strengthens defenses against potential drone attacks.

Britain's Ministry of Defence has written to former service members to verify their contact information and military skills to ensure the country is prepared for a national emergency or potential conflict, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting confirmed Friday.

The outreach comes as the International Institute for Strategic Studies warned Thursday that suspected Russian-directed sabotage across Europe could trigger a "mass-casualty event."

NATO WARNS PUTIN COULD STRIKE BEFORE EUROPEAN ARMY RESPONDS, POINTS TO US AS MILITARY MODEL

The think tank found that sabotage incidents rose 16% in the year through September 2026, with Germany and Poland accounting for more than half of the cases. Researchers warned that a major attack could spark calls for retaliation and divide European governments.

"I want the country to be alert, not alarmed," Streeting told BBC Radio 4's "Today" program.

"You can't not look at what's going on in Europe and not be concerned about a threat environment which has deteriorated in recent years and is sadly increasing," he said.

Streeting said the government needed updated records of its strategic reserve in case former service members were called upon to respond to a domestic disaster or overseas conflict.

He cited Russian incursions into Polish airspace, suspected Russian-sponsored sabotage across Europe and Iran-linked threats to British military bases.

Last week, a suspected Russian projectile landed in eastern Poland about 60 miles from a British-led military exercise. The incident happened the same day Britain's defense secretary and chief of the air staff visited troops.

INSIDE THE PENTAGON'S DOOMSDAY PLAN TO KEEP AMERICA FIGHTING IF GLOBAL WAR ERUPTS

"And so against that backdrop, against that threat environment, the government and the country has to be ready to face down those risks," Streeting said. "Because the more ready we are, the less likely we are to find ourselves in a conflict, in a war. That is my goal. That is the goal of this government."

The Ministry of Defence said in a news release it was contacting thousands of former military personnel this week as part of a drive to "strengthen the UK’s readiness and deliver on recommendations made in the Strategic Defence Review."

"Service Chiefs are writing to members of the Strategic Reserve, asking them to stay connected and update their details, providing Defence with a better understanding of the skills and experience it could draw upon if needed."

"In the coming months, Strategic Reservists will have the opportunity to volunteer for training and exercises, such as the UK’s participation in NATO’s flagship Steadfast Defender next spring."

The outreach marks the first time since the Cold War that Britain's defense ministry has contacted reservists on such a scale to encourage participation in military exercises, according to The Telegraph.

TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE

Meanwhile, Britain's domestic intelligence agency, MI5, and the defense ministry have reportedly warned British companies supplying military equipment to Ukraine that they could be targeted by Russian saboteurs.

The Royal Air Force is strengthening security at military bases, using hardened aircraft shelters and installing anti-drone netting to protect exposed fighter jets, according to The Times.

The measures follow Iranian threats against military bases in England that prompted tighter security and the relocation of U.S. military aircraft.

Suspected drone incursions over European airfields have also heightened concerns about Russian aggression.

"We take the security of our bases, equipment and personnel very seriously and are always adapting to counter any potential threats," a Ministry of Defence spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING

"This includes investing an additional £470 million to strengthen security at military sites, including better physical protection, surveillance and counter-drone capabilities.

"We have already invested £15 million in drone and counter-drone technology and introduced restricted airspace over 44 critical Defence sites."

The developments come as President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, signaling a shift in tone toward the Russian leader, whom he called a friend last week.

Trump said he made the request during a meeting with Putin in China last week, adding that he believed it could help secure a deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

Trump's comments came a day after he hosted NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte in Florida. The two leaders issued a joint statement urging Russia not to expand its war in Ukraine.

"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Trump said on Truth Social.

World.title: Trump takes on Somali welfare dependency in Thanksgiving message, lays out who should stay in US
World.content:

In a lengthy Thanksgiving message on Truth Social Thursday, President Donald Trump praised a small fraction of the Somali community, saying they should be allowed to remain in the United States, while calling for the immediate removal of those receiving government assistance while unemployed.

The holiday post mixed praise for "AMERICAN PATRIOTS" with criticism of the "Radical Far Left" and Minnesota’s Somali community, which Trump has frequently accused of public assistance fraud in the state.

"I want to thank the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job, and are actually willing to work, without receiving Government Assistance," Trump wrote in the post. "These are wonderful American ‘citizens,’ and should be allowed to stay in our Country, and celebrate Thanksgiving with us. The others should be thrown out, immediately, thereby saving the Great State of Minnesota, which has no chance if they are allowed to stay."

SOMALIS IN MINNESOTA UNLEASH FURY ON TRUMP AFTER FEDS RAID ILHAN OMAR'S DC HOME

Trump’s remarks echo ongoing criticism from some Republicans regarding public benefit usage and fraud cases within the community.

During a House Oversight Committee hearing in January, Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, highlighted data on government support programs, noting that 54% of Somali-headed households in Minnesota receive food stamps.

SNAP FOOD STAMP FRAUD HAS NEFARIOUS TERRORISM LINKS, TOP AGRICULTURE WATCHDOG WARNS CONGRESS

Elsewhere in the post, Trump claimed that "murderers, drug dealers, and criminals" — who he said illegally entered the U.S. from foreign prisons and mental institutions — have largely been deported.

"They are mostly gone now, brought back to their point of origin and, hopefully, living a beautiful and idyllic life, and promising, ideally, never to kill innocent people again," he wrote.

World.title: Kevin Durant dishes on Steelers coach Mike McCarthy’s alleged ice cream snack habits after making NBA history
World.content:
Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Pittsburgh Steelers ended abruptly just one day before Thanksgiving. The team cut ties with the veteran quarterback shortly after benching him and following his disparaging comments about coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday.

Rodgers, who was in his second season with the Steelers, made a series of allegations questioning McCarthy’s focus and work ethic. He claimed the coach had been caught "snoring" during team meetings and recently inadvertently ended a speech with "one, two, three, Packers."

Another allegation came from former Steelers defensive lineman Breiden Fehoko, who claimed that a Steelers player sent him a message reading: "McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand."

Several sports figures have weighed in on Rodgers’ abrupt departure, with NBA star Kevin Durant among the latest to comment.

"Happy Thanksgiving, hiring a ice cream sandwich assistant for the day, great idea Mike," the Houston Rockets forward wrote on X on Thanksgiving morning.

Durant's post surfaced hours after a 3-pointer in the first half of the Rockets game against the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, made him the fifth NBA player to score 33,000 career points. Houston went to defeat Durant's former team 116-104, with Durant ending the game with 20 points.

McCarthy addressed the allegations raised by Rodgers, telling reporters the team's front office was ""very in tune with everything that goes on in football operations as far as my job responsibility."

Rodgers acknowledged that his time with the Steelers was over, saying, "That ship has sailed."

Mason Rudolph is expected to start when the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos kicks off. Rodgers suggested he was unaware he wouldn't be the starter going forward until a teammate alerted him.

Steelers owner and president Art Rooney II responded with a show of support for McCarthy, telling the Post-Gazette that he "expects" McCarthy to "be our coach this season, next season and beyond."

Rodgers expected to enter the waiver wire

The NFL's trade deadline for this season had already passed by the time Rodgers was released, meaning the four-time league MVP will have to go through waivers before another potentially interested team claims him. If Rodgers makes it through waivers unclaimed, he would then be an unrestricted free agent.

Durant addresses confrontation with Dillon Brooks

The Rockets-Suns game also managed to produce some holiday fireworks, as Durant and Dillon Brooks got wrapped up in a heated verbal back-and-forth. While players jawing back and forth isn't a new phenomenon, the exchange between Durant and Brooks raised eyebrows because it happened during a live play.

Durant untucked his Rockets jersey and pushed his forehead up against Brooks' forehead. Referees whistled for double technical fouls, with Brooks leaving the game due to a technical foul he received a few minutes prior to the confrontation with Durant.

Durant address the confrontation after the game, telling reporters, "I mean, I just love basketball. That simple."

World.title: A rising political star in China is the latest victim of Xi’s purge
World.content:
He was on the rise among China’s political elite, hosting tech leaders and senior American officials. But now Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a member of the country’s influential politburo, appears to be the latest senior official brought down by President Xi Jinping’s sweeping purge.

The hammer unexpectedly came down on Chen in the form of a two-line bulletin on the Xinhua news agency Tuesday: He is “suspected of serious violations of Party discipline and law and is currently under disciplinary review and supervisory investigation” — a common euphemism for corruption crackdowns on ruling Communist Party officials under Xi.

Public announcements such as these usually mark the end of a political career in China. Chen has made no public statement.

He is the fourth politburo member to be purged in less than two years, part of a broader crackdown that has swept aside top military leaders as Xi consolidates power. He is set to extend his rule next year, at a party congress that is held once every five years and looms over the preceding months.

But Chen’s abrupt downfall took many close observers of China by surprise, given his profile and career path would usually point to a bright future.

“He was potentially going to the highest level, which would be the standing committee. And I think from a lot of Western observers, people thought he had even better prospects,” Damien Ma, the Singapore-based director of the Carnegie China think tank, told NBC News.

Xi’s pursuit of loyalty

Some analysts have speculated that Xi, increasingly viewed as likely to rule for life, may have been purging a viable replacement. Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London, said however that Chen was “someone who could rise further but not as a successor.”

Chen, a 62-year-old technocrat known as a friend of foreign business and an advocate for AI, was an environmental scientist who studied in London and swiftly rose through the party’s ranks. He served as China’s environmental minister, Beijing’s mayor and the party secretary in Shanghai — a post once held by Xi and widely considered a stepping stone to bigger things.

Just last month, Chen hosted Apple Chairman Tim Cook, welcoming the U.S. tech giant to “make full use of Shanghai’s strengths” and bring more products to the city, a financial and cultural hub that has long served as a connection between China and the international community.

In his last public appearance last week, during a tour of a shipping facility, Chen called for advancing the industry’s digital transformation.

By Wednesday, Chen’s name has been removed from some official websites. A webpage on the Shanghai government site showing that meeting with Cook is now showing a 404 message, or not found.

Chen Jining and Sen. Chuck Schumer in Shanghai in 2023. Aly Song / AFP via Getty

Chen is just the latest senior official in the crosshairs of Xi’s long-running anti-corruption campaign and emphasis on party discipline, which analysts say is as much about loyalty as it is about reform.

“It is a warning to all technocrats, as Chen was a rising star among technocrats and had no apparent failures in a technocratic way. So, message is: adhere to strict party discipline and demonstrate unquestionable loyalty to Xi or else,” Tsang said.

The party’s Central Committee, which has about 200 mostly male leaders, vowed to “ensure more rigorous discipline enforcement, and make full use of discipline as a guide, restraint, guarantee, and incentive” at its closed-door gathering, the fifth plenum, last month.

“What they’ve been building as part of this discipline machine over the last 15 years is to kind of implement their sort of internal operating system of how they deal with, let’s say, bad eggs within the party,” Ma, of Carnegie China, said.

“The top leadership is normalizing this anti-corruption, this self-cleansing,” Ma said. “It is now a normal part of what the party expects, and they’re trying to embed that over time and down to every single level,” he added.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping, right, and Zhang Shengmin, second left, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in March. Kevin Frayer / Getty ]

The Chinese government has not announced any charges against Chen, who was the youngest member of the country’s elite decision-making body. The 24-member Politburo was unveiled in 2022 but is now down to 21 members after the purges. Last month, top general Zhang Shengmin was elevated to the body in a rare addition.

Chen’s undoing comes a year before the party’s top leadership is reshuffled at the 21st Communist Party Congress, when Xi is expected to solidify control even further and cement another five-year term at the helm of the country.

From London to Shanghai

Born in 1964, Chen studied at the prestigious Tsinghua university, long a major pipeline for senior party officials and where he served as president from 2012 to 2015. His name has now been removed from Tsinghua’s online list of former presidents.

After studying at Tsinghua in the 1980s, he moved for a decade to Britain, where he obtained a doctorate from Imperial College London in 1993.

Chen returned to Tsinghua’s environmental science and engineering department in 1998 before being named the university’s president in 2012, according to an official biography.

He’s authored dozens of papers, including on carbon emission reduction and water quality monitoring.

The relatively young Chen would ride around campus on his bike and built a reputation for pushing institutional reforms in his three years at the helm of the university, according to an article in People’s Digest, a magazine affiliated with the People’s Daily, the community party’s official newspaper.

The article, titled “From University President to Cabinet Minister,” was published in 2015, the same year he was picked to lead the Environmental Protection Ministry. In 2017, Chen became mayor of the capital, Beijing, where he oversaw the 2022 Winter Olympics during the Covid pandemic.

World.title: How are you affording the holidays?
World.content:
After a year of high gas prices, inflation ticking back up and a lot of Americans feeling pessimistic about the economy, we want to know how people are affording the annual wave of holiday gifts, travel and entertainment costs.

Retailers are expecting holiday sales to increase slightly more than last year as consumer spending has remained resilient, despite the pressures on household budgets. Even in tough economic years, like coming out of the Great Recession, people tend to prioritize spending on the holidays.

We’d like to hear from you about how you’re approaching holiday spending in this economy. Are you planning on spending more or less? Are there things you’re cutting back on? Or ways you are looking to come up with extra cash?
