Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow.

Also read | Congress takes Samvidhan Raksha marches on Constitution Day, targets BJP over ‘vote chori’

Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”.

Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Congress chief added, “Amit Shah said in Parliament, 'It has become fashionable to invoke Baba Saheb Ambedkar’s name. If you had invoked God’s name so much, you would have attained heaven.’ You people yourself are stealing in the name of Lord Ram; you are not going to get heaven”.

Later, in the day Congress State unit leaders were detained while taking out Constitution Protection March. “We [Congressmen] were taking out the ‘Constitution Protection March’ peacefully and were detained, but our resolve to protect the Constitution became stronger. The place may change; the paths may be blocked, but the struggle to protect the Constitution has not stopped and will not stop,” said Anil Yadav, a senior Congress leader. Lucknow police took Congress leaders to Lucknow’s Eco Garden and freed in the evening.

“The BJP government cannot tolerate even voices raised in support of the Constitution and democracy. The police force’s arrest of Congress leaders and workers who peacefully took to the streets, vowing to defend the Constitution, is deeply shameful. Is it now a crime to demand protection of our Constitution?

“Remember, the repression of power cannot erase the values ​​of the Constitution, nor can it silence the voice of democracy. Congress will continue its struggle until the rights of every citizen, the power of every vote, and the Constitution are respected,” said Dwijendra Tripathi, a senior Congress worker based in Lucknow.

World.title: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material.

Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026

“Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said.

The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”.

Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments

The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”.

The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate.

The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country.

Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout

The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.

“However, upon examining the use to which foreign contributions have been put by the appellant, it is seen that such funds have been utilised and deployed for activities that are perfectly in line with the stated objectives of the appellant, namely, of providing legal-aid and engaging in social welfare activities,” Justice Bhambhani said.

The court, in its 69-page judgment, said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains.

“In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant’s activities amount to an attempt to portray a ‘wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community’. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light,” it said.

World.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died
World.content:
Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday (November 26, 2026). He was 80.

His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Mr. Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, who was ousted in 1964.

Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine.

After 21 years at Time, where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his US State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton.

Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.

Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board.

Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.

His first wife, Brook Shearer, died in 2009, and he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.

World.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
World.content:
Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098.

Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help!

Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer.

With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

World.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
World.content:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.

Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.

E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.

Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

World.title: BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row
World.content:
The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year.

Also read | Infant denied birth certificate in West Bengal after father’s name deleted in SIR

The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA.

On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun.

“This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday.

Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said.

There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir’s selection board’s official X handle ‘suspended’ amid anti-board protests over cheating case
World.content:
The official X handle of the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) was reportedly suspended on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as protests against the recruitment board continued in the wake of the recent case of cheating during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination in Jammu. Meanwhile, activists and aspirants, who were seeking postponement of the Sub-Inspector examination, were allegedly detained in Jammu.

Also read | How J&K recruitment Board’s cheating case put a spotlight on Lok Bhavan, CM office powers? | Explained

Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on Wednesday (November 25), apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online. The JKSSB has not issued any statement on the suspension of its X handle. It had around 129.1K followers.

Meanwhile, several aspirants held protests in Jammu against the Board and demanded postponement of the upcoming Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) examination scheduled for November 29.

Meanwhile, the Board said it put in place fresh measures to check cheating. It has asked the Deputy Commissioners to appoint invigilation staff through a randomisation process, drawing from a pool of staff already identified.

“Exam centres will be allotted to candidates at random, but admit cards will now be available for download only three days before the exam instead of seven,” it said. The magistrates have been tasked to supervise the frisking of candidates and exam staff. All staff deployed at a centre, including service providers, will have to hand in their mobile phones and other gadgets, which will be kept locked in the centre’s control room until the exam ends, it added. The Board also increased jammers at exam centres and pressed CCTV for live monitoring.

Unsatisfied by the Board’s assurances, scores of aspirants held street protests in Jammu. Vinkal Sharma, an activist, said, “We demand postponement of the SI examination till the Board maintains transparency.”

The J&K Students Association (JKSA) alleged that Mr. Sharma and over a dozen other protesters were detained by the police. “The detentions are deeply unfortunate and unjustified. It is an attempt to suppress legitimate democratic dissent. All detained students and aspirants should be released,” said the Association.

Former Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah, in a post on X, said, “Enough of this blame game between the two power centres. They must stop passing responsibility and start acting. Postpone the November 29 JKPSI examination and constitute an independent SIT to probe the alleged JKSSB FAA irregularities. They are demanding justice, transparency and accountability. Their future cannot be held hostage to administrative failures.”

On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. The Board has faced more than three major allegations of scams during recruitment examinations in the past six years.

World.title: Father-son duo drugs man, takes him on  bike 40 km away, pushed him into Rajkot river
World.content:
Eight days after the body of a 27-year-old man was found on the banks of Bhadar river in Rajkot rural, the Junagadh Police on Wednesday arrested a father-son duo for his muder.

According to police, the accused, Nasir Khan Pathan and his son Daud Khan Pathan, allegedly rendered Sameer Hanif Jamal Shaikh unconscious by giving him a spiked lassi, took him on the victim’s two-wheeler to a riverside 40 km away and pushed him into the river. According to police, Shaikh is believed to have died by drowning.

However, the results of the postmortem and toxicology tests are still awaited from the FSL, police said.

World.title: Leopard caught after 4 days of search at Bharuch township
World.content:
For four days, a leopard managed to avoid capture despite leaving behind its pugmarks in Bharuch’s GNFC township. On Thursday, it was finally rescued near the golf course as it was trapped in a cage set up by the forest department.

The seven-year-old male leopard was caught a day after officials found fresh pugmarks near two water sources in the township, Bharuch Range Forest Officer Divya Chaudhari said. “Though it was not seen again at the spot where it was first sighted on Sunday, the tracks indicated that it was still moving through the area. We had found its pugmarks near the water source in the township.”

World.title: Nadda invokes Ambedkar’s ‘Grammar  of Anarchy’, calls Rahul ‘abodh balak’
World.content:
Union Minister J P Nadda on Thursday invoked a warning given by Dr B R Ambedkar in a phrase called ‘Grammar of Anarchy’ and accused the opposition led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of spreading anarchy in the country. “Marching towards parliament and saying ‘Gyanesh Kumar Istifa (resignation) Do’, is it anarchy or not?,” he asked.

Nadda was addressing a public meeting at Tagore Hall in Ahmedabad on the occasion of ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’ organised by the BJP to celebrate the Constitution Day.

In his speech, Nadda alleged that the Opposition Congress is ‘anti-Constitution’ and ‘anti-Ambedkar’ and that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ‘lives it (the Constitution)’. He also alleged that Congress’s history is replete with insults and misuse of the Constitution.

“Ambedkar had given three warnings. In his first warning, he had mentioned Grammar of Anarchy. What is that? If a person takes law in his hands while going beyond constitutional provisions, it will be called the grammar of anarchy. It will be called the definition of anarchism,” Nadda said at the event that was also attended by Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, among others.

“You tell me, if one goes to the Supreme Court with a procession to give an application, is it anarchy or not? You tell me, if one marches towards parliament and says ‘Gyanesh Kumar istifa do’, is it anarchy or not? These people have done this work of spreading anarchy,” Nadda alleged.



In the same context, Nadda also invoked Ambedkar’s another statement related to the Constitution implying that ‘no Constitution is good or bad, but the people who practice it are’. “Till 2014, bad people ran it and after 2014, good people ran it,” he alleged.

Citing numerous instances where the opposition Congress and its allies allegedly disrespected or damaged the Constitution, Nadda alleged that the Congress misused Article 356 on more than 90 occasions to topple elected governments.

“Do you know how many times did the Congress use Article 356 to topple elected governments? More than 90 times. And how many times did Indira Gandhi use it? Fifty times. It has been 12 years since Modi became PM. Except for Manipur, that too for a limited period, till today, we have not toppled a single elected government,” Nadda claimed.



He then cited the example of West Bengal under the leadership of then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. “Mamata had not shielded the Constitution in West Bengal. But we defeated her under the leadership of Narendra Modi on the basis of the (mandate of) people,” he said.

Nadda said that in 2020, he faced a life threatening attack in which three accused have now been arrested. “They were workers of TMC (Trinamool Congress),” he said.

Directly targeting the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi while calling him as ‘abodh balak (immature boy)’, Nadda referred to the imposition of emergency in the country in 1975 and said, “Friends, they are invoking freedom. This ‘abudh balak’ does not know what his grandmother did. This ‘abudh balak’ does not know what his father did.”



Nadda claimed that Indira Gandhi had imprisoned more people during Emergency than Britishers during the Quit India movement and other such freedom struggles.

Nadda said that it was the BJP that has provided respect to Ambedkar and Constitution while adding that it was under Modi that November 26 was declared Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas.

He also said that Ambedkar was the foundation of the principle of Uniform Civil Code. Ambedkar had opposed imposition of Article 370 in Jammu & Kashmir which has been abrogated by the BJP, he said.

Before arriving at Tagore Hall for the event, Nadda had gone to the Saranpur area in Ahmedabad to pay floral tributes to a statue of Ambedkar.

World.title: Gukesh-Sindarov play out 3rd draw in row after opening surprise from world champ
World.content:
Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov will head into the first rest day of the World Chess Championship 2026 after a long fought-out, 60-move draw in game 3 on Thursday. The world champion might be the happier of the two players with the sequence of results having nullified two games with black pieces, that too against a player who has been in red-hot form since winning the FIDE World Cup exactly a year ago in Goa.

At the post-match press conference both players were asked how much pressure the three draws put on them to be the first ones to score a point.

Sindarov, playing in his first World Championship match, shrugged off the question: “It’s a very hard question. I don’t know what to say. Really, I don’t think about this.”

Gukesh, playing in his second match, was more eloquent.



“Usually this means we are playing good chess, the quality is high,” the world champion said. “There’s always pressure in every game of the match. Three draws sounds like a big thing, but in the context of 14 games we are nowhere close to the half-way mark. It’s a long match. We both are playing good chess. We’re strong opponents so it’s not easy to win a game whenever you want to. We try to create chances and make the most out of them, but so far none of us have got really big chances.”

After Berlin and London, the 2026 World Chess Championship match took a detour via Rio de Janeiro, thanks to Gukesh playing the Rio de Janeiro line of the Berlin with black pieces. The second game had ended in a quick, 20-move draw, but right before the first rest day of the tournament, both players strapped in for the long haul. In the second game, Gukesh had seen his surprise of playing the London fizzling out. Thursday’s surprise — playing bishop to e7 — was a more potent surprise, one that forced his opponent to burn time on his clock. It led to Gukesh having more time on the clock for the first time in three games.

“There’s always things happening behind the scenes, some mind games in a world championship match. It’s a long match against the same opponent. There’s always a lot of things happening, lot of thinking, lots of trying to outsmart the other,” said Gukesh when asked about trying to get a psychological edge over his opponent with an opening surprise like Be7.

“This is the psychological part of the game,” explained chess legend Judit Polgar on the Chess.com stream after seeing Gukesh play Be7. “It’s not a very trendy move, this last one. Often it’s quite provocative, you’re asking the player with white pieces to hit the knight on e4,” said British GM David Howell to Polgar.



“This is a bit of a shocker,” gasped Peter Svidler on the FIDE commentary. “It’s extremely rare. I wonder if it’s ever been played in a World Championship match.”

Peter Leko, who was contending for the World Championship title in 2004 against Vladimir Kramnik the last time Switzerland hosted the prizefight, said he had contemplated playing the Rio line with black’s dark-squared bishop on e7 against Vladimir Kramnik in the final game 22 years ago.

“There was a rest day before the final game, and we spent the whole rest day preparing the bishop e7 surprise for Kramnik. But finally at the end of the day, I made the decision that I will not play the Rio de Janeiro line, because there was something that kept on bothering me. I thought it was a completely new thing, so we cannot risk it. I should have played it, but I simply had such incredible respect for Kramnik that I thought that even against bishop e7 he would be armed,” lamented Leko.

Leko had been ahead by a point at that stage and Kramnik had needed to win on demand. The rules at that stage dictated that if the reigning world champion — Kramnik, in this case — managed to stay level on points after 14 games, he would retain the title. After aborting the Be7 ploy, Leko had lost the final game to miss out on becoming world champion. Then, a few months later, he had seen bitterly that another player had played the same idea with black in Wijk aan Zee a few months later and taken a quick draw.



What the opening surprise from Gukesh also did was given him an edge on the clock. By the 10th move, Gukesh had a 20-minute advantage on the clock, for the first time in the three-game-old match. In the first two games, Gukesh had perpetually found himself under clock pressure. Not today. Gukesh blitzed out his first 15 moves, using barely two minutes on his clock.

By the time Sindarov made his 16th move, he had almost an hour less than the world champion. By the end, Sindarov had just over eight minutes for the final 10 moves before getting an added 30 minutes on his clock and getting increments of 30 seconds for each move.

World.title: Weakening democratic values: BJP, Congress target each other
World.content:
The Himachal Pradesh Congress Committee organised a ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’, and the BJP leaders participated in ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas’, to mark Constitution Day in Shimla, Thursday, while accusing each other of undermining and weakening democratic values.

Following a call by the All India Congress Committee (AICC), state Congress president Vinay Kumar led the march, which witnessed the participation of thousands of party workers from across the state. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu didn’t attend the event due to a short illness.

The march began at Chaura Maidan, where Congress leaders paid floral tributes to Dr B R Ambedkar, the architect of the Indian Constitution. It culminated at the Ridge after the party leaders and workers took a pledge to protect the Constitution before Mahatma Gandhi’s statue.

World.title: Beyond the ban: How a Pakistani drama is finding fans in India
World.content:
On Thursday, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) directed Netflix not to stream Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan’s Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, the platform’s first Pakistani original, in India. The decision came after the ministry received several representations against its possible release in India. The series is due to premiere on December 4.

The ministry reiterated its May 8, 2025 advisory, asking streaming platforms to discontinue Pakistani content “in the interest of national security”. Two cine workers’ bodies—the All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE)—had also sought a ban.

While the proposed release of the series has run into opposition, another Pakistani drama continues to find a devoted audience in India. Fans have even come together to organise watch parties for Dar-e-Nijaat—from Delhi to Bengaluru.

Written by Umera Ahmed and directed by Saqib Khan, Dar-e-Nijaat airs on Pakistan’s ARY Digital and streams online via ARY Plus on Fridays and Saturdays at 8:00 pm. Though the broadcaster’s official YouTube channel is blocked in India, the show is available for streaming through some YouTube channels.

‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ being screened at a watch-party in Delhi. (Express Photo) ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ being screened at a watch-party in Delhi. (Express Photo)

The story centres on two women whose lives echo each other across generations. Zaryab, a young woman from a wealthy background, is left shaken after her boyfriend deceives her. She falls into self-doubt. Her paternal grandmother arranges her marriage to Abu Bakar, a calm, considerate man who neither judges her past nor imposes his views. Abu Bakar’s mother, Khushbakht, had endured a similar trauma as a young girl, but chose not to pass that pain on. She became a warm, supportive mother-in-law, a contrast to the toxic ones television usually shows.



But organising watch parties for Dar-e-Nijaat has not always been a smooth affair. Bengaluru lost two events this week after social media objections. Police said organisers had not sought permission in both cases.

The Bloom Society Club, which cancelled its November 28 screening, said, “After careful consideration, we’ve decided not to proceed with hosting or promoting Pakistani television serial screenings as an event.”

A screening for the fans

Abu Sufiyan, the founder of Tales of City, an experiential storytelling platform that often holds heritage walks, was a regular viewer of the show.

After two months of requests from his followers, he planned a watch party for 10-15 people in Delhi. The tickets were priced at Rs 861. But the poster for the screening drew an unexpectedly strong response, with 860 people posting comments. The organisers expanded the guest list to 45.

‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ being screened at a watch-party in Delhi. (Express Photo) ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ being screened at a watch-party in Delhi. (Express Photo)

They also organised quiz games for fans, some of whom dressed up as characters. “We also wanted to make it a meaningful discussion,” Sufiyan says.



The surprise of the night came when director Saqib Khan joined them via Zoom for a 40-minute call to talk about the screenplay, camerawork, and character arc, before settling in to watch Episode 33.

Nishima Snehal, a finance professional from Ghaziabad who also posts styling videos on Instagram, arrived dressed as Abu Bakar, the show’s male protagonist. “I was the only girl dressed as Abu Bakar,” she says. Nishima started watching Pakistani dramas in 2012, with Fawad Khan’s show ‘Zindagi Gulzar Hai’ being among the first she watched.

In Mumbai, the impulse was more personal. Nabila Uruj, an art business owner who recently moved from Bengaluru, did not yet have friends. A keen follower of Ahmed’s work, she got the idea of hosting a watch party after seeing women in the US hosting watch parties for shows like The Summer I Turned Pretty and group outings for movies like Verity. “It was just a random thought,” she says.



Her Instagram post declaring such a watch party “blew up”, drawing a large number of inquiries within two days. A friend found a private space at a café, and about 30 people came one Sunday. For Rs 950, they had unlimited food and drinks, and gift bags to take home. “Since we did the watch party after the episodes were already aired, people were mostly talking to each other, socialising…. They just wanted to be in a space with no responsibility. To just sit and chill,” says Nabila.

The pull of a gentleman

Whatever brought them to the room, the talk kept returning to the character Abu Bakar. What sets him apart, fans say, is how little he does that ought to be remarkable. He cares for Zaryab through her anxiety attacks and does not judge her for her past. “That is what women are drawn to, right? Gentleness,” says Nabila.



Sneha Jha, who works in Gurugram, is a regular viewer of the show. “I like how the show depicts romance, in the old-school progression where it takes time to reach that level of comfort to talk and get to know each other,” she says.

Threat messages

After reels from the Delhi evening went viral, Sufiyan says, hostile comments multiplied. Women were abused in comments and private messages, and he archived the event post to protect them.

Aanchal describes “threats and use of abusive language” in her direct messages on Instagram, some even aimed at parents and partners. She stopped posting about dramas for a few days.

World.title: Reconversion plea pending with temple, Christian family moves Kerala HC, claims ‘heckler’s veto’
World.content:
EIGHT MEMBERS of a Christian family have approached the Kerala High Court seeking directions to the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) and the Kottarakkara Sree Mahaganapathy Temple administration to allow their reconversion ceremony “to return to their ancestral Hindu faith” at the temple.

The petitioners, hailing from Kollam district, have said in their petition that it has been about five months since they applied to the Kottarakkara temple administration to perform their “Mathaparivarthanam” (religious conversion) ceremony, which is among the list of approved vazhipadu (offerings) at the temple, but the applications have remained undecided.

Seeking the court’s intervention, the plea said: “The inaction amounts to a ‘heckler’s veto’ over the petitioners’ freedom of conscience and right to freely profess religion under Article 25, violates their dignity and autonomy under Article 21, is arbitrary under Article 14, and is in breach of the Board’s statutory duty under Sections 15A and 31 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.”

Heckler’s veto refers to a situation where the State or courts restrict a citizen’s fundamental rights because of an anticipated or actual hostile, violent, or disruptive reaction from opponents or crowds.

The petitioners’ counsel, Advocate Sajith Kumar V, told The Indian Express that the matter was listed on Thursday before a Division Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji and has been posted for further hearing on December 4.



The petitioners in their plea said their forefathers were Hindus belonging to the Kurava community. “In the generation of the parents of the 5th petitioner (Samuel), the family embraced Christianity [under the Church of South India], and the petitioners are, as per the existing records, Christians… The petitioners have, over time, developed a sincere and abiding faith in their ancestral religion and have decided to return to the Hindu fold (swadharma). The decision is entirely their own, taken freely, without any coercion, undue influence, allurement or inducement from any quarter.”

The plea said Samuel is a senior citizen suffering from age-related ailments and it is “his earnest wish to return to the faith of his forefathers during his lifetime, so that his last rites may be performed according to Hindu customs. The matter is thus one of deep personal and religious significance to him and to the whole family, and every day of delay causes them anxiety.”



The petitioners pointed out that the “Mathaparivarthanam” offering at the temple is open to any person who seeks it and remits the prescribed fee and does not contemplate any application, permission, enquiry, recommendation or approval, and assigns no role whatsoever to the Temple Advisory Committee, local residents or any other religious body.

The petitioners submitted that “since the administration was not prepared to conduct the vazhipadu on 24.06.2026, each of the petitioners submitted an individual application to the 4th respondent (temple administrator) seeking performance of the conversion ceremony at the temple…”

On June 27, the temple advisory committee “addressed a letter” to the administrator saying “that it had come to know that applications for conversion had been submitted”. It asserted that “conversion is prohibited by laws of the Central and State governments; alleged that conducting the conversion in the temple was a deliberate attempt to use the temple’s name to create news in social, visual and print media; apprehended that the temple would needlessly become a centre of controversy and legal proceedings, harming its reputation and income….”



The administrator in turn submitted a report seeking instructions from the Assistant Devaswom Commissioner, Kottarakkara, saying that “some members of the advisory committee and some neighboring residents had expressed objections; and that if any Christian organisations were later to complain, it might bring disrepute to the department.” The Assistant Devaswom Commissioner, in turn, forwarded it to the TDB Commissioner.

The plea said that when no action was forthcoming, one of the petitioners filed an RTI application to which the public information officer responded that “no reply had been received from the Board on the report”.

The petitioners contended that “the apprehension of complaints from Christian organisations amounts to ‘heckler’s veto’, which the Constitution does not recognise”. “Third parties have no locus standi over the petitioners’ choice of faith. No religious organisation has any legal right to control the faith of persons who choose to leave it. The Supreme Court in Shakti Vahini v. Union of India…held that assertion of choice by adults is an inseparable part of liberty and dignity, and that groups claiming to act on behalf of a community cannot interfere with it. The Board, established to administer Hindu religious institutions, cannot make a Hindu religious ceremony conditional on the consent of organisations of another faith.”



The petitioners said “the ceremony and its record are also legally significant for” them. “The Supreme Court has recognised that a person whose forefathers belonged to a Scheduled Caste and who reconverts to Hinduism may regain membership of that caste, subject to proof of origin, genuine reconversion and acceptance by the community. The Supreme Court… stressed that reconversion must be genuine and must be established by evidence. A public ceremony conducted by the Board itself, under its own notified procedure, is the most reliable evidence of a genuine reconversion. By withholding it, the respondents deprive the petitioners of that evidence.”

World.title: How Dhoni injected yellow in a sea of purple with 33-ball 66 in IPL 2010
World.content:
By Rohit Bose

It had rained before the match in 2010 in which Shane Bond made his debut for KKR against CSK. A portion of the Eden Gardens was pulled down and under construction for the World Cup next year that India co-hosted.

MS Dhoni’s crowning moment had to wait until next year in 2011. By then, he was three years into his first ICC trophy — the inaugural T20 World Cup in 2007 that’s seared in our memories for Yuvraj Singh’s six sixes off Stuart Broad in Durban.

When CSK came out to bat, the spectators, even those wearing KKR jerseys and headgears, were waiting for one man. He walked in at No. 5 almost in the inning’s mid-way with CSK tottering.

Dhoni’s shadow-batted, lumbering up. He wasn’t thinking about just gathering runs, it looked. It was more like an indestructible tank rolling forward.

His batting partner met him a little away from the pitch. Hard to determine, but Dhoni, I reckon, said nothing. He tapped relentlessly on the pitch and adjusted his helmet.

Dhoni bumped his gloves like a boxer before a bout and threw up his hands to ensure his sleeves did not get in the way of his biceps.



After taking his stance, his left shoulder gave that slight jerk like a gun’s recoil.

Long before the yellow wave and his demi-god status in Chennai, the city of Dada — Kolkata — lapped him up with a roar. Sourav Ganguly, leading KKR, was on the field.

In his unbeaten 66 off 33, Dhoni made us stare at the dark sky. We squinted hard to locate the white dot through the floodlights rocketing towards the stands. That year, CSK would go on to clinch their first IPL title.

That year against Kings XI Punjab, a must-win to secure a semifinal spot, Dhoni who had by then exhibited his ability to trim the chase down to a big hit, finished with an unbeaten 54 off 29 chasing 193 in Dharamshala.



The CSK start was rocky with Murli Vijay and Mathew Hayden picked off within the first four overs and the team wobbling at 27. Suresh Raina and S Badrinath fought the storm before Raina was dismissed and Dhoni entered. The equation settled at 45 off 20 balls and Dhoni faced Irfan Pathan with 16 needed in the last over. He snatched victory with a six — that was one of the only two he hit.

What distinguished Dhoni from other hitters was his ability to push into gaps and build his innings through relentless running between wickets. Even before the opposition realised, he was set, knew the pitch and also the cracks in attacks.

Not just the nerve-jangling knockouts or the heart-racing finals, Dhoni’s gem came in a group-stage match at Chinnaswamy against one of the table-bottoms RCB in 2019. Chasing 162, and at a ground known to be a batting-romp, CSK’s top order collapsed as Dale Steyn struck twice. Dhoni joined Ambati Rayadu. But his partners at the other end kept changing.

Umesh Yadav came for the final over with 26 to defend. Then the master-class of sheer hitting began — three sixes, one of it jetted on the roof, and a four with a double on the fourth delivery. And of all things, a slower delivery got Dhoni. He misses. Shardul Thakur is stumped, giving RCB a 1-run victory.



A year before in Chinnaswamy, the ending wasn’t the same and the build-up was emotional. Dhoni was back in yellow after his Pune interlude. He had to reassure his fans — nothing had changed and so when RCB piled 206, and CSK at 74/4, the stage was set for the run-hunter. Dhoni finished with 70 off 34 with eight sixes.

Among the ball-hammerers, Dhoni was the obliterator. Sometimes I felt the speed of his shots should be measured in Mach.

But at Eden Gardens in 2010, Dhoni’s strokes were remodelling a batting culture. More than any of his lionised innings, that night stands out for me as I saw the distinct shift as his approach became precise and controlled. His gift of hitting wasn’t meant to work for long, especially on the international stage. But it did and without any precedent.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Re1 per litre, diesel by Rs2 per litre
World.content:
The government reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of diesel by Rs2 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs313 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs346 per litre on Nov 27 (Friday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively, as of price reductions made to both on Wednesday.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says
World.content:
The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told AFP.

Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting and it is very important”, confirming that defence and foreign ministers from the Gulf kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact in August, with the three Muslim nations pledging to come to each other’s aid in the event of an attack.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated barrages by the Houthis in Yemen, with the group targeting cities, oil facilities and shipping since fighting in Yemen’s civil war intensified in July.

“Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear,” Khawaja said on Wednesday, praising Riyadh’s handling of the conflict with the Houthis, who hold swathes of territory in Yemen, including its capital Sanaa.

He said the pact, which was formed during the expansion of the war in the Middle East following US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, was still at a “nascent stage”.

“Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” he added.

Khawaja declined to comment on how the pact would react to a direct attack by Iran on Saudi Arabia and identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and set a roadmap for further agreement on reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz and for negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

But the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy to resuscitate the ceasefire, led principally by mediators Qatar and Pakistan.

Khawaja said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

World.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.

Bilawal made the remarks while speaking at another “Meet the Press” event, this time at the Multan Press Club. The Bhutto scion is on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, making stops in Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh so far.

Responding to a query about him calling former premier Imran Khan a “political prisoner”, Bilawal explained that he made the “controversial” statement in a polarised political environment, where those terming him a political prisoner could not be convinced otherwise and those declaring him a convict and corrupt could not be convinced otherwise.

Bilawal stressed that in his speech, not the press queries, he made an observation that was not about Imran, but rather about Pakistan’s political history wherein elected premiers often end up going to jail later on or come to power after being imprisoned.

“Whatever opinion you may hold about Khan sahib, even if you think he is not a political prisoner, there is no denying the fact that PTI is a political reality,” the PPP chairman stressed.

He emphasised that even if Imran was considered a “convicted felon or terrorist or whatever”, prisoners in a respectable society were entitled to their rights.

Bilawal said that although the PTI founder “tried to deny my family those rights”, he would not want to continue the cycle of “repeating the same mistakes” in vengeance.

“Khan sahib is a convict, he is in jail, but PTI is a political reality. Until PTI’s trust is restored in this system […] and they are able to play their role in the Parliament, the reset that is being discussed cannot take place in that manner,” he maintained.

The PPP chairman’s latest remarks come amid a growing debate over a “system reset” in the country. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units , arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

In a similar vein, the Bhutto scion on Monday had called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

During Thursday’s address, Bilawal reiterated his call to regain the opposition’s “lost trust” in the system and for the government to undertake confidence-building measures (CBMs) to convince it that institutions such as the Parliament, the Election Commission of Pakistan, the courts, and the accountability system could be trusted again.

Responding to a query, Bilawal reiterated that the disputed reserved seats of the 2024 elections were a “low-hanging fruit” through which the opposition’s trust could be restored and that could serve as a CBM.

The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol.

“Political parties will have to negotiate among themselves, or approach the court, or carry out reforms, so this gets done,” Bilawal suggested, adding that he was “not happy that another party” does not have its electoral symbol today.

“Personally, I believe they (PTI) should have received the reserved seats,” said Bilawal, whose PPP was one of the parties to challenge the Supreme Court ruling that declared PTI eligible for those seats.

However, in a deviation from that, Bilawal today said, “When PTI itself is saying that I am PTI, then we should listen to what they say and acknowledge it. However, that did not happen.”

Referring to the SC Constitutional Bench’s 2025 order that overturned the July 2024 ruling and consequently handed the seats to the coalition parties, Bilawal said, “That order, in my opinion, was also slightly extra.”

He said that even if his stance was that PTI should not get the reserved seats based on the argument that their leaders did not contest as PTI candidates, “how can those seats be given to me or the PML-N or JUI?”

Bilawal added: “According to that very argument, the argument on which you say that PTI cannot get [reserved seats] because they are not PTI, they are SIC, then I am not PTI either, JUI is not PTI, PML-N is not PTI.”

The PPP chairman stressed he was only raising this point because he believed if the opposition’s trust is to be restored, the government will have to think about such “goodwill gestures”.

‘All decisions have to be made in Parliament alone’

At the same time, the PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part and urged the opposition to view its role as a responsibility rather than a choice.

“They should sit in our finance committee in the Parliament. When the government presents the budget, [they should give their] input,” he said, adding that the opposition’s role was essential to tackling unemployment, inflation and poverty.

“But they haven’t been doing it for quite some time. They come for the judiciary, but there is also a committee for the judiciary, they do not sit in that either. They are not present in all committees of the Parliament,” Bilawal pointed out.

He called on the opposition to review if they benefitted from their boycott of such parliamentary initiatives, urging that it take part in the recently proposed electoral reforms committee.

“Until there are free and fair elections, until our country, our nation, all provinces, and all parties have confidence in this electoral system, there will be no trust, and the governments formed or referendums held as a result of that electoral system will lack legitimacy and strength,” Bilawal asserted.

The PPP chairman reiterated his stance that any “reset or reboot of our system” should be democratic and political, with all political stakeholders, including the opposition, made part of the conversation.

“If we want to make the Parliament functional, then all decisions have to be made in the Parliament alone,” he said, adding that decisions taken “outside the Parliament” would leave the system incapable of overcoming challenges.

Regarding a proposed “reset” in the country, Bilawal said even though he had not started the conversation, the discussion was welcomed.

“This country’s system has collapsed. I believe we should take this conversation forward: if the system has collapsed, why is that? How did it happen? Did it happen on its own? Because of political workers? Because of political parties?” he questioned.

“If you do not want to determine the responsibility for it, then don’t. But if you’re sick and I need to get you treated, then first I have to diagnose you to figure out what the illness is.”

He stressed that unless the stakeholders together identified why the system collapsed, there would be difficulties reviving it.

Recalling his Nov 17 remarks, Bilawal said the “system, meaning the 1973 Constitution, did not collapse on its own, it was made to collapse again and again”.

The PPP chairman called for a debate to identify the “diagnosis” with consensus, adding that a “reset should not be decided by a few former and current media anchors, media owners, and a few people belonging to business sectors, as they would not draw attention to people’s real issues”.

At one point, Bilawal remarked that nationalist parties in Sindh label PPP as “wafaaqparast” (pro-Centre) and those in Islamabad “affectionately call us “qoumparast” (nationalist), but his party was “Pakistan-parast and awaamparast”.

‘You can’t have a hard state with thin skin’

The Bhutto scion further said, “This country should have enough courage that we can listen to the truth and tolerate each other’s differences of opinion.”

He termed the reactions to his Nov 17 press conference as “inappropriate”, contending that there were patriotic Pakistanis on both sides of an argument even if they had differing opinions.

Bilawal continued: “If anyone thinks that we can be silenced through such cheap tactics, that is not possible.

“It is now said these days that ‘Pakistan is a hard state’. For Pakistan to be that, the hard state should have thick skin. You can’t have a hard state with thin skin.”

Responding to a question, Bilawal said he not only condemned the recent actions against the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief during his stay in Lahore, but also termed them “incomprehensible”.

“If you will take such revengeful actions even against Maulana Fazlur Rehman, then do you expect them to clap for you or praise you?” he remarked.

The PPP chairman argued that as an opposition member, it was Fazl’s “patriotic duty” to criticise the government. “We should have a thick skin and absorb that criticism,” he said, adding that any suggestion in it that could lead to better decisions should be incorporated.

‘Non-existent press freedom’

During his address, the PPP chairman also highlighted the importance of a free press, adding that he wanted to restore the “power” previously held by press clubs across the country.

“With your voice, your columns, you used to make and topple governments,” the Bhutto scion remarked.

“I don’t want to topple any government, nor do I want to form another one. But I believe your role is to hold up a mirror to those sitting in power,” he added.

Bilawal said he was not denying “mistakes” made by him over time, insisting that his party’s intention was not to weaken the press.

He referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), which was amended in January 2025 despite countrywide protests by journalists’ bodies.

He remarked that regardless of the PPP’s intention, the country had now arrived at a point where press freedom was non-existent.

The PPP chairman noted that if the media was given space only to regurgitate what those in power talked about among themselves, then issues related to economic crises and difficulties faced by the people at the grassroots level would not come to the forefront.

‘27th Amendment a success but judicial system lacks trust’

Bilawal also elaborated on his earlier remarks about the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, insisting that an impression was being given as if he was backing away from them or criticising them.

In his Nov 17 remark, the PPP chairman, who had strongly advocated for the amendments at the time of their passage, had said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor bilateral agreement; it was passed with brute majority”.

He had also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation.

The next day, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution.

“It’s not black and white,” Bilawal said today, stressing that the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment were passed through mutual consensus.

He defended that the 26th Amendment was passed with as much consensus as could be developed and declared the passage of the 27th Amendment with a two-thirds majority a “success”.

“But, at the same time, I believe we cannot ignore the fact today that our opposition does not have confidence in this judicial system,” Bilawal stated, adding that judges and lawyers he interacts with are also “not comfortable” with the current status of the judiciary.

“Does this mean I am saying we should tear it up? No. I am merely asking what steps we can take, how can dialogue be held with all stakeholders, so that we can restore that lost trust?”

The PPP chairman clarified that while an attempt was made to make his “brute majority” remarks on the 27th Amendment controversial, as if he had meant force or used the word “brutal”, he had simply referred to the two-thirds majority that the legislation had.

‘Accountability system used solely for political opponents’

During his address, the PPP chairman also doubled down on his criticism of the country’s accountability system, asserting that its structure was “based on political victimisation”

“Unfortunately, no matter how big the claims the governments came in with, the more emphasis they placed on eradicating corruption, the more corruption there has been,” he remarked.

Bilawal contended that despite strong rhetoric by governments on ending corruption, they failed to do so as the accountability system was “used solely against political opponents”.

The PPP chairman regretted that ongoing discussions in the Parliament, the federal cabinet, seminars, or even television talk shows did not pay attention to the fundamental issues faced by the public.

“People are distressed about managing two square meals. They’re worried whether they should educate their children or arrange medicines for their elders,” he said.

Bilawal noted there was “restlessness and distress” among Pakistan’s youth, who faced unemployment and, even if employed, their salaries were spent on just commuting to and from work.

“If we truly want this system to serve the public, want our country to be capable of facing every problem, whether they are economic hardships or foreign difficulties, then we will have to take steps as soon as possible so we can establish unity, political stability, and restore trust in all institutions,” he stated.

World.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in several parts of Karachi
World.content:
Residents of Karachi faced difficulty in commuting on Thursday due to road blockages and traffic congestion.

Karachi Traffic Police (KTP) said that Superhighway, near Al Asif Square, had been closed due to a protest.

“Both inbound and outbound roads are closed for traffic due to a protest,” police said, without elaborating.

It said that those coming from Hyderabad to Karachi should use Punjab Adda, Total Pump and Faria Chowk as an alternative route.

In updates issued at around 9:30pm, KTP said that the roads on both sides of the Hub River Road remained closed to traffic, as well as the roads on both sides of the Superhighway near Al Asif Square.

“The heavy traffic coming from Hub River Road to Karachi has been lined up, and light traffic is being diverted from Rais Goth towards the inner area,” it said in one Facebook post, adding that the traffic from Karachi towards Hub was also being diverted towards Hamdard University near Northern Bypass.

KTP assured commuters that its personnel were “taking necessary measures” to ensure traffic flow.

In another post, KTP said traffic coming from Shahrah-i-Pakistan towards Al Asif Square was being diverted via Adil Shah Ramp towards Gulshan through Rashid Minhas Road.

It reiterated that the alternative route for those coming from Hyderabad was to use Punjab Adda, Total Pump and Faria Chowk heading towards Mubina Town police station.

Meanwhile, heavy traffic was being diverted to Northern Bypass from near Burraq fuel station, it added.

“Traffic police officers and personnel are present at the site and are taking necessary measures to maintain traffic flow,” the advisory said.

In another post, KTP said both roads linking Ghaghar Phatak near Sassi Toll Plaza at the National Highway have been closed to traffic due to a protest.

Providing the alternative route, it said light traffic coming from Thatta was being diverted from ICI Chowk towards the FFC Factory Area, Steel Mill and Steel Mill Chowrangi.

On the other hand, vehicles heading from Steel Mill to Ghaghar Phatak could proceed towards Thatta via Superhighway after using a link road from the T-junction before Sassi Toll Plaza.

At 8:30pm, the traffic police issued an alert about heavy traffic congestion at Abu Al-Hasan Isfahani Road, Madras Chowk and its surroundings; Maskan Chowrangi towards Superhighway; and Nipa towards Mausamiyat and its surroundings.

It noted that the traffic flow was slow due to the incoming and outgoing roads being shut to vehicles near Al Asif Square, adding that traffic police personnel were present and managing the flow.

Earlier in the day, KTP also said that both incoming and outgoing roads at Lucky Pahari, Hub River Road had been closed to traffic due to a protest.

“Heavy traffic on both roads is backed up. Small vehicles are being diverted through inner areas,” it said.

Around 5pm, traffic police said that Sharea Faisal near Baloch Colony flyover had been closed to traffic due to a protest. Later, it said that the protest had ended and traffic was back to normal.

Meanwhile, traffic police said that personnel were present on Natha Khan Bridge to keep traffic flowing toward the airport, adding that effective measures were being taken to ensure uninterrupted traffic flow.

World.title: AJK govt removes Rawalakot mayor over allegations of 'anti-state activities'
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government on Thursday removed Rawalakot Mayor Abdul Naeem Khan from office and terminated his membership of the municipal corporation over his alleged “involvement in anti-state activities”.

A notification issued by the Local Government and Rural Development Department said the action was taken under Section 23(2) of the Local Government Act, 1990.

According to a separate notification by the AJK Home Department, dated Nov 15, Khan’s name was among those placed on the Fourth Schedule under Section 16 of the AJK Anti-Terrorism Act.

The notification, listing at least 28 names, cited a decision of a cabinet meeting held on June 5, adding that the AJK president approved placing “activists” of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) on the Fourth Schedule.

Khan, who reportedly belongs to the Jammu Kashmir Peoples Party (JKPP), was elected mayor in 2023.

Before his election, he had headed a faction of the Rawalakot traders’ body with JAAC leader Umar Nazir Kashmiri serving as his deputy. After Khan became the mayor, Kashmiri was made the president of the traders’ forum.

The region has witnessed violence-marred protests over the past few months, particularly in June and July, with reports of sporadic unrest in recent weeks. At the root of the tensions was JAAC’s demand to abolish the 12 refugee seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly.

Rawalakot of Poonch district witnessed multiple protests in June and July, with clashes between demonstrators and law enforcement personnel on at least two occasions.

On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the then-PPP-led AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the local ATA.

The federal government had accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest in AJK.

On Wednesday, the AJK Legislative Assembly offered to reopen negotiations with JAAC, subject to the disbandment of armed groups, surrender of those allegedly involved in serious crimes and an unequivocal commitment to pursue demands through constitutional and democratic means.

Registration of 14 private schools in Poonch cancelled

Separately, the AJK Elementary and Secondary Education Department has approved the cancellation of registration of 14 private educational institutions across Poonch district, including Rawalakot, Hajira, Jandali and Thorar.

An order issued by the department on Thursday said the decision had been approved by the chairman of the AJK Private Educational Institutions Regulatory Authority (Peira) under Rule 8(3) of the Private Educational Institutions (Registration, Regulation and Promotion) Rules, 2015.

The action was taken on the basis of reports alleging that the institutions had been involved in activities contrary to the integrity and solidarity of the state, the order said.

Of the 14 institutions, seven are located in Rawalakot and its adjoining areas, three in Hajira, and two each in Thorar and Jandali.

Copies of the order have been forwarded to relevant departmental authorities, the Poonch divisional commissioner, the chairman of the Federal Board, the chairman of the AJK Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Mirpur, and education officials in Poonch division.

Previously, the registration of 10 private schools was cancelled on similar grounds.

World.title: Achakzai's proposal of national govt only solution to political, constitutional crisis: TTAP
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday maintained that forming a national government is the only solution to the country’s ongoing political and constitutional crisis.

Earlier this week, TTAP Chairman and National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai had called for the formation of a national government and comprehensive constitutional and political reforms to steer the country out of the mounting crises.

However, the main opposition party, the PTI, has distanced itself from Achakzai’s proposal. A joint meeting of its parliamentary groups discussed the matter, and a majority of the members opposed the idea, according to one participant.

Speaking to Dawn on Thursday, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai argued that a national government would pave the way for the release of PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, who has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023.

However, Yousafzai made it clear that the proposed arrangement could not be imposed or negotiated behind closed doors.

TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai. — Photo via X/File

He stressed that all political forces, particularly PTI and its founder, must be part of consultations before any decision on the formation of a national government.

However, he warned that excluding any political force would undermine the democratic legitimacy of a possible national government.

“The political uncertainty cannot be overcome through political victimisation or unilateral decisions, but requires serious and meaningful dialogue among all political parties, democratic stakeholders and the establishment,” the TTAP spokesperson stated.

“The proposal for a national government is neither directed against any political party nor intended to provide political advantage to any particular group,” he affirmed, describing it as an effort to restore public confidence in democratic institutions and end political polarisation.

Under the proposed framework, the first priority would be restoration of a democratic environment in which “fundamental rights, constitutional freedoms, freedom of expression and political activities” are protected, Yousafzai said.

He added that such an arrangement would allow all the parties to participate in peaceful political activities without discrimination.

The TTAP spokesperson also called for making the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) independent under a mutually agreed, credible and non-partisan chief election commissioner who enjoyed the confidence of all major political parties.

Yousafzai said the proposed national government should ensure free, fair and transparent general elections across the country in accordance with the Constitution so that the people’s actual mandate was reflected in the composition of the elected government.

He also called for a multi-party conference to be convened before the formation of the proposed government.

The meeting, he said, should focus exclusively on reaching a consensus over the mechanism, framework and necessary arrangements for holding credible elections and establishing a genuinely representative government.

The TTAP spokesperson cautioned that the national government must not become an alternative to the people’s mandate or a permanent political arrangement. Its sole purpose should be to facilitate elections and transfer power to representatives chosen by the electorate, he emphasised.

“Pakistan needs neither an imposed political arrangement nor a government established through political expediency,” he said, adding that the authority to govern must flow exclusively from the free and fair vote of the people.

He said the ultimate objective should be a country governed under one Constitution, an independent electoral system and a government that genuinely represented the will of the people.

World.title: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl among nine party leaders barred from Sargodha district for 30 days
World.content:
LAHORE: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman is among nine party leaders barred from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha district for 30 days, according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner.

The development came as the party was scheduled to hold a rally in Sargodha on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, states that the restriction was imposed under Section 7(1) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, read with the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008, and would remain in force for 30 days from Nov 25.

Besides Maulana Fazlur Rehman, whose district is listed as Dera Ismail Khan, the notification names eight other party leaders: Maulana Naseer Ahmad Abrar, Maulana Amjad Khan and Prof Ghazanfar Aziz, all from Lahore; Maulana Safi Ullah from Bhakkar; Maulana Muhammad Noor Khan Hans from Multan; Maulana Muhammad Zakria Shah from Faisalabad; Maulana Muhammad Yahya Abbasi from Muzaffargarh; and Maulana Jamal Abdul Nasir from Dera Ghazi Khan.

According to the notification, the deputy commissioner reviewed a report submitted by the Sargodha district police officer and expressed concerns that the individuals had a history of delivering provocative and objectionable speeches that could threaten public order.

It described them as “firebrand speakers” whose speeches were allegedly provocative and inflammatory, adding that they were likely to assemble crowds unlawfully and incite public sentiment against the state and its institutions.

The order further stated that their presence could create a law and order situation and pose a potential threat to peace and security.

Meanwhile, several senior JUI-F leaders were detained in Sargodha and served notices for allegedly violating Section 144, police said. Several local JUI-F leaders were also detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Khushab district.

Separately, the JUI-F chief, in a video message, said that despite the road restrictions and blockade, he was leaving for Sargodha.

He demanded that the government immediately remove all restrictions, release detained party leaders and workers and ensure that constitutional rights and civil liberties are protected.

JUI-F Punjab spokesperson, Hafiz Ghazanfar Aziz, said the government was continuing its “high-handed tactics” against the party.

Aziz claimed that a large number of party workers had been stranded on the road and that arrests were being made across Punjab, with cases registered against JUI-F activists.

Fazl should engage in dialogue: Tarar

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that based on Fazl’s statements and attitude in recent days, it “seemed that he wants there to be a confrontation”, adding that the government did not want so.

Asked about the actions against JUI-F on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’, Tarar said, “Traffic jams keep happening in the country; it is no big matter. I would not give too much importance to this issue, it is not an important issue.”

The minister said one should not go to the extent of concocting a “pro-Afghanistan, anti-Pakistan narrative”.

He said the JUI-F chief should engage in negotiations through a “democratic and political process”.

Noting bitterness and increased use of inappropriate remarks, Tarar said one should “retain space [for talks] in politics and not enter a dead end”.

The minister said it was unfitting for a senior politician to create an “anti-Pakistan narrative”, accusing Fazl of “promoting unrest in the country”.

He affirmed that the government had remained engaged with the JUI-F chief and accorded him respect, including on the matter of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“I personally believe that matters should be resolved through mutual understanding and by sitting together and talking,” Tarar emphasised.

Asked about notices issued to Fazl’s family by the accountability watchdog, the information minister maintained that the institutions function independently and there is no “ill intention” behind the actions.

Fazl-govt rift

On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to the deployment of a heavy police contingent.

The development came after tensions persisted between JUI-F and the Centre. Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks .

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.
